Staged, gated pipeline — enforcing completeness and hon-
esty
skills/pomi-take-off/references/pipeline.md · 73 lines

The take-off runs as a sequence of stages, each with a script that can HALT the run. The point
is to remove discretion: a take-off cannot be presented as a deliverable while a file is unread,
a scheduled element is unmeasured, or a quantity is fabricated/assumed. Run the stages in
order; do not skip a failing gate.

Stage 1 — input validation & manifest
python scripts/stage1_validate.py <input_dir> --out manifest.json

Registers every input file, classifies it, and confirms at least one measurable source (drawing
PDF or DXF). Halts (exit 2) if there is nothing to measure. The manifest is the spine of the
no-skipping rule — every measurable file must later be marked processed, and the Stage 3.5
coverage gate fails if any is still unread.

Stage 2 — inventory reconciliation
python scripts/stage2_reconcile.py inventory.json takeoff.json --out reconcile.json

inventory.json is the AUTHORITATIVE element list read from the schedules (every column mark,
every wall, every core). The stage checks that each scheduled element appears in the take-off
and fails (exit 1) on any that is scheduled but unmeasured. This is the check that catches a
whole discipline being skipped (e.g. shear walls present on the wall schedule but absent from
the take-off). Build the inventory from the schedule sheets first — it is the master against
which coverage is judged.

Stage 2b — drawing-by-drawing extraction (strict no-skip)
python scripts/extract_drawings.py <input_dir> --manifest manifest.json --out evidence.json

Walks every drawing one at a time and records a per-drawing extraction (title block, marks,
sizes, reinforcement tokens, vectors). Its rule: no drawing may be skipped. Each is visited
and marked OK / EMPTY / ERROR. If any measurable drawing is EMPTY (e.g. a scan with no
text layer) or ERROR, it halts (exit 1) — you must supply a readable copy or pass --allow-
empty to record it explicitly as a gap (which then must appear in AN.COVERAGE). This is what
makes “every sheet was read” a coded fact, not a claim. It also updates each file’s status in
the manifest, feeding the Stage 3.5 G6 coverage gate.




                                                 86
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                     87



Stage 3 — propose the take-off
The measurement itself: read each element from the drawings/schedules, apply the POMI
rules (see ref-pomi-rules.md — pomi-measurement.md is WITHDRAWN), and assemble the take-off
JSON (see takeoff-format.md). Every quantity is Nr × basis; missing inputs are left blank/flagged,
never filled. Capture markup coordinates for call-outs.

Stage 3.5 — gate check (must pass before building)
python scripts/stage3_5_gate_check.py takeoff.json --manifest manifest.json --reconcile reconcile.json

Five content gates plus coverage; any FAIL exits non-zero: - G1 NULL-QTY — a measured line
with no dimensions and no quantity, on a non-pending item. - G2 DUPLICATE — a repeated
item code. - G3 PERCENT/FACTOR — a quantity derived by bare factor/percentage/ratio
or a per-area rule (dimension cross-products and timesing are fine). - G4 FABRICATION
— a fabrication/assumption token (typical, assumed, approx, TBC, nominal, generic …) in a
priced item. An assumed storey height in a priced concrete item fails here — which is correct:
resolve the input or mark the item pending, do not ship the assumption. - G5 NO-UNIT —
an item with no unit. - G6 COVERAGE — any manifest file unread, or any Stage 2 element
MISSING.
If a value genuinely cannot be evidenced (e.g. no section for storey height), the honest res-
olution is to leave those quantities pending and list the required drawing — not to bake in an
assumption that G4 will (rightly) reject.

Stage 4 — build outputs
python scripts/build_takeoff.py takeoff.json out.xlsx — the workbook (live formulas, linked col-
lection, R34 hyperlinks). python scripts/markup_drawings.py takeoff.json <pdf_dir> <out_dir> — the
call-out marked-up drawings + index.
Build only after Stage 3.5 passes. A run that reaches Stage 4 with gates failing is not a take-off
— it is a draft with known holes, and must be reported as such.


The 25 seats, the pipeline, the boundary matrix and the
review gates
skills/pomi-take-off/references/seats-and-pipeline.md · 311 lines

This plugin runs as an office, not as a single surveyor. Each seat is a declared role with its
own authority, its own inputs and its own output. Role and seat transitions are always
declared explicitly in output. No silent transitions.
Aligns with the house convention used by bom-buildings (control / discipline / conditional seats,
lettered adversarial gates) and consolidates the 13 role prompts proven in the takeoff-v51 rig.
25 seats   =   23 standing   +   2 conditional
 7 stages (0–6)    |   4 adversarial gates (A–D)

     v1.2 — DIRECTOR REMOVED, CHECKERS RENAMED. C5 Director is abolished
     and its escape-hatch authority with it: a halting gate now halts, and C3 is the end
     of the escalation road. C4 Technical Manager becomes the third checking lens, K3.
     The four review seats are K1 Junior Engineer · K2 Senior Engineer · K3 Techni-
     cal Manager · K4 Senior QS, one engine with four disjoint registers — see seats/07-
     K-checker-engine.md. The two shadows are Z1 QA · Z2 Rules. Old names S2, S3, R1,
     R2, R3 are retired.

SECTION 1 — CONTROL SEATS (main thread, sequential) =============================
C1 DOCUMENT CONTROLLER Opens and closes the record. Builds the drawing register
from every title block: number, revision, title, discipline, scale, date, status. Detects revision
conflicts (two revisions of one sheet → latest governs, both logged). Builds the DXF layer map.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                88



Compiles the information deficiency log. At close: certifies the record, not the engineering —
every section has a tab, no padding tabs, collection equals the take-off per item code, totals
are live formulas not pasted values, no #REF! / #VALUE! / #DIV/0!, audit tabs populated, every
drawing hyperlink resolves, file properties carry no tool name. States facts of the record only.
Every decision is a script’s exit code, not a judgement.
C2 PROJECT MANAGER Runs the office. Does not measure or judge content. Drives one
job through the chain from intake to issue. Owns the run folder, the Rev sequence and the
seat deployment list.
C3 LEAD QS / TAKE-OFF MANAGER Detects mode and disciplines; deploys only the seats
present. Enforces the boundary matrix (Section 5). Consolidates seat outputs. Owns the
no-double-count check and the final build.
(C4 Technical Manager has moved to the checking chain as K3. C5 Director is abolished —
see the v1.2 note above. There is no escape hatch. The flags that once admitted a set past
a halting intake gate do not exist; a halting gate halts, and the only way past it is the missing
information. C3 decides contested quantities under J04 and is the end of the escalation road.)

SECTION 2 — EXTRACTION SEATS (the §11 chain, in this skill) ==========================
E1 CAD PROBE ENGINEER Runs the probe over the native set. Records per sheet: block-
insert counts, layer lengths, closed-poly areas, size tokens, plate_layout, plate_serves_floors,
cad_state. Owns condition C1 (R36-CAD). An unreadable plate title is written as null +
a gap — never a ×1 assumption.
E2 SCHEDULE READER Rebuilds every schedule from its own sheet by text-coordinate band-
ing: group by Y, order by X, pair tag ↔ size ↔ QUANTITY by column. Owns condition C2.
Never infers a schedule count from a plan or from scattered text. Reference check: the door
schedule must return D2 = 84.
E3 DESIGN BASIS ENGINEER Codes cited, grade and cover tables, design loads, U-values,
equipment duties with margins (design vs selected), diversity factors, fire strategy, authority
NOCs. Evidence only — records over-design candidates, never acts on them.

One subagent per detected discipline. Each receives its drawing subset, the layer map filtered
to its discipline, its scope boundary extract from Section 5, and — where a priced baseline
exists — no sight of it until its take-off is locked (a seat that reads the bill before measuring
anchors to it). Seats do not communicate. Boundary conflicts are resolved by C3 against
Section 5, never by negotiation.

SECTION 4 — SUPPORT, REVIEW AND BILLING SEATS ==============================
S1 MARKUP SPECIALIST Works under the measurement seat. Colours up the drawings so
the measurement can be traced: area/volume as a semi-transparent fill, linear as a coloured
boundary, one colour per sub-item, legend row carrying quantity and unit. No measurement
authority — marks exactly what the seat measured, where they measured it. If a placement
looks wrong, raises it; does not move it. Owns the DWG Ref → markup link integrity.
K1–K4 THE CHECKING CHAIN — one engine, four disjoint registers, run in series through
C2. Full prompt: seats/07-K-checker-engine.md. None of them edits anything; all of them write
comments the measurer disposes of by APPLY or REFUSE-with-justification, three rounds
maximum, escalating to C3.
The registers are disjoint on purpose. Four reviewers given the same take-off and no instruc-
tion all do the same thing — read down the items and re-add the dimensions — so the office
records four approvals of a document that was checked once. A comment raised outside your
own register is OUT OF LENS and is routed to the level that owns it, never dropped.
K1 JUNIOR ENGINEER — source fidelity. Does each number exist on the drawing it says
it came from? The only level that goes item by item to the source, so the one unforgivable
failure is reading the take-off instead of the drawing.
K2 SENIOR ENGINEER — the set. Is the SET right? Relationships between items, and the
things that are ABSENT — which no item-by-item pass can see, because an item never written
cannot be checked. Mass balance, coincident counts, companions, boundary, coverage.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              90



K3 TECHNICAL MANAGER — specification and method. Is this the right rule, applied to
the right thing, described well enough to price? The only level with authority to say the POMI
clause is wrong. Owns deemed-included / enumerate-separately, mandatory statements, and
whether a tenderer could price the description without asking a question.
K4 SENIOR QS — exposure, adversarial. The take-off leaves the office under this name.
May not trust the three levels below. Assume good faith and poor evidence: the measurer
is not lying, the measurer is guessing where the drawing is silent — and a guess that has
passed three checks looks exactly like a measurement, because internal consistency is what a
good guess has. Ranks by commercial weight, names the single-source quantities, and states
in one paragraph where the bill is weakest. Silent approval is not permitted at any level.
Verdicts: APPROVED / APPROVED WITH CORRECTIONS / REJECTED.
Z2 RULES COMPLIANCE SHADOW The rulebook is law — POMI measurement rules, the
locked house template, the conditions C1–C5. Changes nothing; a breach returns the work to
the measuring seat.
Z1 QA SHADOW The outsider who opens the deliverable the way the client will. Changes
nothing; passes or fails with evidence.
B1 BILL COMPILER Builds the POMI section pages, item lettering (skipping I), To Collection
/ COLLECTION / Carried to Summary plumbing, and the formula link from each bill Qty to the
measurement total. Applies the round-up rule: measured at two decimals, billed to the next
whole unit.
B2 RATE & COMMERCIAL OFFICER Rate assignment by item class with the min/max enve-
lope check; market or baseline rates govern over the library; provisional-sum allowance policy;
dayworks. Owns condition C4 — an unstated rating takes the lower-cost classification plus
a TQ.

A gate failure returns the work to the named seat. No seat clears its own gate, and no gate
is cleared by the seat that produced the work under review.
There is no escape hatch. No seat may admit a set past a halting gate — the authority that
once did was the Director’s and the Director is abolished. A gate that halts, halts, and the
only thing that clears it is the missing information. C3 decides contested quantities under J04
and is the end of the escalation road, but C3 cannot waive a gate.

SECTION 8 — SCALING =================================================
EVERY SEAT IS DEPLOYED ON EVERY JOB — determinism §4.12, agreed v1.2. The scaling
table below is withdrawn.
A seat whose evidence contains nothing returns COMPLETE with every element at status
ABSENT, quantity zero, and its detection path recorded. It does not return empty and it is not
skipped.
This is deliberately the expensive option. Deploying only the disciplines the evidence appears
to contain makes detection a single point of failure for coverage: a whole trade can be missing
from a bill because nobody was asked to look, and nothing in the output says so. An ABSENT
return at zero is a POSITIVE STATEMENT that a seat looked and found nothing, and every
checker downstream can see it.
What varies between projects is therefore not the seat count — it is how many seats return
ABSENT. Consequence: J01 discipline deployment is withdrawn from the judgement
register.

DETERMINISM SPECIFICATION
skills/pomi-take-off/references/determinism.md · 890 lines


Binding on every seat. Version 1.0.
Read before any other reference, on every run, by every seat.
This file exists because a prompt that is merely rigorous produces a different answer every
time it is run. Rigour says what is acceptable. Determinism says what is produced.
THE SAME INPUTS PRODUCE THE SAME OUTPUT, BYTE FOR BYTE, EXCEPT FOR run_id
AND timestamps.
A run that cannot meet that is not a measurement process. It is an opinion with a schema.
================================================================
SECTION 1 — THE DETERMINISM CLASSES ====================================
Every field emitted by every seat carries one of three classes. The class is declared in the
seat’s output schema, not decided at runtime.
D DETERMINISTIC — produced by a script from stated inputs by a stated algorithm. The
model does not compute it, does not adjust it, and does not override it. Where a script exists
for a value, using the model instead is a BLOCK condition.
T TRANSCRIBED — read verbatim off a document by the model and typed into a field without
alteration. Not rounded, not normalised, not tidied, not unit-converted. The literal string, plus
a separately recorded normalised form where one is needed.
J JUDGED — the model chose. Every J field is enumerated in judgements[] with the options
considered, the rule applied, and the reason. A seat is measured by how few of these it emits.
RULES
1.1 A value that a script can produce is class D. Producing it by model is a BLOCK. 1.2 A value
printed on a document is class T. Deriving it instead of reading it is a BLOCK. 1.3 Class J is
permitted only where §3 explicitly names it as a judgement point. A J field at any other location
is a BLOCK. 1.4 Every J field appears in judgements[]. An unlogged judgement is a BLOCK. 1.5
Every seat reports its determinism ratio: D_count, T_count, J_count, and J as a percentage of
the whole.

SECTION 4 — DECISION TABLES ===========================================
Where a decision was prose, it is now a table. Tests run TOP TO BOTTOM and the FIRST
MATCH WINS. There is no “best fit” and no weighing.

1 contains “SCHEDULE” -> SCHEDULE 2 contains “LEGEND” or “SYMBOL” -> LEGEND 3

none of the above -> UNTYPED
Rule 5 sits BELOW rules 1–4 deliberately: “STAIRCASE DETAIL SCHEDULE” is a schedule.
Rule 9 sits last because “DETAIL PLAN” is a detail.

                             4.11 TRADE TO BILL SECTION [class D]


AGREED SPLIT: the building is MEASURED BY TRADE and BILLED BY POMI SECTION. The
two are different cuts and this table is the only place they meet.
Measurement seats are the trades. The boundary matrix (seats-and-pipeline §5) says which
trade owns an element. This table says which bill section that trade’s items land in.

       SEAT BILL SECTIONS IT WRITES INTO
       M1 Enabling & Substructure B Site Work
       M2 Concrete & Structure C Concrete Work · E Metalwork (structural)
       M3 Masonry, Finishes & Openings D Masonry · F Woodwork ·
       G Thermal and Moisture Protection ·
       H Doors and Windows · J Finishes ·
       K Accessories · M Furnishings
       M4 Mechanical HVAC Q Mechanical Engineering Installations
       M5 Public Health & Fire Q Mechanical Engineering Installations
       M6 Electrical & ELV R Electrical Engineering Installations
       M7 External Works & Landscape B Site Work (external to the building line)
       M8 Conveying & Preliminaries P Conveying Systems · A General Requirements
       X1 Specialist Systems L Equipment · N Special Construction
       X2 Temporary Works A General Requirements


THE SHARED-SECTION RULE. Four sections receive work from more than one seat:
A from M8 and X2 B from M1 and M7 Q from M4 and M5 R from M6 alone, but ELV and power
are separate item groups within it
Inside a shared section, the ITEM GROUP is owned by exactly ONE seat. Two seats never
write into the same item group, and C3 assembles the section from the contributing take-offs
in the order of this table — M1 before M7 in B, M4 before M5 in Q, M8 before X2 in A. The
order is fixed so that the same project measured twice produces the same page breaks and
the same item letters.
A seat that finds work belonging to a section it does not write into has found a boundary breach,
not a new section. CROSS_REF at zero, name the owner.

                                   4.13 RATE SOURCE [class D]


For each item the rate is taken from the FIRST available source in this order. The seat does
not pick the most favourable, the most conservative, or the most convenient — the seat that
picks its source picks its answer.
1 A CONTRACT RATE that applies. Contractual, not commercial. Whether it is a good rate is
irrelevant to whether it binds.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                98



2 A PROJECT-SPECIFIC QUOTATION, in date, for this scope. Its date is recorded with it.
3 MARKET DATA for this jurisdiction, not older than 12 months. Tender returns and published
indices. The jurisdiction is recorded — a Dubai rate is not an Abu Dhabi rate and neither is a
Riyadh rate.
4 THE HOUSE RATE LIBRARY. Last, always, and never used to avoid a blank.
5 NONE AVAILABLE -> BLANK RATE + a technical query.
A blank rate is a legitimate output. It says “nobody has priced this, and here is what we need
in order to”. A library rate says “this is what it costs”. Where nobody knows, only one of those
is true, and the difference is what a client relies on.
Rates from different tiers are NEVER averaged, and rates from different dates are never av-
eraged at all. Two readings taken on different bases are not two readings of one number.

       4.11a THE SECTION LETTERS [class D — and the correction to house practice]


AGREED: THE BILL FOLLOWS POMI’S OWN LETTERS. POMI runs A to R and skips I.
A General Requirements J Finishes B Site Work K Accessories C Concrete Work L Equipment
D Masonry M Furnishings E Metalwork N Special Construction F Woodwork P Conveying
Systems G Thermal and Moisture Protection Q Mechanical Engineering Installations H Doors
and Windows R Electrical Engineering Installations
THERE IS NO SECTION S. Communications, data, CCTV, fire alarm, BMS and access con-
trol are ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING INSTALLATIONS and are billed in R, as separate item
groups within it.
CROSSWALK — house lettering used on bills issued before this correction. Every revision
comparison against an earlier issue must pass through this table, and C1 records which set
the earlier bill used.

            HOUSE (as issued) POMI (governs from v1.2)
            K Specialties → K Accessories same letter, correct title
            N Furnishings → M Furnishings LETTER CHANGES
            — (not used) → L Equipment newly available
            — (not used) → N Special Construction newly available
            S Communications & ELV → R Electrical SECTION DISSOLVED into R
            F Wood & Plastic → F Woodwork same letter, correct title
            J1 ID Finishes → J Finishes not a letter. An ID package
            is an item group inside J,
            not a section of its own.


The two that bite: an item billed at N on an earlier issue is at M now, and an S-section bill has
no counterpart — its content is inside R. A gap analysis run across the change without this
crosswalk will report the whole of S as omitted and the whole of M as new, and both readings
are false.

                    4.12 DEPLOYMENT [class D — replaces judgement J01]


AGREED: EVERY SEAT IS INSTANTIATED ON EVERY PROJECT.
A seat whose evidence contains nothing returns COMPLETE with every element at status
ABSENT, quantity zero, and its detection path recorded. It does not return empty and it is not
skipped.
This is deliberately the expensive option. The cheap one — deploy only the disciplines the
evidence appears to contain — makes C3’s detection a single point of failure for coverage: an
entire trade can be missing from a bill because nobody was asked to look for it, and nothing in
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              99



the output says so. An ABSENT return at zero is a POSITIVE STATEMENT that a seat looked
and found nothing, and it is visible to every checker downstream.
Consequence for J01: discipline deployment is no longer a judgement. J01 is WITHDRAWN
from the register. The deployed set is fixed, and what varies between projects is how many
seats return ABSENT.

================================================================
SECTION 6 — CANONICAL ORDERING ========================================
Every output array is sorted before emission, so that two runs diff cleanly and a reviewer sees
changes rather than reshuffling.
inventory[] path ascending drawing_register[] drawing_number_key, then revision descending
sheet_map[] doc_id ascending schedule_index[] doc_id, then schedule_title schedules.rows[]
schedule_title, then tag counts[] subject, then block_name spaces.rooms[] doc_id, then
room name consolidated_register[] pomi_section, then element_code, then line_id com-
ments_register[] station, round, comment_id gaps[] / not_found[] class, then affected subject
judgements[] judgement_id, then subject every other array its first field, ascending, string
comparison
Ties break on the next field in the sort key, then on the record’s own id. Where a record has
no id, it is assigned one from a stable hash of its content — never from insertion order, never
from a counter.
================================================================
SECTION 7 — TIE-BREAK RULES ===========================================
Where two options remain equally valid after every stated test:
7.1 Two documents equally authoritative -> lowest doc_id 7.2 Two revisions, both apparently
current -> BLOCK, never pick 7.3 Two schedule columns both matching a heading pattern ->
leftmost 7.4 Two tags equidistant from a value within K02 -> leftmost 7.5 Two sweep regions
overlapping -> the smaller region owns the shared blocks 7.6 Two seats both entitled by the
matrix -> BLOCK, matrix is defective 7.7 Two variance buckets both matching -> impossible:
4.5 is ordered and first match wins
A tie-break is always logged. A silent tie-break is a BLOCK.

Where a script exists for a computation, the model does not perform it, does not check it by

A number in an output that a script should have produced is a BLOCK, whether or not it is

================================================================
SECTION 9 — IDEMPOTENCY =============================================
9.1 Re-running any seat on identical inputs produces byte-identical output, except run_id and
timestamps. 9.2 Every seat emits input_digest: a stable hash over its ordered inputs. Two runs
with the same digest and different outputs is a defect in the seat, reported as such. 9.3 No
seat consults the current date, a random source, or any state outside its declared inputs. 9.4
No seat’s output depends on the order files happened to be listed in. Ordering comes from
§6, never from the filesystem. 9.5 Where a seat is re-run after an upstream change, it re-runs
WHOLE. There is no partial re-run and no incremental patch, because a patch depends on
what was there before and is therefore not idempotent.
================================================================
SECTION 11 — 100% DETERMINISTIC EXTRACTION ===============================
Extraction is not interpretation. A drawing file is a data structure, and reading a data structure
requires no model.
THE MODEL IS REMOVED FROM THE READ PATH ENTIRELY. EVERY EXTRACTED VALUE
IS CLASS D. E1 EMITS ZERO CLASS-J FIELDS.
This applies to PDF exactly as it applies to DXF. A PDF is not one thing; it is three separable
things, and only one of them was ever difficult.
TEXT characters with coordinates GEOMETRY vector paths with coordinates RASTER pixels

             11.1 SOURCE TIERS [class D — determined by probe, not by choice]


Every document resolves to exactly one tier. The test is mechanical and runs top to bottom,
first match wins.
T1 DXF / DWG entities carry text and geometry T2 PDF, text layer present extractable words
with coordinates (page.extract_words() returns ≥ K25 words) T3 PDF, text outlined, vector
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                101



geometry no words; get_drawings() returns present paths T4 PDF, raster only no words, no
vector paths
Record source_tier on every document. It governs which read path applies and what is and is
not available from that sheet.

                     11.2 GEOMETRY EXTRACTION [T1, T2, T3 — class D]


Vector geometry is exact, and it exists in a vector PDF exactly as it exists in a DXF. It is never
obtained by looking at a picture.
T1 ezdxf: LINE, LWPOLYLINE, POLYLINE, ARC, CIRCLE, HATCH boundary, INSERT position
and name. Lengths and areas computed by the script. T2, T3 pymupdf page.get_drawings():
every path item as (“l”, p1, p2) line, (“c”, …) bezier, (“re”, rect), with stroke and fill colour,
width and closure. Coordinates are exact PDF points. Lengths and areas computed by the
script. T4 NO VECTOR GEOMETRY EXISTS. Any length or area from a T4 sheet is obtainable
only by scale calibration at §11.6, and every such value carries geometry_source: SCALED and
confidence MED at best.
Coordinates are rounded to K40 before comparison, so that two exports of the same drawing
produce identical keys.
REGION ASSEMBLY. A CAD-exported PDF does not contain rooms. It contains a tessellation: a
hatched area arrives as thousands of small filled triangles, and a wall line arrives as hundreds
of separate two-point segments. The region is IN the source; it is simply shredded. Two
mechanical operations put it back, and neither invents anything:
FILLED REGIONS group filled paths by fill colour, union each group. The boundary of the
union is the boundary that was drawn. Regions below K49 are glyph fills — outlined text —
and are dropped. LINEAR RUNS build a graph on K40-rounded endpoints and walk maximal
chains through degree-2 nodes. A chain is one drawn run.
Both are deterministic: same paths in, same regions out. Neither closes a gap, smooths a
corner or snaps at any tolerance other than K40. A boundary that is open in the source stays
open, and an open boundary is not an area.

                          11.3 RASTERISATION [T3, T4 only — class D]


Where text must be recovered from pixels, the pixels are produced by a fixed pipeline. Every
parameter is a constant. No parameter is chosen per document.
1 Render the page at K26 DPI, K27 colour mode, using the pinned renderer. 2 Binarise by
K28. Global Otsu, computed over the whole page. Local or adaptive thresholding is BANNED:
its result depends on window placement, which depends on page size, which makes two crops
of one page disagree. 3 Deskew is K29 — DISABLED. Deskew resamples, resampling is
implementation-dependent, and a UAE consultant’s issued PDF is not skewed. A genuinely
skewed scan is recorded as such and its sheet is flagged, not silently straightened. 4 No
sharpening, denoising, contrast stretch or morphological operation. Each is a free parameter
and every free parameter is a source of drift.
The rendered bitmap is hashed. The hash is recorded against the document, so a re-render
that differs is detected rather than absorbed.

                                 11.4 OCR [T3, T4 only — class D]


OCR is deterministic when it is pinned. LSTM inference is not sampled; the same bitmap and
the same parameters give the same characters every time. Non-determinism enters through
unpinned versions, variable parameters and adaptive preprocessing, and §11.3 has removed
the last of those.
0 TILING. The page is OCR’d in a FIXED GRID of K50 tiles overlapping by K51, and every
word’s coordinates are mapped back to page space.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                102



 This is not an optimisation. Tesseract's layout analysis returns NOTHING
 on a large sparse drawing — two dimension strings on a 3000 x 2200 page
 yield zero words, and the same strings read perfectly from a crop. A
 construction drawing is exactly that shape: a very large page carrying
 scattered text. Without tiling, §11.4 reads nothing at all on the sheets
 it exists for.


 The grid is fixed, so it is deterministic. K51 is large enough that any
 word falls whole inside at least one tile. A word found in two tiles is
 ONE word: same text and centres within K51/2 are the same reading, and the
 duplicate with the lower confidence is dropped — ties broken by bounding
 box then text, so the survivor never depends on tile order.

1 Engine mode K32. Page segmentation K30 for a sheet classified SCHEDULE, K31 for every
other class. 2 Output in TSV: word, bounding box, confidence. The coordinates are what
make the schedule banding algorithm applicable to OCR output exactly as it is applied to
a text layer — one algorithm, four tiers. 3 CHARACTER WHITELIST BY FIELD CLASS. A
quantity column is read with K34, a dimension with K35, a tag with K36. This is the single
largest accuracy gain available and it is free: a whitelist cannot turn a 3 into a B, because B is
not in the alphabet. 4 CONFIDENCE FLOOR K33. A word below it is ILLEGIBLE. It is never
the best guess, never the likelier reading, never inferred from context. 5 No language model,
no dictionary correction, no autocorrect. A dictionary that turns “D2” into “D3” because D3
is commoner has destroyed the read.

                   11.5 DUAL-ENGINE UNANIMITY [numerics only — class D]


Determinism is not accuracy. A pinned pipeline that misreads a character misreads it identi-
cally forever. That is better than a moving error, because it is findable — but it is still wrong.
For every NUMERIC field recovered by OCR, K37 requires two independent pinned engines
to agree character for character.
agree -> value accepted, class D, confidence MED disagree -> ILLEGIBLE, both readings
recorded, gap raised
Two deterministic engines combined are deterministic. The combination raises accuracy with-
out surrendering reproducibility, and it converts the residual error class from “silently wrong”
to “visibly unread”.

                         11.6 SCALE CALIBRATION [T4 only — class D]


A T4 sheet has no vector geometry, so any length must come from the raster. That is permitted
only under calibration, and never from a scale bar.
1 Locate K38 printed dimension strings whose endpoints are identifiable in the raster — two,
independently, on different axes where possible. 2 For each, compute px-per-mm from the
printed value and the measured pixel span. 3 The two must agree within K39. Outside it,
the sheet is SCALE_UNVERIFIED and no length is taken from it. 4 Record both calibration
dimensions, both ratios and the variance.
A scale bar is not a calibration. It rescales with the sheet, so it agrees with a rescaled drawing
perfectly and tells you nothing.

                  11.7 ELEMENT PRESENCE [replaces judgement J07 — class D]


J07 is withdrawn from the §3 register. Presence is now a decision table. Tests run top to
bottom, first match wins.
1 a schedule row exists for the element -> PRESENT 2 a sheet in the register is named for
it -> PRESENT 3 a legend entry defines its tag, AND that tag occurs -> PRESENT on a sheet
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              103



4 a block insert whose name maps to it occurs -> PRESENT 5 the specification names it as
required work -> PRESENT 6 none of the above -> ABSENT
ABSENT is emitted with quantity zero and its detection path recorded. It is never omitted,
and it is never NOT_FOUND — absence of evidence is ABSENT, absence of a readable value
is NOT_FOUND, and they are different findings.

                             11.8 TOOLCHAIN AND INPUT PINNING


Determinism across a single run is worthless without determinism across time. A library
upgrade that changes a rounding behaviour silently changes every quantity, and nothing in
the output would show it.
Every run records toolchain[]: { “tool”: “”, “version”: “”, “hash”: “” } pinned, at minimum:
ezdxf · pymupdf · pdfplumber · the OCR engines and their trained data · the renderer · openpyxl
· the recalculation engine.
Every document records content_hash (sha256 over its bytes).
Every seat records input_digest: sha256 over its ordered inputs and the toolchain block.
Same input_digest and different output is a defect in the seat, reported as one. Same in-
put_digest across two dates and different output means the toolchain moved, and the toolchain
block will show which tool.

                                      11.8a WHAT §11 COSTS


A T2 sheet — vector, with a text layer — extracts in seconds. Geometry is read straight out of
the file and no pixel is touched.
A T4 sheet does not. At K26 the page is rendered to roughly 14,000 x 10,000 pixels, tiled
at K50, and every tile is read by two independent engines. That is minutes per sheet, not
seconds, and it does not parallelise past the cores available.
This is not a defect to optimise away. It is the PRICE OF A RASTER ISSUE, and it is worth
stating to a client, because the alternative to paying it is guessing. Two consequences follow,
and both are commercial rather than technical:
1 ASK FOR THE DXF. One request at intake removes the whole cost and raises every quantity
from SCALED/MED to exact. 2 BATCH IT. K14 sheets at a time, run while other work proceeds.
A T4-heavy set is a programme item, not something absorbed silently.

                                11.9 WHAT REMAINS, HONESTLY


After §11, extraction is reproducible: same bytes in, same values out, on any machine, on any
date, provably.
It is NOT thereby correct. A whitelist-constrained, dual-engine, confidence- floored OCR read
of a poor scan can still be wrong. What has changed is that it is wrong in a fixed, locatable,
one-time-fixable way, and that every value it could not read with confidence is ILLEGIBLE
rather than plausible.
Accuracy is bought elsewhere — by the two-source rule, the cross-check gates and the ad-
versarial review. Determinism is what makes those gates mean something, because a gate
applied to a moving target proves nothing.

AD.1 Every emitted field carries a determinism class D, T or J. AD.2 No field is class J outside
the §3 register. AD.3 Every J field appears in judgements[] with options, rule and reason. AD.4
The determinism ratio is reported. AD.5 Every threshold used appears in §2 by ID; no inline
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                 104



constant duplicates one. AD.6 Every decision listed in §4 was made by its table, top to bottom,
first match winning. AD.7 Every closed-vocabulary field holds a listed value. AD.8 Confidence
was assigned by the §5 rule, not by impression. AD.9 Every array is sorted per §6. AD.10
Every tie-break is logged with the rule that broke it. AD.11 No computation listed in §8 was
performed by the model. AD.12 input_digest is emitted. AD.13 No date, random source or
undeclared state was consulted. AD.14 Re-running this seat on these inputs would produce
this output.
— EXTRACTION, §11 —————————————————— AD.15 Every document carries a
source_tier T1–T4, set by probe. AD.16 No extracted value was produced by the model. E1
emits zero class-J fields. AD.17 Every length and area from T1–T3 came from vector geom-
etry, never from a picture. AD.18 Every T4 length carries geometry_source SCALED and a
calibration. AD.19 Rasterisation used K26–K29 exactly; no deskew, no denoise, no sharpen-
ing, no adaptive threshold. AD.20 The rendered bitmap hash is recorded per rasterised page.
AD.21 OCR used the pinned engine at K30/K31/K32 with the field-class whitelist at K34–K36.
AD.22 No word below K33 confidence was emitted as a value. AD.23 No dictionary, language
model or autocorrect touched an OCR result. AD.24 Every OCR numeric passed K37 dual-
engine unanimity, or is ILLEGIBLE with both readings recorded. AD.25 Every T4 sheet used
for a length has two calibration dimensions agreeing within K39. AD.26 No length was taken
from a scale bar. AD.27 Element presence was decided by the §11.7 table, not judged. AD.28
toolchain[] is recorded with exact versions and hashes. AD.29 content_hash is recorded per
document and input_digest per seat.


R-FOLDER-SEQUENCE — folder by folder, revision by revi-
sion
skills/pomi-take-off/references/folder-sequence.md · 45 lines

When the inputs are split across several folders, the take-off is produced one folder at a
time, in the order the folders appear, and each completed folder is issued as a numbered
revision before the next folder starts. This keeps a steady issue rhythm and a clean audit
trail of how the works developed.

The rule
   • Each subfolder is a successive issue of the same scope — e.g. Tender, then IFC, then
     IFC-RevB. Folder order = issue order (as the folders are listed).
   • For each folder, in order, run the full gated pipeline: validate → read every drawing (no-
     skip) → measure → reconcile against the schedules → gate check → build. On success
     it is issued as a revision: first folder → Rev 0 (baseline), next → Rev 1, and so on,
     automatically.
   • Because each issue supersedes the previous, every Rev ≥ 1 carries a “REVISION
     CHANGES” sheet inside its own workbook listing what the new issue added, omit-
     ted and changed (old → new quantity and the difference) versus the prior Rev. The
     revision Excel is the only deliverable — the delta lives inside it, not as a separate file.
   • A folder that fails reconciliation or the gates HALTS the whole sequence at that
     folder. The next folder does not start until it is resolved. Folders are never skipped.

How it runs
python scripts/run_batch.py <parent_dir> --out <parent_dir>/out

<parent_dir> contains the issue subfolders. Each issue subfolder must hold, by the time the
batch finalises it, the model-produced evidence for that issue: <issue>/work/inventory.json and
<issue>/work/takeoff.json (built exactly as in the single-folder pipeline — pipeline.md). The batch
then, per folder in order: reconciles, gate-checks, builds out/Rev{N}/TakeOff_Rev{N}.xlsx + call-
out drawings, embeds the supersede delta for N ≥ 1, appends to out/revisions.json, and moves
to the next folder — stopping immediately if any folder fails.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                  105



Why per-folder, not all-at-once
Issuing folder-by-folder means each revision is a complete, gated, defensible deliverable in
its own right, and the change between issues is explicit. A later issue can never quietly drop
scope: the supersede sheet shows every omission, and the reconciliation gate still requires
every scheduled element of that issue to be measured.


HOUSE TEMPLATE — LOCKED (R-VERBATIM)
skills/pomi-take-off/references/house-template.md · 429 lines

Version 2.0 — measured from the issued tender bills. Every figure below was read out
of the client’s own workbooks, not inferred and not designed. verify_template.py diffs the pro-
duced workbook against this file and fails the run on any deviation.
     Supersedes the Enabling Works template, which is withdrawn to house-template-
     ENABLING-WORKS-WITHDRAWN.md. That template was measured honestly, but off a single
     5-page PDF that turned out not to be this office’s issue format: it had US Letter
     paper, Calibri 8.9 pt, six Excel columns and a fully ruled grid. The issued bills are
     A4, Arial 10 pt, eight Excel columns and vertical rules only. A workbook built to
     the old template is not this format and never was. Do not read that file to build
     anything.
Source of measurement. Eleven issued tender workbooks — a Cover, Pricing Preambles,
a Grand Summary and Bills 1 to 8 — comprising 61 non-cover sheets and several hundred
bill pages. Figures below are the values those sheets actually carry; where the set is not
unanimous the spread is stated and the house value named.
No project identity is recorded here. Client, project, package, building, section content,
quantities and rates are fields the run fills, never constants. Only wording that is the same on
every job is frozen.

THE DESCRIPTION-AND-VARIANTS STRUCTURE — the house billing convention
This is how the issued bills compose an item, and the STRUCTURE is used in every one
of the 31 bill sheets — including Equipment, Furnishings and Signage. What varies by
discipline is what the variants vary BY: thicknesses in Concrete and Masonry, sizes in
Mechanical and Electrical, widths and types in Finishes, and named schedule references,
not sizes, in Equipment and Furnishings (0 sized runs out of 35 and 25 respectively). Do
not expect a size; expect the structure. The wording formulas differ by discipline too — see
description-conventions.md.

Walls                                                       ← element heading, one line
                                                            ← blank
Precast concrete block, bedded and jointed in cement        ← DESCRIPTION BLOCK
mortar including wall ties, bed, joints, reinforcement,        no item ref, no quantity,
head restraint, ties and anchors including wall head,          no rate. Two lines or more.
vertical and base, joints, filler, sealant and grouting
complete in accordance with the Specifications and
Drawings
                                                            ← blank
Hollow Block Walls                                          ← sub-heading, one line (optional)
                                                            ← blank
A   Walls, 100mm thick, type C0a         34      m2   95    ← VARIANTS. One row each,
                                                               one blank row between.
B   Walls, 150mm thick, type C0b         24      m2   101
                                                               Each inherits the
C   Walls, 200mm thick, type C0c         46      m2   106      description above.

On MEP the variants are pipe sizes — 20mm PPR Piping, 25mm, 32mm, 40mm, 65mm, 80mm — under one
“Supply and install all Domestic Water Piping System … including but not limited to all pip-
ing, fittings, angles, ells, tees, reducers, valves, heads, supports…”. On Concrete they are
thicknesses; on Finishes, widths. Same structure every time.
Why this is one spec entry (kind: "item_group") and not a narrative followed by loose
items. The description is what makes the rate binding. A line reading 20mm PPR Piping at 16.00
says nothing about whether the rate covers the fittings, the valves, the supports or the testing
— the paragraph above it does, and that paragraph is what the contractor is held to. Split
them into separate spec entries and a later edit can move one without the other, leaving a
priced size with nothing behind it. So:
    • The builder emits the description block once, then every variant, as one atomic group,
      and the group never splits across a page — a contractor pricing page 5 cannot read page
      4.
    • verify_template.py fails a run of sized variants that has no description block of two or more
      lines above it, looking back past any one-line sub-heading.
The item letters run straight through the group — the variants take the next letters in the
page’s sequence, they do not restart.

Item serial letters — A, B, C … and NEVER I or O They run A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, J, K,
L, M, N, P, Q, R, S … — restarting at A on every page, and skipping both I and O. They are
not sequential through a section.
Measured across every sheet in the issued set: I appears zero times and O appears zero times
as an item reference; the longest observed page runs A B C D E F G H J K L M N P Q R S. Confirmed
by the office as the house rule.
The reason to gate this rather than trust it: I next to 1 and O next to 0 is exactly the confusion
a priced bill cannot afford, and the error is invisible once printed — every other letter on the
page still looks right, so nothing draws the eye to it.
verify_template.py rebuilds the expected sequence for each page and fails on any deviation. Run
against the issued bills it finds nine pages that break the rule — one uses I (…G H I J L M N), one
repeats itself (A B A B C D E F…), and seven skip letters where an item was deleted in a revision
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                       109



and the sequence was never re-lettered (A C E G H J K, A B D E, A B C D F G, C D E). Those are
defects in those pages, not in this rule.

8. WORKBOOK ARCHITECTURE
One workbook per bill. Inside it, a Cover sheet precedes every section sheet — Cover 1,
Summary, Cover 2, {first section}, Cover 3, {second section}, and so on. Cover sheets are A1:J38, use
merged rows A{n}:I{n}, and carry the project identity only.
The Grand Summary is its own workbook and links to each bill workbook by external reference.



9. HOW THIS FILE IS ENFORCED
verify_template.py opens the produced workbook and re-derives every figure above indepen-
dently — widths, heights, fonts, number formats, border map, band offsets, the 62-row rhythm,
the =SUM ranges and every frozen string. It does not read the builder’s constants; if it did, the
two would agree by construction and prove nothing.

       One deliberate regularisation. The issued page B/1 renders its item AMOUNT

2. FROZEN STRINGS — headers and plumbing

AMOUNT carries a leading space and AED a trailing space. They are in the issued cells and they
shift the centred string; keep them.
Rules: - The printed section title is the PACKAGE name; the POMI classification is
declared separately. The issued sample heads section B ENABLING WORKS, which is not POMI’s
title for B (POMI calls it Site Work). That is legitimate on a commercial heading — but it is
declared, not assumed: the spec carries pomi_section_title, and verify_sections.py tests THAT
against POMI’s own headings. Omit the declaration and the printed title is tested instead, so
a bill cannot claim a POMI section by silence. - Page 1 of a section carries the bare section
title. Every continuation page carries the same title with the suffix [CONT'D] — a single space,
square brackets, apostrophe, upper case. - Item references restart at A on every page and
run A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, J, … — the letter I is skipped. (The sample runs H then J.) -
Page codes are B/1, B/2, B/3 …, collection page B/S. - The COLLECTION page lists one row per
preceding page, in order, each with its amount cell. - A page carrying no priced item — the
Generally page — shows To Collection with a blank amount, not a nil dash, and its line on the
COLLECTION page is blank too. The builder tells the two cases apart with COUNT(), and totals
with SUM() rather than + so a blank line cannot poison the addition.

3A. ITEM DESCRIPTIONS — the wrap is frozen too
Item descriptions are supplied by the project, but their line breaks are computed and writ-
ten into the cell, not left to Excel to recompute when the file is opened. The builder measures
with Carlito (metric-compatible with Calibri) at a usable width of 224.5 pt and joins the lines
with explicit newlines.
That width was calibrated against every wrapped description on the issued pages: any value
between 223.3 and 227.9 pt reproduces all ten of them break for break. 224.5 sits mid-
window and stays under Excel’s own usable width (228.7 less ~3 pt of cell padding), so a
pre-written line can never re-wrap and silently add a row.
The item letter, quantity, unit and amount are vertically centred against the whole de-
scription block, which is how the issued sheet sets them.

Group headings — SITE WORKS, Site preparation, Ground Improvement, Excavation & Filling, Disposal,
Shoring — all sit in the Description column in bold AND underlined, ONE style. There is no
separate style for a trade heading versus an element heading.

THE TWO QUANTITY COLUMNS — the rule the whole format turns on
Qty         = No of Units x (Area | Volume | Length)          MEASURED value, 2 dp
Total Qty   = ROUNDUP( SUM of that item's Qty rows , 0 )      BILLED value, BOLD

Verified on every item of the issued sheet:

                 Item                 Qty                                   Total Qty
                 Site clearance       1,152.03                              1,153.00
                 Excavation           9,897.79 + 740.14 = 10,637.93         10,638.00
                 Shoring 9.2 m        101.11                                102.00
                 Capping beam         102.00 + 36.00 = 138.00               138.00


The BOQ page links DIRECTLY to Total Qty. It is already rounded. Applying ROUNDUP
again on the bill page double-rounds and is wrong.
Sub-measure rows. Where an item is built up from more than one measurement, the ITEM
row carries the description, unit and Total Qty; each constituent sits on its own row below
carrying only Ref (the label), its dimension columns, Qty and DWG Ref. The item row’s own
dimension columns stay empty.
Live formulas, not typed numbers. Area = Length x Width · Volume = Area x Height · Qty = No of
Units x (Area | Volume | Length) · Total Qty = ROUNDUP(SUM(constituent Qty rows), 0).

Font must be set on EVERY cell explicitly. Do not change the workbook default font to
achieve it — Excel measures column width in characters of the default font, so changing it
silently renarrows every column. The default stays Calibri 11; every cell is written as Calibri
7.2.

5. ROUNDING — where each figure lives
Both figures appear on the MEASUREMENT SHEET, in two different columns. This is the
correction to the earlier reading of this template:
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                               118



     Qty carries the MEASURED quantity at two decimals. Total Qty carries the BILLED
     quantity — ROUNDUP(SUM of the item's Qty rows, 0), in bold.
The BOQ page then takes Total Qty as it stands. It is already rounded, and applying ROUNDUP
a second time on the bill page is wrong.
Rounding is UP to the next whole unit for m, m², m³ and nr.
Never round the measurement to make it agree with the bill. The difference between the two
columns IS the rounding, and it is visible on purpose — 1,152.03 against 1,153.00, 10,637.93
against 10,638.00, 101.11 against 102.00.

6. DWG REF HYPERLINK (R-MARKUP-LINK)
Column 14 is not text. Every populated DWG Ref cell is an Excel hyperlink whose display text
is the drawing number (S-02-002) and whose target is the marked-up PDF that proves that
quantity:
markups/{NN}. {Trade Item}.pdf

numbered in bill order — 1. Site Clearance.pdf, 2. Ground Improvements.pdf, 3. Excavation.pdf, 4.
Shoring.pdf. Relative path, so the workbook and the markups/ folder travel together.

A measured row with no markup link is a FAIL (gate G7). Every quantity in the bill must
be traceable to a coloured region on a drawing.

7. MARKED-UP SHEET — layout
One PDF per bill item group, built by overlaying the issued drawing. Reproduce exactly:
   • Banner, centred across the top: SECTION {letter} - {SECTION TITLE} in ~20pt.
   • Identity block, two columns beneath the banner, boxed: Project: {project} / Building:
     {building} on the left; Drawing: {drawing_no} / Filename: {filename} on the right.

   • Legend panel, right-hand margin, boxed and separated from the drawing by a vertical
     rule. Title Legend right-aligned in ~16pt, then the group name (Enabling Works), then one
     row per measured item: a filled colour swatch, the item name, the quantity, the unit.
     Legend
     Enabling Works
     [swatch] Site Clearance     1,152.03 m2
     [swatch] Excavation - Depth - 9.20m       9,897.79 m3
     [swatch] Shoring - Depth - 9.2m    101.11 m

     Item name, then quantity to two decimals with separators, then the unit. One swatch
     colour per measured item, consistent between the legend and the drawing.
   • Footer, centred: CostX.
   • The measurement itself, over the drawing:
        – area/volume items → semi-transparent colour fill across the measured region
        – linear items → coloured boundary line along the measured run, ~2pt
        – one distinct colour per sub-item, so Depth 9.2m and Depth 9.7m read apart.
Naming convention in the legend follows the sample: {Item} - Depth - {d}m for depth-split items
(Excavation - Depth - 9.20m, Shoring - Depth - 9.2m).

Points that are easy to get wrong:
        • heading and narrative are different kinds. A heading is bold and underlined and takes
          one row; a narrative is regular weight, underlined, and takes one row per supplied line.
          Do not push a heading through as a one-line narrative.
        • narrative lines are frozen. The builder writes them as given, one per row, trailing spaces
          and all. It does not re-wrap them. Break them where the source breaks them.
        • item.description is NOT pre-split. The builder computes the wrap (§3A). Give it the whole
          sentence.
        • item_key links the bill line to the measurement sheet. With it, QTY becomes a live
          reference to Total Qty. Without it, supply qty — or neither, and the line bills nil.
        • rate_only still honours qty. The issued sheet bills Vibro Compaction as 1 Item, Rate Only.
        • Pagination is a spec decision. One entry in boq_pages is one printed page. If the content
          overflows the 56-row body band the builder aborts rather than reflowing — split the page
          in the spec.
        • A page may not END on a heading. A heading left as the last row with its items
          overleaf is an orphan; the builder aborts. Move the heading to the next page.
        • pomi_section_title is REQUIRED, even where it matches the printed heading. The printed
          heading is the package name a client reads; the POMI classification is a recorded fact. A
          declaration present only when it differs is one nobody can trust, so the builder refuses to
          compile without it.
        • The Generally page is its own boq_pages entry, and the COLLECTION page is generated; do
          not list it.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                120



8B. THE WORKED EXAMPLE
references/issued-sample-spec.json is the spec that reproduces the client’s issued five-page sam-
ple exactly — every heading, narrative, item, rate-only line and page break. It is the regression
fixture for this template. Build it, render it, diff it against the issued PDF; it must come back
0 mismatches. Change the builder and re-run it before changing anything else.

9. HOW THIS FILE WAS VERIFIED — and how to verify it again
Reading a format and reproducing it is not the same as matching it. This template was wrong
in nine ways that only surfaced when a replica was rendered and diffed against the issued
PDF: the typeface, the page borders, the Rate Only column, four weight/underline rules, the
nil-quantity format, and the row heights the recalculation gate was destroying.
The method, and the standard for any future change:
  1. Build a spec that reproduces the issued sample exactly — every string, every page.
  2. Run the builder, then render the workbook to PDF.
  3. Extract every text span from both PDFs and compare (column, weight, string). Not a
     visual check. A span-by-span diff.
  4. Extract the vector rules from both and compare the x of every vertical and the y of every
     horizontal.
  5. Read the saved workbook back after the recalculation gate. Recalculation is a round trip
     through another application and it rewrites things — row heights, cell hyperlinks — that
     were correct when they were written.
The current replica diffs 0 mismatches across all four pages — 70 / 82 / 22 / 19 text spans,
each in the same column, at the same weight, carrying the same string.


Take-off Workbook Format — LEGACY v1
skills/pomi-take-off/references/takeoff-format.md · 155 lines

     This is NOT the client’s issued house format. It describes the older multi-tab
     dimension-paper workbook rendered by scripts/build_takeoff.py, kept so that earlier
     runs can still be re-rendered. Its Arial 9 / blue header styling is that format’s, not
     the house one.
     For anything issued to the client, the governing document is house-template.md v2.0 —
     Arial, the fourteen-column measurement sheet, the 62-row BOQ pages with vertical
     rules only, the COLLECTION page — rendered by build_house_takeoff.py and gated by
     verify_template.py.

The output is a multi-tab Excel dimension-paper take-off. Do not build the workbook by
hand — assemble a take-off JSON and render it with scripts/build_takeoff.py, which guarantees
the house format, the live formulas, and the linked collection block. This file documents the
JSON contract and the format so you know what to produce.

Workbook structure
   • INDEX tab first: bill letter, discipline, and tab pointer for every section actually pro-
     duced.
   • One tab per POMI section present in the project, named "<Letter>. <NAME>" (e.g. C. CONCRETE).
     Only emit sections the project contains — detect from the evidence; do not pad with
     empty sections.
   • Three audit tabs at the end: AN.RECONCILIATION, AN.SUBSTANTIVE, AN.COVERAGE (mandatory — see
     universal-rules.md).

Section tab layout (fixed)
Two independent blocks sit side by side, with column M as a narrow spacer:
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                           121



Take-off block (cols A–L) — the measurement, one item after another:

A           B          C         D      E        F       G         H        I      J          K      L
Ref    Level           Item      ElementNr       L (m)   W         H/Thk Qty       Tot.       Unit   Grid /
(draw- /               code      /                       (m)       (m)   each                        loca-
ing)   Floor                     build-                                                              tion
                                 up


Each item is: a header row (code in C, full spec narrative in D, both bold) → one or more
dimensioned lines → a qty to bill row whose J cell sums the item’s line totals.
     • I (Qty each) = a live formula of whichever dimensions are present (=F*G*H, =F*H, …) or a
       direct value when the line gives qty_each.
     • J (Tot.) = =E*I always (E is the Nr timesing multiplier).
     • qty to bill J = =SUM(...) over the item’s line totals.
Collection block (cols N–P) — an independent list from row 3, one row per item code:

                                             N           O     P
                                             Item code   Qty   Unit


O is a live formula linking to that code’s qty to bill cell (=J<row>), so the collection always
equals the take-off. (The sample file held static values here; we link them per the agreed
method so the workbook recalculates.)

Styling (matches the reference file exactly)
Handled by the builder — listed so you can verify: - Font Arial 9 throughout; tab title Arial 11
bold in A1. - Header band row 2: white bold text on fill 1F4E78 (dark blue), wrapped, centred.
Freeze panes at A3. - Measurement lines: thin grey border on cols A–L. Item header row and
qty to bill row: bold, no border. - Collection block cells: fill E2EFDA (light green). - Numbers:
#,##0.00. No emoji, no colour-coding beyond the above.


Item coding
<SECTION LETTER>-<SEQUENCE> running A, B, C … within the section (C-A, C-B, …). Companion items
(formwork, reinforcement) get their own sequential codes; tie them to the parent element
with a shared note in the description (e.g. “raft R1”) rather than a code suffix, unless a suffix
reads more clearly to the QS.

JSON contract
{
    "project": "Project name or null (NEVER hard-code a real project name in the skill)",
    "descriptor": "G+4+R or null",
    "sections": [
      {
          "letter": "C",
          "name": "CONCRETE",
          "items": [
            {
                "code": "C-A",
                "description": "Full POMI spec narrative: 100 mm blinding under raft, C15",
                "unit": "m2",
                "lines": [
                  {"ref":"{dwg}","level":"{level}","desc":"Blinding to raft underside",
                  "nr":1,"L":1200.00,"W":null,"H":null,"qty_each":720.00,
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                122



                        "location":"Grids {x}-{y} / A-G"},
                        {"memo":"basis / reuse note, rendered italic with no quantity"}
                    ]
                }
            ]
        }
    ],
    "audit": {
        "reconciliation": [["sample","result","variance","action"]],
        "substantive":           [["row","gate","token","confidence","action"]],
        "coverage":              [["section","source document","available/assumed","note"]]
    }
}


Drawing hyperlinks (R34) Every tagged drawing number in the Ref (drawing) column (col
A) should be a working hyperlink to its source drawing, so anyone reviewing the take-off
can click a reference and open the drawing it was measured from. Provide a drawing_links map
at the top of the JSON, keyed by drawing number:
"drawing_links": {
    "{dwg-s}": "drawings/{dwg-s}.pdf",
    "{dwg-a}": "Tender_Drawings.pdf#page=12",
    "CHW-LAYOUT": "https://docs.example.com/CHW-LAYOUT.pdf"
}

Targets may be a relative path (to a drawings folder beside the workbook), an absolute path,
or a URL; append #page=N to land on a specific page of a combined PDF. The builder turns
each matching col-A cell into a blue underlined hyperlink. A single line may override the
register with its own "ref_link". If a drawing has no entry, the reference stays as plain text (no
fabricated link) and the gap can be noted in AN.COVERAGE — never invent a path.
Item field notes: - "pending": true on an item (used for reinforcement with no bar bending
schedule) renders the element and its Nr floor multiplier with the quantity columns blank and
a “PENDING BBS” flag in the qty-to-bill cell, instead of a computed total. The collection
block reflects the same flag. Use it so rebar is always visible on the sheet without inventing a
weight; also log the gap in audit.coverage.
Line field notes: - Give either L/W/H dimensions (so Qty each computes live) or a direct qty_each
when the area/volume is read straight off a schedule. If both appear, the dimensions win and
qty_each is ignored. - nr is the timesing multiplier (floor count, number of identical bays, both
faces of formwork, …). Default 1. - A {"memo": "..."} line renders as an italic, non-priced note
— used for the formwork reuse / procurement basis and any other build-up commentary. - An
optional "markup": {"page": 1, "x": 330, "y": 250} block records where the element sits on its
vector PDF drawing (PDF points, top-left origin), used by the drawing call-out markup. See
drawing-markup.md. Omit it if you cannot place the item — it will still be listed in the drawing
legend. - unit is set once per item and flows to both the take-off Unit column and the collection
block.


ITEM DESCRIPTION CONVENTIONS — measured from the
issued bills
skills/pomi-take-off/references/description-conventions.md · 103 lines

How this office composes the wording of a bill item. Measured across eleven issued tender
workbooks, 31 bill sheets and 3,605 priced items. Binding on B1 and on any seat that drafts
an item description.
No project wording is recorded here. Where the issued bills name a particular design
standard, that name is a field the run fills, never a constant.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                         123



1. THE STRUCTURE IS UNIVERSAL. THE SIZES ARE NOT.
A description block followed by a run of priced variants that inherit it appears in every one
of the 31 bill sheets — Site Work, Concrete, Masonry, Metalwork, Woodwork, Thermal &
Moisture, Doors & Windows, Finishes, Accessories, Equipment, Furnishings, Conveying, Me-
chanical, Electrical, Signage, Landscaping, Roads, Dayworks and General Requirements alike.
What differs is what the variants vary by:

Sections                           The variants are                  Example
C Concrete · D Masonry · G         thicknesses                       Grade slab, 150mm thick · Walls,
Thermal                                                              250mm thick, 2hr fire rated
Q Mechanical · R Electrical        sizes                             20mm PPR Piping · 25mm · 32mm ·
                                                                     40mm · 65mm · 80mm
J Finishes · K Accessories         widths and types                  200mm wide, type I-NS 2
L Equipment · M Furnishings        named types and schedule          FD-1 · FCO
· Signage                          refs, not sizes


Counted: 15 of Concrete’s 34 shared-description runs carry sized variants, 11 of Mechanical’s
31, 4 of Masonry’s 11 — but 0 of Equipment’s 35 and 0 of Furnishings’ 25. So do not
expect a size. Expect the structure.
     An earlier version of this file said the sized pattern held “in every section”. It does
     not. The structure does; the sizes are a civil-and-MEP habit. Equipment, Furnish-
     ings and Signage bill by named type, and a rule that demanded a size there would
     be wrong.



2. THREE CLOSING FORMULAS, BY SECTION FAMILY
The description block ends with a formula that binds the rate to the project documents, and
the formula differs by discipline. All three are frozen except for the bracketed field.

Family 1 — structure and envelope · sections B, C, D, E, G
     … complete in accordance with the Specifications and Drawings

143 uses. C 66 · G 41 · E 12 · D 10 · B 7 · J 7. A variant adds the approving party: … in accordance
with the Specifications, Drawings and the {approving party} approval.


Family 2 — finishes and fit-out · sections F, J, K
     … in accordance with the {design standard document}, Specifications and Drawings

334 uses, 326 of them in Finishes. The {design standard document} is the project’s own design
book — on the sample project a theme design booklet. Name it from the project’s own
documents; never carry a name across from another job. The order of the three varies
in the issued bills (…Specifications and Drawings / …Drawings and Specifications); the house form is
the one above.

Family 3 — MEP · sections Q and R            The full sentence, and it is a template:
     Supply and install all {system} as shown on the drawings and/or as specified including but
     not limited to {the components the rate covers} and any other items required for a complete
     installation as indicated.

63 openers · 39 as shown on the drawings and/or as specified · 99 including but not limited to · 72
closers. Q and R both, in roughly equal measure.
The middle list is what the rate is deemed to include and it is the commercially operative part.
Worked example from a piping description: piping, fittings, angles, ells, tees, reducers, valves,
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                               124



heads, supports. From a drainage one: fittings, angles, ells, clean outs, reducers, trust blocks,
vaults, trenching, backfilling, supports, acoustic insulation.
Write that list from the POMI deemed-included list for the clause being billed (pomi-
verbatim.md), not from memory. A component omitted from the list is a component the contrac-
tor can claim for; a component included that POMI already deems included is harmless but
redundant.



3. A DEFECT IN THE ISSUED BILLS, FOR AWARENESS
Section R closes eight descriptions with
     … required for a complete installation a indicated.

a for as. It is a typo repeated through the Electrical bills. Do not reproduce it — the correct
closer is Family 3 above. Recorded here so that a comparison against those bills does not read
the corrected wording as a deviation.



4. HOW A DESCRIPTION IS LAID OUT
Set out in house-template.md §4. In short: the description block occupies consecutive rows of
column C with no item reference, no quantity and no rate; one blank row; then each variant on
its own row with one blank row between. An optional one-line sub-heading may sit between
the description and the variants — Hollow Block Walls, uPVC Pipe. The whole group is atomic and
never splits across a page.
verify_template.py fails a run of sized variants carrying no description block above it.



AETRAA Universal Rules — Take-off Edition
skills/pomi-take-off/references/universal-rules.md · 85 lines

These are the AETRAA house rules, applied to quantity take-off. Read once at session start.
They are mandatory and cannot be overridden by user input during a run. Where the source
rules assume a priced bill or a render, the spirit is preserved: the take-off must be evidence-
based, transparent, net, and honest about what is missing.

Platform rules
   • P1 / R-NO-CODE — No Python, script, tool, library, or variable references in any user-
     facing output. The workbook reads as a professional QS take-off only. Method labels,
     where needed, use neutral terms (“measured to scale”, “schedule cell”, “vector take-off”,
     “visual”, “computed”).
   • P3 — No emoji in any cell, label, heading, or note.
   • P4 — Formal RICS QS language throughout. No casual phrasing in the workbook.
   • P9 — Zero storage beyond the output file(s). Do not log user inputs.
   • P12 — 4-pass dual-role pipeline, mandatory every run:
        – Pass 1 (QS): read the evidence, identify sections present, capture every dimen-
          sion/count with its source.
        – Pass 2 (QS): independently re-measure a sample and reconcile against Pass 1.
        – Pass 3 (Senior QS): adversarial challenge — re-open every assumption, every form-
          work face, every floor multiplier, every riser length. The Senior QS may not trust
          Pass 1.
        – Pass 4: render the workbook only after Pass 3 is clean.
   • P16 — Use clickable multi-choice questions for any genuinely optional setting with a
     fixed list (e.g. which sections, measurement scope). Free text only for open answers.
     Do not halt for a missing project name — use it if given, else a neutral placeholder, and
     proceed.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              125



   • P17 — live formulas. Quantities are computed by live Excel formulas (Qty each, Tot., qty
     to bill, and the linked collection block). Never paste a value where a formula belongs;
     changing a dimension must cascade to the item total and the collection. (The visual
     styling matches the reference file rather than the blue/yellow input convention, because
     matching the reference is the explicit deliverable — but the formula-liveness requirement
     stands.)

Measurement integrity gates
   • R-NO-HALLUCINATION — Every quantity traces to a document, a DXF, or the §11 ex-
     traction record (extraction/extraction.json). No “typical”, “assumed”, “standard practice”.
     If the evidence is silent, the item is a gap recorded in AN.COVERAGE, not a number.
   • R-COUNT-FROM-DRAWINGS — Counts counted individually; lengths measured to
     scale. No per-N-m² rules, no ×1.2 factors to derive one quantity from another.
   • R36 — floor multiplier — Record floor scope verbatim; carry the count in the Nr column.
     Never pre-multiply at measurement time.
   • R34 — drawing hyperlinks — Every tagged drawing number in the Ref (drawing) column
     links to its source drawing (PDF path/URL, #page=N for a page), so the measurement is
     traceable to the drawing in one click. Build a drawing_links register keyed by drawing
     number and pass it to the builder. If a drawing is not available, leave the reference as
     plain text and note it in AN.COVERAGE — never fabricate a link target.

Substantive gates (scan every line before Pass 4)
   • G+.25 Fabrication-token scan — flag: typical, placeholder, assumed, estimated, ap-
     proximate, guess, standard practice, UAE typical, TBC, ballpark, rough, nominal, generic.
     Any hit moves to AN.SUBSTANTIVE and the line’s confidence drops to LOW. Exception:
     the token sits inside a quoted drawing label.
   • G+.26 Confidence honesty — HIGH = verbatim from a schedule/dimension/spec; MED
     = explicit derivation citing a drawing or an extraction record + HIGH base values; LOW
     = anything else. Downgrade dishonest tags.
   • G+.27 Percentage / factor scan — outside wastage/contingency/VAT/fee contexts, bare
     ×1.1 / ×0.6 uplifts, per-bay or per-N-m² rules, and “factor/ratio” derivations are forbid-
     den. This is the gate that catches a formwork reuse factor sneaking into a quantity —
     measure contact area, keep reuse as a memo.
   • G+.28 Pattern-check omission — do not add elements because they are customary
     (kickers, water stops, weep holes, access hatches). Measure only what the evidence
     shows; if an allowance is needed, raise it for the user to decide.

Mandatory audit tabs
Every workbook carries three audit tabs (the builder creates them from the JSON audit block):
   • AN.RECONCILIATION — Pass 2 sample results, variances found, and how each was
     resolved.
   • AN.SUBSTANTIVE — every G+.25–G+.28 finding: the row, the gate, the token, the
     confidence, the action taken. A clean run has none; any present are honest disclosures
     for the user.
   • AN.COVERAGE — which source documents fed which sections, what was available vs
     assumed, and every gap (e.g. “reinforcement — no bar bending schedule in evidence; one
     BBS would resolve”).
A clean run still carries AN.RECONCILIATION and AN.COVERAGE.
