SECTION GP — GENERAL PRINCIPLES
10 groups · 34 clauses · 12 carrying arithmetic

GP1 Principles of measurement
GP1.1
       These principles of measurement provide a uniform basis for measuring bills of quan-
       tities for works of construction. More detailed information than is required by this
       document may be given to define the precise nature of work or the circumstances
       under which it is to be carried out.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Scope. More detail than POMI requires MAY be given — this is the clause every
HOUSE build-up is made under.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              192



GP1.2
     Amendments to these principles of measurement for use in a particular locality or
     adopted for work not envisaged by this document shall be stated; an appendix is
     provided for such amendments to be recorded.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Local amendments SHALL BE STATED and recorded in POMI’s own Appendix.
A house rule not recorded there is undeclared.

GP1.3
     These principles of measurement may be applied equally to the measurement of
     proposed works and of completed works.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Applies equally to proposed and completed works — so the same formulae serve
a take-off and a final account.

GP2 Bills of quantities
GP2.1
     The objects of bills of quantities are: 1. To assist in the accurate preparation of
     tenders, by providing for measurement of quantities on a uniform basis 2. To provide
     a basis for the financial control of a project, in accordance with the conditions of
     contract.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. The TWO stated objects of a bill of quantities: 1 TO ASSIST IN THE ACCURATE
PREPARATION OF TENDERS, by providing for measurement of quantities ON A UNIFORM
BASIS · 2 TO PROVIDE A BASIS FOR THE FINANCIAL CONTROL OF A PROJECT, in accor-
dance with the conditions of contract. No arithmetic — but object 2 is why a quantity must
stay traceable after award, not only until tender.

GP2.2
     Bills of quantities shall describe and represent the works to be carried out; work
     which cannot be measured accurately shall be described as approximate or given in
     bills of approximate quantities.
Unit: RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
In practice. THE PROVISIONAL RULE, and it is a DUTY, not a fallback. Bills shall DESCRIBE
AND REPRESENT the works; WORK WHICH CANNOT BE MEASURED ACCURATELY SHALL
BE DESCRIBED AS APPROXIMATE, or given in bills of approximate quantities. HOUSE RULE:
WHERE THE INFORMATION IS NOT CLEAR, THE ITEM IS MARKED PROVISIONAL — never
estimated into a precise-looking figure, and never silently omitted. A provisional item carries
FOUR things: (1) the quantity as best it can be derived, (2) the word PROVISIONAL in the
description, (3) WHY it is provisional — what is missing, which document would settle it, and
(4) the technical query raised to close it. Both failure modes are worse than the mark: an
invented precise quantity transfers a risk nobody has priced, and an omitted item is found by
the contractor after award. GP2.2 is what makes ‘I do not know’ a compliant answer.

GP2.3
     Conditions of contract, drawings and specifications shall be provided with the bills
     of quantities.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Conditions, drawings and specification issued with the bill.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                               193



GP2.4
     The section headings and classifications do not impose restrictions upon the format
     and presentation of bills of quantities.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Section headings do not restrict format — which is why a commercial heading
may differ from POMI’s, if declared.

GP3 Measurement
GP3.1
     Work shall be measured net as fixed in position and each measurement shall be taken
     to the nearest 10 millimetres; this principle shall not apply to dimensions stated in
     descriptions.
Unit: RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
d = round(d_drawn / 0.01) × 0.01

In practice. NET as fixed in position, each dimension to the nearest 10 mm. Round each
dimension as taken, not the product. Dimensions in DESCRIPTIONS are exempt.

GP3.2
     Unless otherwise stated, no deduction shall be made from items required to be mea-
     sured by area for voids of less than 1.00 m².
Unit: RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
A_net = A_gross − Σ A_void   for A_void ≥ 1.00 m²

In practice. The area deduction threshold. Applies to items measured BY AREA.

GP3.3
     Minimum deductions of voids shall refer only to voids within the edges of measured
     areas; voids which are at the edges of measured areas shall always be deducted,
     irrespective of size.
Unit: RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
deduct ALL voids at an edge, any size

In practice. The exception to GP3.2, and the one most often missed. Interior voids under
1.00 m² stay; edge voids always go.

GP3.4
     These principles of measurement may be used with other units of measurement but
     the particular amendments shall be stated.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Other units may be used if the amendment is stated.

GP3.5
     Notwithstanding these principles of measurement, a separate minor building or
     structure may be enumerated.
Unit: NR — enumerated — a count
N = 1 per minor building

In practice. A separate minor building or structure MAY be enumerated whole instead of
measured.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                   194



GP4 Items to be fully inclusive
GP4.1
     Unless otherwise stated, all items shall be fully inclusive of all that is necessary
     to fulfill the liabilities and obligations arising out of the contract and shall include:
     1. Labour and all associated costs 2. Materials, goods and all associated costs 3.
     Provision of plant 4. Temporary works 5. Establishment charges, overheads and
     profit.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. What EVERY rate is deemed to include, FIVE heads: 1 LABOUR AND ALL ASSO-
CIATED COSTS · 2 MATERIALS, GOODS AND ALL ASSOCIATED COSTS · 3 PROVISION OF
PLANT · 4 TEMPORARY WORKS · 5 ESTABLISHMENT CHARGES, OVERHEADS AND PROFIT.
This is THE clause that makes waste, laps, rolling margin, working space and bulking rate mat-
ters — add any of them to a quantity and the same money is billed twice.

GP5 Description of items
GP5.1
     Items which are required to be enumerated, or for which an item is required, shall
     be fully described.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Enumerated items and items must be FULLY DESCRIBED.

GP5.2
     Items which are to be measured by length or depth shall state the cross-sectional size
     and shape, girth or ranges of girths or such other information as may be appropriate;
     for items of pipework it shall be stated whether the diameter is internal or external.
Unit: RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
In practice. Length and depth items STATE the cross-sectional size and shape, girth or range
of girths. FOR PIPEWORK IT SHALL BE STATED WHETHER THE DIAMETER IS INTERNAL
OR EXTERNAL. HOUSE ELECTION: INTERNAL DIAMETER IS STATED, converting from a
nominal or external figure where the schedule gives that instead. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-
LEVERAGE STATEMENT IN AN MEP BILL: POMI expresses the Q2.2 60 mm threshold as an
INTERNAL diameter, so a pipe quoted at 65 mm EXTERNAL may be under 60 mm internal —
and a whole class of enumerated fittings appears or disappears on the basis alone. The same
threshold governs J6.3 cl.11 versus J6.4 for decoration.

GP5.3
     Items which are to be measured by area shall state the thickness or such other
     information as may be appropriate.
Unit: RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
In practice. Area items STATE the thickness.

GP5.4
     Items which are to be measured by weight shall state the material thickness and
     unit weight if appropriate (for example, ductwork).
Unit: RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
W = A × m_per_m2   or   L × m_per_m   or   V × ρ

In practice. Weight items STATE the material thickness and unit weight IF APPROPRIATE —
POMI’s own example is DUCTWORK. THE QUALIFIER IS POMI’S: the statement is required
where it bears on the work, not mechanically on every weight item. It plainly IS appropriate
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                195



for sheet material sold by gauge — ductwork, sheet metal, flashings — where the thickness is
the whole difference in cost, and for rolled sections where the unit mass identifies the section.
Take the density and unit mass FROM THE SPECIFICATION OR MANUFACTURER’S DATA,
never from memory, and record the source on the row.

GP5.5
     Notwithstanding these principles of measurement, proprietary items may be mea-
     sured in a manner appropriate to the manufacturer’s tariff or customary practice.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Proprietary items may follow the manufacturer’s tariff — a declared departure
from the formulae here.

GP5.6
     The description of items in bills of quantities may refer to other documents or draw-
     ings and any reference to such information shall be understood to fulfill any require-
     ment of these principles of measurement; alternatively, reference may be made to
     published information.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. A description may refer to another document, and that reference satisfies POMI’s
requirement.

GP6 Work to be executed by a specialist nominated by the employer
GP6.1
     Unless otherwise required by the conditions of contract, work which is required to
     be executed by a specialist nominated by the employer shall be given as a sum; such
     sum shall be exclusive of contractor’s profit and in each case an item shall be given
     for the addition of profit.
Unit: SUM — a SUM — a money figure, not a measured quantity
Sum, exclusive of profit + separate profit item

In practice. Nominated specialist work.

GP6.2
     An item shall be given in each case for assistance by the contractor, which shall
     include: 1. Use of contractor’s administrative arrangements 2. Use of construc-
     tional plant 3. Use of contractor’s facilities 4. Use of temporary works 5. Space for
     specialist’s offices and stores 6. Clearing away rubbish 7. Scaffolding required by
     the specialist, giving particulars 8. Unloading, distributing, hoisting and placing in
     position items of plant, machinery or the like, giving particulars.
Unit: ITEM — an ITEM — a lump, not a measured quantity
In practice. ONE ITEM for ATTENDANCE by the contractor on a nominated specialist, EIGHT
heads: 1 USE OF THE CONTRACTOR’S ADMINISTRATIVE ARRANGEMENTS · 2 USE OF
CONSTRUCTIONAL PLANT · 3 USE OF THE CONTRACTOR’S FACILITIES · 4 USE OF TEM-
PORARY WORKS · 5 SPACE FOR THE SPECIALIST’S OFFICES AND STORES · 6 CLEARING
AWAY RUBBISH · 7 SCAFFOLDING required by the specialist, GIVING PARTICULARS · 8
UNLOADING, DISTRIBUTING, HOISTING AND PLACING IN POSITION items of plant or ma-
chinery, GIVING PARTICULARS. Heads 7 and 8 REQUIRE PARTICULARS — an attendance
item that does not describe the scaffolding and the hoisting is not priceable.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                196



GP7 Goods, materials or services to be provided by a merchant or tradesman nomi-
nated by the employer
GP7.1
     Unless otherwise required by the conditions of contract, goods, materials or services
     which are required to be provided by a merchant or tradesman nominated by the
     employer shall be given as a sum; such sum shall be exclusive of contractor’s profit
     and in each case an item shall be given for the addition of profit.
Unit: SUM — a SUM — a money figure, not a measured quantity
Sum, exclusive of profit + separate profit item

In practice. Nominated merchant goods, materials or services.

GP7.2
     Fixing goods and materials shall be given in accordance with the relevant clauses
     in these principles of measurement; fixing shall be understood to include unload-
     ing, storing, distributing and hoisting the, goods and materials. Particulars shall be
     given of any requirements for the contractor to arrange for delivery or pay any costs
     of conveying goods or materials.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. FIXING measured to the relevant clauses; fixing INCLUDES unloading, storing,
distributing and hoisting.

GP8 Work to be executed by a government or public authority
GP8.1
     Unless otherwise required by the conditions of contract, work which may only be
     carried out or by a government or public authority shall be given as a sum; such
     sum shall be exclusive of contractor’s profit and in each case an item shall be given
     for the addition of profit.
Unit: SUM — a SUM — a money figure, not a measured quantity
Sum, exclusive of profit + separate profit item

In practice. Work only a government or public authority may do — DEWA, Etisalat, du.

GP8.2
     An item shall be given in each case for assistance by the contractor as described in
     clause GP6.2.
Unit: ITEM — an ITEM — a lump, not a measured quantity
In practice. Attendance, as GP6.2.

GP9 Dayworks
GP9.1
     The cost of labour in dayworks shall be given as a sum; alternatively, a schedule of
     the different categories of labour may be given containing a provisional quantity of
     hours for each category.
Unit: SCHEDULE
one priced line per labour category × PROVISIONAL hours

In practice. DAYWORK LABOUR. POMI permits A SUM or, expressly, A SCHEDULE OF
CATEGORIES carrying a PROVISIONAL QUANTITY OF HOURS for each. HOUSE ELECTION:
THE SCHEDULE. A sum is one number against one number and reveals nothing about the
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                               197



rates that will be applied when daywork is ordered; a schedule prices each category, so the
tender is comparable AND the rates are fixed before anyone needs them. The hours are
PROVISIONAL by POMI’s own wording and adjust on the actual, so the schedule costs nothing
in accuracy.

GP9.2
     The cost of labour included in a sum or schedule shall include wages, bonuses and all
     allowances paid to operatives directly engaged on dayworks (including those operat-
     ing mechanical plant and transport) in accordance with the appropriate employment
     agreement or, where no such agreement exists, the actual payments made to the
     work people concerned.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. What daywork labour cost includes.

GP9.3
     The cost of materials in dayworks shall be given as a sum; alternatively, a schedule
     may be given containing a provisional quantity of different materials.
Unit: SCHEDULE
one priced line per material × PROVISIONAL quantity

In practice. DAYWORK MATERIALS, as a SCHEDULE with provisional quantities — same
election as GP9.1. GP9.4 fixes the basis: the NET INVOICED PRICE, INCLUDING DELIVERY
TO SITE.

GP9.4
     The cost of materials included in a sum or schedule shall be the net invoiced price,
     including delivery to site.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Daywork materials at NET INVOICED PRICE including delivery.

GP9.5
     The cost of constructional plant employed exclusively in dayworks shall be given as
     a sum; alternatively, a schedule of the different categories of plant may be given
     containing a provisional quantity of hours, or such other period of time as may be
     appropriate, for each category.
Unit: SCHEDULE
one priced line per plant category × PROVISIONAL hours

In practice. DAYWORK PLANT, as a SCHEDULE with provisional hours — same election as
GP9.1. NOTE THE WORD ‘EXCLUSIVELY’: only plant employed EXCLUSIVELY in dayworks
is here. Plant shared with the permanent works is an OVERHEAD under GP9.8 cl.4 and must
not appear. GP9.6 fixes what the rate covers: fuel, consumable stores, repairs, maintenance
and insurance.

GP9.6
     The cost of constructional plant included in a sum or schedule shall include fuel,
     consumable stores, repairs, maintenance and insurance of plant.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. What daywork plant cost includes.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                               198



GP9.7
     An item shall be given for the addition of establishment charges, overheads and
     profit to each of the sums or schedules of labour, materials or plant.
Unit: ITEM ×3
one addition item against EACH of the three schedules

In practice. An item for the addition of establishment charges, overheads and profit TO
EACH of the sums or schedules of labour, materials and plant. THE WORD IS ‘EACH’ —
three schedules produce THREE addition items, so a daywork section is SIX blocks, not four:
labour schedule + its addition, materials schedule + its addition, plant schedule + its addition.
A single combined addition cannot be applied when only one of the three is expended.

GP9.8
     Establishment charges, overheads and profit shall include: 1. Costs related to the
     employment of labour 2. Costs related to the storage of materials, including han-
     dling and waste in storage 3. Contractor’s administrative arrangements 4. Con-
     structional plant, except plant employed exclusively on dayworks 5. Contractor’s
     facilities 6. Temporary works 7. Sundry items.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. What ESTABLISHMENT CHARGES, OVERHEADS AND PROFIT comprise,
SEVEN heads: 1 COSTS RELATED TO THE EMPLOYMENT OF LABOUR · 2 COSTS RELATED
TO THE STORAGE OF MATERIALS, INCLUDING HANDLING AND WASTE IN STORAGE · 3
THE CONTRACTOR’S ADMINISTRATIVE ARRANGEMENTS · 4 CONSTRUCTIONAL PLANT,
EXCEPT plant employed exclusively on dayworks · 5 THE CONTRACTOR’S FACILITIES · 6
TEMPORARY WORKS · 7 SUNDRY ITEMS. Head 2 is the one that matters to a measurer:
WASTE IN STORAGE is an overhead, which is a second reason a quantity never carries waste.

GP10 Contingencies
GP10.1
     Unless otherwise required by the conditions of contract, contingencies shall be given
     as a sum; no item shall be given for the addition of profit.
Unit: SUM — a SUM — a money figure, not a measured quantity
In practice. Contingencies as a sum. NO profit item — the opposite of GP6/7/8/9.7.


SECTION A — GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

A1 Conditions of contract

In practice. Schedule of clause headings.

A1.2
     Where there is an appendix to the conditions of contract requiring insertions to be
     made, a schedule of the insertions shall be set out in the bills of quantities.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Schedule of appendix insertions.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                199



A2 Specification
A2.1
     Where the specification contains clauses related to any of the following General Re-
     quirements, the bills of quantities shall make reference to the appropriate clauses.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Bill refers to the specification’s General Requirements clauses.

A3 Restrictions
A3.1
     Particulars shall be given of any restrictions, which shall include: 1. Access to and
     possession or use of the site 2. Limitations of working space 3. Limitations of work-

B8.5
     Excavation in rock shall be so described; alternatively, it may be measured as extra
     over excavation (that is, the volume of rock shall be measured but no deduction shall
     be made from the volume of excavation in which the rock occurs).
Unit: M3 — by volume, cubic metres
ROUTE A   V_soil = V_total − V_rock   (two items, summing to the total)
ROUTE B   V_excavation = V_total UNCHANGED
          V_rock       = measured AS WELL

In practice. Excavation in rock. POMI’S PRIMARY LIMB IS ‘SHALL BE SO DESCRIBED’ —
rock described as its own excavation item, the two summing to the total. EXTRA OVER IS THE
EXPRESS ALTERNATIVE, and it is the HOUSE ELECTION: the volume of rock is measured
but NO DEDUCTION is made from the excavation in which it occurs. Under the elected route
the base dig stays whole, which matters because rock is FOUND, not designed. DEDUCTING
THE ROCK FROM THE EXCAVATION LOSES THE BASE ITEM — the same error as B15.2 rock
boring, D2.2 faced work and G2.3 special sheets, and the one people reverse. B8.6 defines
rock, and it is an OPINION, not a geological test.

B8.6

     only be removed by means of wedges, special plant or explosives.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Definition of rock: removable only by wedges, special plant or explosives, in the
employer’s representative’s opinion.

B9 Excavation
B9.1
     Unless otherwise stated, excavation shall be measured by volume as the void which
     is to be occupied by the permanent construction, or vertically above any part of
     the permanent construction, classified as follows: 1. Oversite excavation to remove
     top soil, stating the average depth 2. Excavation to reduce levels 3. Excavation in
     cuttings 4. Basement excavation 5. Trench excavation to receive foundations, which
     shall include pile caps and ground beams 6. Pit excavation to receive foundation
     bases, stating the number 7. Excavation for diaphragm walls, stating the width of
     the permanent construction and the type of support fluid.
Unit: M3 — by volume, cubic metres
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              207



V = N × L × W × D

In practice. Excavation as the VOID TO BE OCCUPIED by the permanent construction, or
vertically above any part of it — L and W are the PERMANENT CONSTRUCTION’s dimensions,
not the dig’s. SEVEN classes: 1 OVERSITE EXCAVATION to remove top soil, STATING THE
AVERAGE DEPTH · 2 EXCAVATION TO REDUCE LEVELS · 3 EXCAVATION IN CUTTINGS ·
4 BASEMENT EXCAVATION · 5 TRENCH EXCAVATION to receive foundations, which SHALL
INCLUDE PILE CAPS AND GROUND BEAMS · 6 PIT EXCAVATION to receive foundation bases,
STATING THE NUMBER · 7 EXCAVATION FOR DIAPHRAGM WALLS, STATING THE WIDTH
of the permanent construction AND THE TYPE OF SUPPORT FLUID. Three classes carry a
mandatory statement: 1 average depth, 6 the number, 7 width and support fluid.

B9.2
     Excavation of trenches for service pipes, drain pipes, cables or the like shall each
     be measured by length, stating the average depth; disposal and filling shall be un-
     derstood to be included.
Unit: M — by length, metres
Len = Σ L, per trench type
d_avg STATED

In practice. Trenches for service pipes, drain pipes, cables or the like shall EACH be mea-
sured BY LENGTH — ‘each’ meaning ONE ITEM PER TRENCH TYPE, not one combined trench
item — STATING THE AVERAGE DEPTH. DISPOSAL AND FILLING ARE DEEMED INCLUDED,
so NOTHING ELSE is measured for that trench: no disposal row under B11, no filling row un-
der B12, no earthwork support. A drainage trench carrying all three has been paid three times
for one operation, and it is the most double-counted item in a site-work bill.

B9.3

Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Tunnel excavation is B24, not B9.

B11 Disposal
B11.1
     Disposal of material arising from excavation, dredging or tunnelling shall be mea-
     sured by volume as equal to the volume of excavation, dredging or tunnelling and
     each shall be classified as follows: 1. Backfilled into excavation 2. Backfilled in
     making up levels 3. Backfilled oversite to make up levels, giving details of special
     contouring, embankments or the like 4. Removed, which shall include providing a
     suitable tip.
Unit: M3 — by volume, cubic metres
V_disposal = V_excavation    (EXACTLY)
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                               208



In practice. Disposal EQUALS the excavation, dredging or tunnelling volume EXACTLY —
no bulking, no shrinkage. FOUR classes, each measured separately: 1 BACKFILLED INTO
EXCAVATION · 2 BACKFILLED IN MAKING UP LEVELS · 3 BACKFILLED OVERSITE TO MAKE
UP LEVELS, GIVING DETAILS of special contouring, embankments or the like · 4 REMOVED,
which SHALL INCLUDE PROVIDING A SUITABLE TIP — so tipping charges are in the rate,
never a separate item.

B12 Filling
B12.1
     Filling material (other than that arising from excavation, dredging or tunnelling)
     shall be measured by volume as equal to the void to be filled, classified as follows:
     1. Filled into excavation 2. Filled in making up levels 3. Filled oversite to make up
     levels, giving details of special contouring, embankments or the like.
Unit: M3 — by volume, cubic metres
V_fill = V_void_to_be_filled

In practice. Filling material OTHER THAN that arising from excavation, dredging or tun-
nelling — so IMPORTED fill only; site-won material returned is B11 ‘backfilled’, and the test
is WHERE THE MATERIAL CAME FROM. Measured as EQUAL TO THE VOID TO BE FILLED
— the designed void, not the loose volume delivered. THREE classes: 1 FILLED INTO EXCA-
VATION · 2 FILLED IN MAKING UP LEVELS · 3 FILLED OVERSITE TO MAKE UP LEVELS,
GIVING DETAILS OF SPECIAL CONTOURING, EMBANKMENTS OR THE LIKE. Note there is
NO ‘removed’ class, the asymmetry with B11’s four: imported material is not taken away. If
you want to bill ‘filling — removed’, you are in the wrong clause.

C1 Generally

     Reinforced poured concrete and plain poured concrete shall each be so described.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Reinforced and plain poured concrete EACH SO DESCRIBED.

C1.2
     Poured concrete required by the specification to be placed, compacted, cured or
     otherwise treated in a particular manner shall be so described.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Special placing, compacting, curing or treatment SO DESCRIBED.

C1.3
     No deduction shall be made for voids less than 1.00 m3, nor for the volume of any
     reinforcement or structural metal enclosed in the concrete, except that voids caused
     by boxed or tubular structural metalwork shall always be deducted.
Unit: RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
V_net = V_gross − Σ V_void(≥1.00 m³) − Σ V_boxed_or_tubular_steel

In practice. The concrete deduction rule. NO deduction for rebar or for solid enclosed steel.
BOXED OR TUBULAR steel is ALWAYS deducted, at any size.

C1.4
     Unless otherwise described, horizontal surfaces of concrete shall be understood to
     be tamped.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Horizontal concrete surfaces UNDERSTOOD TO BE TAMPED unless otherwise
described — so a tamped finish is not a measurable item.

C2 Poured concrete
C2.1
     Unless otherwise stated, poured concrete shall be measured by volume, classified
     as follows: 1. Foundations, which shall include combined or isolated bases 2. Pile
     caps, which shall include ground beams 3. Blinding 4. Beds, which shall include
     roads and footpaths, stating the thickness 5. Suspended slabs, which shall include
     floors, landings, roofs or the like, stating the thickness 6. Walls, which shall include
     attached columns, stating the thickness 7. Columns, which shall include casing to
     metal stancheons 8. Beams (measured below the slab), which shall include lintels
     and casing to metal beams 9. Staircases, which shall include steps and strings 10.
     Diaphragm walls 11. Other classifications (for example, tunnel linings, bridge abut-
     ments) as may be appropriate.
Unit: M3 — by volume, cubic metres
V = N × L × W × T
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                               219



In practice. Poured concrete by VOLUME, ELEVEN classes: 1 FOUNDATIONS, which IN-
CLUDE combined or isolated bases · 2 PILE CAPS, which INCLUDE GROUND BEAMS · 3
BLINDING · 4 BEDS, which INCLUDE ROADS AND FOOTPATHS, STATING THE THICKNESS
· 5 SUSPENDED SLABS, which INCLUDE floors, landings and roofs, STATING THE THICK-
NESS · 6 WALLS, which INCLUDE ATTACHED COLUMNS, STATING THE THICKNESS · 7
COLUMNS, which INCLUDE CASING TO METAL STANCHEONS · 8 BEAMS, MEASURED BE-
LOW THE SLAB, which INCLUDE lintels and casing to metal beams — V = N × b × (D − t_slab)
× L · 9 STAIRCASES, which INCLUDE STEPS AND STRINGS · 10 DIAPHRAGM WALLS · 11
other classifications, e.g. tunnel linings, bridge abutments. Classes 4, 5 and 6 each STATE
THE THICKNESS.

C2.2
     Poured concrete suspended slabs of special construction, including floors, landings,
     roofs or the like, shall be measured by area; coffered and troughed slabs shall be so
     described, giving details of solid margins or the like.
Unit: M2 — by area, square metres
A = Σ (L × W) − voids

In practice. Suspended slabs of SPECIAL construction BY AREA, not volume. Coffered and
troughed SO DESCRIBED with details of solid margins.

C2.3
     Where an item is required to be measured by volume and the thickness stated, then
     items of differing thickness may be grouped together, provided that the range of the
     different thicknesses is stated.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Differing thicknesses MAY be GROUPED provided the RANGE is stated. HOUSE
RULE: grouping is used, but ONLY WITHIN ONE CONSTRUCTION STAGE — substructure,
superstructure, roof. Items are never grouped ACROSS stages, because a 200 mm raft and
a 200 mm roof slab do not price alike and a range spanning them tells a tenderer nothing.
Grouping removes the individual thickness statement C2.1 cl.4, cl.5 and cl.6 require, so the
stated range is what carries that duty and it must be tight.

C3 Reinforcement
C3.1
     The weight of bar reinforcement shall be the net weight without addition for rolling
     margin, supports, spacers or tying wire.
Unit: KG — by weight, kilogrammes
W = Σ (N_bars × L_bar_INCLUDING_LAPS × m_per_m(Ø))

In practice. THE NET WEIGHT RULE, and read its exclusion list EXACTLY: no addition for
ROLLING MARGIN, SUPPORTS, SPACERS or TYING WIRE. LAPS ARE NOT IN THAT LIST.
A lap is steel fixed in position, so under GP3.1 it IS measured — and the contrast with C3.3,
which excludes laps from FABRIC in terms, proves the omission here is deliberate. WHAT
IS FORBIDDEN is a BLANKET PERCENTAGE UPLIFT with no derivation. HOUSE RULE ON
THE SOURCE: reinforcement is MEASURED FROM THE SECTION DRAWINGS, never from
a bar bending schedule. N_bars = (L_run / spacing) + 1 read off the section; each lap derived
from the SPECIFIED LAP LENGTH (k x diameter) at the positions the section shows. A BBS,
where one is later issued, is a CROSS-CHECK ONLY — reconcile and record the variance,
raise a technical query on a real difference, but do not adopt the schedule’s figure. Chairs,
spacers and tying wire remain excluded at all times.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                   220



C3.2
     Bar reinforcement shall be measured by weight, stating the diameter; bars of differ-
     ing diameters shall be given separately.
Unit: KG — by weight, kilogrammes
W = Σ N_bars × L_bar × m_per_m(Ø)
m_per_m = (π/4) × Ø² × 7850 / 1e6

In practice. Bar reinforcement, STATING THE DIAMETER. Differing diameters GIVEN SEP-
ARATELY — never a blended tonnage.

C3.3
     Fabric reinforcement shall be measured by area, without addition for laps.
Unit: M2 — by area, square metres
A = A_covered, NO addition for laps

In practice. Fabric reinforcement. A lap covers the same square metre twice.

C4 Shuttering
C4.1
     Unless otherwise stated, shuttering shall be measured by area, taken as the net
     area in contact with the finished face of concrete, classified as follows: 1. Soffits;
     shuttering to soffits of special construction shall be so described 2. Sloping soffits,
     which shall include soffits of staircases 3. Sloping upper surfaces, which shall in-
     clude surfaces more than 15° from horizontal 4. Sides of foundations, which shall
     include bases, pile caps and ground beams 5. Sides of walls, which shall include
     attached columns 6. Returns to walls, which shall include ends, projections and
     reveals of openings or recesses 7. Sides and soffits of beams, which shall include
     lintels and breaks in soffits; isolated beams shall be so described 8. Sides and soffits
     of sloping beams, which shall include lintels and breaks in soffits; isolated beams
     shall be so described 9. Sides of columns 10. Staircases, which shall include treads,
     risers and strings but exclude soffits 11. Other classifications (for example, tunnel
     linings, bridges, bridge abutments) as may be appropriate.
Unit: M2 — by area, square metres
A = Σ A_contact

In practice. Shuttering as the NET AREA IN CONTACT with the finished face of the concrete,
ELEVEN classes: 1 SOFFITS — soffits of special construction SO DESCRIBED · 2 SLOPING
SOFFITS, which INCLUDE SOFFITS OF STAIRCASES · 3 SLOPING UPPER SURFACES, which
are surfaces MORE THAN 15° FROM HORIZONTAL · 4 SIDES OF FOUNDATIONS, which IN-
CLUDE bases, pile caps and ground beams · 5 SIDES OF WALLS, which INCLUDE ATTACHED
COLUMNS · 6 RETURNS TO WALLS, which INCLUDE ends, projections and reveals of open-
ings or recesses · 7 SIDES AND SOFFITS OF BEAMS, which INCLUDE lintels and breaks in
soffits; ISOLATED BEAMS SO DESCRIBED — A = L × (2·h_exposed + b) · 8 SIDES AND SOF-
FITS OF SLOPING BEAMS, same inclusions, isolated so described · 9 SIDES OF COLUMNS
· 10 STAIRCASES, which INCLUDE treads, risers and strings BUT EXCLUDE SOFFITS — the
soffit is class 2 · 11 other classifications. The 15° line in class 3 and the staircase split between
2 and 10 are the two places shuttering is most often misclassified.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              221



C4.2
     Shuttering to edges, which shall include face of curb or upstand or break in up-
     per surface of floor, shall be measured by length; items of differing height may be
     grouped together, provided that the range of different heights is stated.
Unit: M — by length, metres
L = Σ L

In practice. Shuttering to EDGES — includes curb face, upstand, break in upper surface of
floor. Heights may be grouped if the RANGE is stated.

C4.3
     Grooves, which shall include throats, rebates, chamfers or the like, 2500 mm2 sec-
     tional area or over shall be measured by length; grooves less than 2500 mm2 sec-
     tional area shall be understood to be included.
Unit: M — by length, metres
if sectional area ≥ 2500 mm² → Len = Σ L
if sectional area <   2500 mm² → DEEMED INCLUDED

In practice. THE 2500 mm² THRESHOLD. Grooves — which INCLUDE throats, rebates and
CHAMFERS — of 2500 mm² SECTIONAL AREA OR OVER are measured by length; under that
they are DEEMED INCLUDED. COMPUTE THE SECTIONAL AREA FROM THE SHAPE, NOT
FROM THE LEG DIMENSIONS. A chamfer is a TRIANGLE: 50 x 50 mm legs give ½ × 50 ×
50 = 1250 mm², which is UNDER the threshold and therefore FREE. A chamfer only reaches
2500 mm² at about 71 x 71 mm legs. A rebate or a throat is rectangular, so 50 x 50 there
IS 2500 mm² and is measured. Reading the leg dimensions as the area bills a whole class of
chamfers POMI deems included.

In practice. Shuttering may be ENUMERATED where more appropriate — decorative fea-

D2 Walls and piers
D2.1
     Walls and piers shall be measured by area, classified as follows: 1. Walls; integral
     piers shall be measured as walls of combined pier and wall thickness 2. Walls built
     against other construction 3. Cavity walls measured as a composite item, including
     skins and cavity; alternatively, the skins and cavity may each be measured by area.
     Closing cavity walls at ends or around openings shall be understood to be included
     4. Isolated piers.
Unit: M2 — by area, square metres
A = Σ (L × H) − voids per GP3.2/GP3.3

In practice. Walls and piers, FOUR classes. cl.1 INTEGRAL PIERS measured as WALLS at the
COMBINED pier+wall thickness. cl.2 walls built against other construction, SO DESCRIBED.
cl.3 CAVITY WALLS — POMI permits EITHER one composite item including skins and cavity,
OR the skins and cavity EACH measured by area. HOUSE DEFAULT: THE COMPOSITE ITEM,
one area at one description carrying the whole build-up, because it prices as one operation.
State it in the preambles. What is wrong is MIXING the two methods in one bill. CLOSING
CAVITY WALLS at ends and around openings is DEEMED INCLUDED under either method.
cl.4 isolated piers.

D2.2
     Faced or fair faced work shall each be so described; alternatively, it may be mea-
     sured as extra over walls, stating whether faced or fair faced on one or both sides
     (that is, the area of faced or fair faced work shall be measured but no deduction shall
     be made from the area of walling on which the faced or fair faced work occurs).
Unit: M2 — by area, square metres
A_wall = FULL area, UNCHANGED
A_faced = measured AS WELL

In practice. Faced or fair faced work: POMI permits EITHER each SO DESCRIBED as its
own wall item, OR measured as EXTRA OVER walls. HOUSE DEFAULT: EXTRA OVER — the
wall area stays whole and the faced area is measured AS WELL, STATING WHETHER ONE
SIDE OR BOTH. NO DEDUCTION is made from the walling on which the faced work occurs;
deducting it loses the base item, which is the same error as B8.5 rock, B15.2 rock boring and
G2.3 special sheets. ‘One side or both’ is a MANDATORY STATEMENT — fair faced both sides
is twice the work at the same wall area.

D3 Sills, etc.
D3.1
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                             226



     Sills, copings, oversailing or receding courses or the like shall be measured by
     length.

L = Σ L

In practice. Sills, copings, oversailing or receding courses.

D3.2
     Arches shall be measured by length.
Unit: M — by length, metres
Len = Σ L

In practice. Arches BY LENGTH. THAT IS THE WHOLE CLAUSE — POMI states no basis
along which the length is taken. HOUSE EXTENSION under GP1.1, declared: the length is
taken on the MEAN GIRTH, L = π × (R_intrados + t/2) × (θ/180) for a curved arch, because the
mean girth is the line the work actually follows and both the span and the intrados understate
it. This is the HOUSE’s basis, not POMI’s, and it is recorded in the Appendix under GP1.2.
GP5.2 separately requires the cross-sectional size or girth to be STATED in the description.

SECTION E — METALWORK
3 groups · 11 clauses · 8 carrying arithmetic

E1 Generally
E1.1
     The weight of metalwork shall be the net weight, without addition for rolling margin
     or welding material and without deduction for holes, splay cuts, notches or the like.
Unit: KG — by weight, kilogrammes
W = Σ (N × L_gross × m_per_m(section))

In practice. THE NET WEIGHT RULE, and it cuts BOTH ways. NO ADDITION for rolling
margin or welding material — a fabricator’s own tonnage adds both, because that is what
he buys and consumes, and both are RATE matters under GP4.1. NO DEDUCTION for holes,
splay cuts, notches or the like — a careful measurer deducts them because they are visibly
not steel, and POMI forbids that too. The two errors pull in opposite directions and partially
cancel, so a wrong figure can foot to about the right total, which is exactly why neither gets
caught. It is the GROSS SECTION over the GROSS LENGTH: a beam notched at both ends
and drilled for twelve bolts is still its full length at its full unit mass.

E1.2
     Welded, riveted or bolted work shall each be so described.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Welded, riveted or bolted work EACH SO DESCRIBED.

E2 Structural metalwork
E2.1
     Unless otherwise stated, structural metalwork shall be measured by weight, clas-
     sified as follows: 1. Grillages 2. Beams 3. Stanchions 4. Portal frames, stating
     the number 5. Roof trusses, stating the number 6. Support steelwork, which shall
     include sheeting rails, braces, struts or the like 7. Other classifications, as may be
     appropriate.
Unit: KG — by weight, kilogrammes
W = Σ N × L × m_per_m, per class

In practice. Structural metalwork by WEIGHT, SEVEN classes: 1 GRILLAGES · 2 BEAMS · 3
STANCHIONS · 4 PORTAL FRAMES, STATING THE NUMBER · 5 ROOF TRUSSES, STATING
THE NUMBER · 6 SUPPORT STEELWORK, which INCLUDES sheeting rails, braces, struts or
the like · 7 other classifications. Classes 4 and 5 carry a mandatory NUMBER as well as the
weight.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                228



E2.2

Unit: ITEM — an ITEM — a lump, not a measured quantity
In practice. Fittings — caps, brackets. An ITEM, not weight.

E2.3
     Fixings (for example, bolts, distance pieces, rivets) shall be given as an item.
Unit: ITEM — an ITEM — a lump, not a measured quantity
In practice. Fixings — bolts, distance pieces, rivets. An ITEM, not weight.

E2.4
     Wedging and grouting bases or the like shall be enumerated.
Unit: NR — enumerated — a count
N = count

In practice. Wedging and grouting bases.

E2.5
     Holding down bolts or the like shall be enumerated; temporary boxes and grouting
     shall be understood to be included.
Unit: NR — enumerated — a count
N = count

In practice.     Holding-down bolts.       TEMPORARY BOXES AND GROUTING DEEMED IN-
CLUDED.

E2.6
     Protective treatment shall be given as an item.
Unit: M2 — by area, square metres
A = Σ A_treated_surface

In practice. Protective treatment. POMI SAYS AN ITEM. HOUSE AMENDMENT, DECLARED
UNDER GP1.2 AND RECORDED IN POMI’S APPENDIX: it is MEASURED BY AREA. The
treated surface is the cost driver — a galvanising or intumescent system prices per square
metre, and the surface area of a tonne of steel varies several-fold between a heavy stanchion
and a light truss. An item forces the tenderer to compute that area himself and price a risk he
cannot see, and it cannot be valued on variation. The AREA is measured; the SYSTEM stays
in the description. Surface area is the developed girth of the section times its length, plus the
area of any plates and cleats.

E3 Non-structural metalwork
E3.1
     Floor plates, duct covers, sheet metal coverings and linings or the like shall be mea-
     sured by area.
Unit: M2 — by area, square metres
A = Σ A

In practice. Floor plates, duct covers, sheet coverings and linings.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                229



E3.2
       Bearers, balustrades, handrails (except where included with a staircase), frames or
       the like shall be measured by length.
Unit: M — by length, metres
Len = Σ L

In practice. Bearers, balustrades, handrails, frames BY LENGTH. POMI’s exception reads
‘except where included with a staircase’. HOUSE ELECTION: THE HANDRAIL IS A SEPARATE
LENGTH ITEM and the enumerated staircase under E3.3 is DESCRIBED AS EXCLUDING IT.
This is within the clause — the handrail is only inside the staircase where the bill puts it there
— and it prices the two properly, because a balustrade is a different trade and a different rate
from the stair. THE STAIRCASE DESCRIPTION MUST SAY ‘excluding handrail’, or the two
readings collide and the handrail is billed twice or not at all.

E3.3
       Matwell frames, cat ladders, gates, staircases or the like shall be enumerated.
Unit: NR — enumerated — a count
N = count

In practice. Matwell frames, cat ladders, gates and STAIRCASES ENUMERATED — never
weighed, never measured by rise. GP5.1 governs: there is no dimension carrying information,
so the words carry all of it. Under the house election at E3.2 the staircase is DESCRIBED AS
EXCLUDING THE HANDRAIL, which is measured separately by length.


SECTION F — WOODWORK
10 groups · 22 clauses · 17 carrying arithmetic

F1 Generally
F1.1
       Timber which is sawn (that is, not milled) and timber which is finished (that is,
       milled) shall each be so described.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. SAWN (not milled) and FINISHED (milled) timber EACH SO DESCRIBED.

F1.2
       Descriptions of timber members shall state whether the sizes are basic (that is, be-
       fore machining) or finished (that is, milled, within permitted deviations).
Unit: RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
In practice. Descriptions SHALL STATE whether sizes are BASIC (before machining) or
FINISHED (milled, within permitted deviations). HOUSE RULE: FOLLOW THE PROJECT DE-
SCRIPTION — take whichever basis the specification and drawings use and state it; do not
convert one to the other and do not assume a house default. The statement is mandatory, its
VALUE comes from the source documents. This matters commercially: a ‘50 x 200’ quoted BA-
SIC finishes at about 45 x 195 after machining — same words, different timber, different price.
An F item with no basic/finished statement is incomplete under GP5, and it is the most-missed
mandatory statement in the section because the size looks complete on its own.

       Work shall be measured flat without addition for laps or seams; finishes on corru-
       gated or ornamental surfaces shall each be so described.
Unit: RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
A = A_covered, NO laps or seams

In practice. Measured FLAT. Corrugated and ornamental surfaces EACH SO DESCRIBED.

J1.2
       Curved, spherical and conical work shall each be so described.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Curved, spherical and conical EACH SO DESCRIBED.

J1.3
       Internal and external work shall each be so described.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Internal and external work EACH SO DESCRIBED.

J2 Backgrounds
J2.1
       Backgrounds shall be measured by area; backgrounds for floor, wall or ceiling fin-
       ishes shall each be so described.
Unit: M2 — by area, square metres
A = Σ A

In practice. Backgrounds BY AREA, with floor, wall and ceiling backgrounds EACH SO DE-
SCRIBED. HOUSE RULE: A BACKGROUND IS ALWAYS MEASURED SEPARATELY FROM
THE FINISH ON IT. A screed under a tile is J2.2 and the tile is J3.1 cl.1 — TWO measured
areas over the same surface, which is not a double count because they are two operations.
The common error is the reverse: billing only the finish and letting the background disappear
into its rate, where it cannot be valued on variation.

J2.2
       Poured backgrounds (for example, screeds) shall each be given separately, stating
       the surface finish.
Unit: M2 — by area, square metres
A = Σ A
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                  239



In practice. POURED backgrounds (screeds) each given separately, STATING THE SURFACE
FINISH.

J2.3
       Pre-formed backgrounds (for example, plasterboard, expanded metal lathing) shall
       each be given separately.
Unit: M2 — by area, square metres
A = Σ A

In practice. PRE-FORMED backgrounds (plasterboard, EML) each given separately.

J3 Finishings
J3.1
       Unless otherwise stated, finishing shall be measured by area, classified as follows:
       1. Floors, which shall include landings 2. Walls, which shall include returns, reveals
       of openings or recesses and attached and unattached columns 3. Ceilings, which
       shall include attached and unattached beams and soffits of staircases 4. Staircases,
       which shall include treads, risers and edges of landings but exclude soffits.
Unit: M2 — by area, square metres
A = Σ (L × H) − voids + reveals + columns

In practice. Finishings, FOUR classes: 1 floors (incl. landings) · 2 walls, INCLUDING returns,
reveals of openings or recesses and ATTACHED AND UNATTACHED COLUMNS · 3 ceilings,
INCLUDING attached and unattached beams and soffits of staircases · 4 STAIRCASES, includ-
ing treads, risers and edges of landings BUT EXCLUDING SOFFITS (those fall in cl.3).

J3.2
       Skirtings, bands, strings, coverings to kerbs, mouldings, coves, channels or the like
       shall be measured by length.
Unit: M — by length, metres
L = Σ L

In practice. Skirtings, bands, strings, coverings to kerbs, mouldings, coves, channels.

J4 Sundries
J4.1
       Non-slip inserts, dividing strips, metal angle beads, lathing at junction of differing
       backgrounds or the like shall be measured by length; alternatively, they may be
       described with the items in which they occur.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Non-slip inserts, dividing strips, metal angle beads and lathing at junctions of dif-
fering backgrounds. POMI permits LENGTH or, expressly, DESCRIPTION WITH THE ITEMS
IN WHICH THEY OCCUR. HOUSE ELECTION: DESCRIBED WITH THE ITEM — no separate
linear item is raised, matching the F6.6 treatment of plastic coverings. THE TWO LIMBS ARE
MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE: a bill carrying an angle-bead length AND a finish description that
mentions angle beads has billed them twice, and the second row reads perfectly reasonably.
So the finish description must NAME them — beads, stops, dividing strips, lathing at junctions
— or the rate is not bound to anything.

sub-frames of a differing material; EDGES OF SASHES DEEMED INCLUDED · 9 RADIATORS,

SECTION K — ACCESSORIES
2 groups · 5 clauses · 4 carrying arithmetic

K1 Generally
K1.1
       For the purposes of identification, accessories to be measured in accordance with
       the principles in this section shall be defined as those being specially manufactured
       or proprietary items not included in other sections.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. THE DEFINITION, and it is a RESIDUAL: accessories are specially manufactured
or proprietary items NOT INCLUDED IN OTHER SECTIONS. SO K IS TESTED LAST — an item
reaches K only after Q, R, H, J and every other section has been tested and none of them takes
it. Reaching for K early pulls work out of the sections that price it properly. HOUSE RULE:
BECAUSE THE SECTION IS DEFINED BY EXCLUSION, EVERY K ITEM MUST BE FULLY
DESCRIBED — what the thing is, what it is made of, how it is fixed, and the schedule or type
reference it comes from. A section defined by what it is not cannot rely on its heading to say
what an item is; only the description can.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                  242



K1.2
       Unless otherwise stated, accessories shall be enumerated.
Unit: NR — enumerated — a count
N = count

In practice. Unless otherwise stated, accessories ENUMERATED — the section’s default, and
‘unless otherwise stated’ is the licence for K2.1’s length. Everything not caught by K2 falls to
this count, FULLY DESCRIBED under GP5.1 and under the K1.1 house rule: the description
is the only thing identifying an item in a section defined by exclusion.

K2 Partitions
K2.1
       Partitions shall be measured by length, taken over all doors and glazed units.
Unit: M — by length, metres
L = Σ L, TAKEN OVER ALL doors and glazed units

In practice. Partitions. NO deduction for the doors and glazed panels in them.

K2.2
       Doors and glazed units shall be enumerated, stating the partition in which they
       occur.
Unit: NR — enumerated — a count
N = count

In practice. Doors and glazed units, STATING THE PARTITION they occur in.

K2.3
       Cubicles or the like shall be enumerated.
Unit: NR — enumerated — a count
N = count

In practice. Cubicles.


SECTION L — EQUIPMENT
1 groups · 2 clauses · 1 carrying arithmetic

L1 Generally
L1.1
       For the purposes of identification, equipment to be measured in accordance with
       the principles in this section shall be defined as specialist equipment related solely
       to the function of a building or department (for example, food preparation or service
       equipment, laboratory equipment, stage equipment).
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Scope: equipment is specially manufactured or proprietary items not in other
sections — food service, laboratory, stage.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                    243



L1.2
       Each category of equipment shall be given as an item; alternatively, individual items
       of equipment may be enumerated.
Unit: NR — enumerated — a count
N = count

In practice. POMI permits EACH CATEGORY AS AN ITEM or, expressly, INDIVIDUAL
ITEMS ENUMERATED. HOUSE ELECTION: ENUMERATED. An ‘Item’ for laboratory or
kitchen equipment prices nothing, compares between tenderers on nothing, and cannot
be valued on variation. GP5.5 sits over this section — a proprietary item MAY follow the
manufacturer’s tariff — so between L1.2 and GP5.5 Section L is the loosest in POMI and the
DESCRIPTION carries everything.


SECTION M — FURNISHINGS
2 groups · 3 clauses · 2 carrying arithmetic

M1 Generally
M1.1
       For the purposes of identification, furnishings to be measured in accordance with
       the principles in this section shall be defined as loose furniture, fittings or the like
       related to the occupation and use of a building or department (for example, rugs,
       curtains, artwork, ashtrays, furnishing accessories).
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
In practice. Scope: furnishings — rugs, curtains, artwork, ashtrays, furnishing accessories.

M1.2

       of furnishing may be enumerated or measured by length, as may be appropriate.
Unit: NR / M
N = count for discrete items
Len = Σ L for continuous ones

In practice. POMI permits EACH CATEGORY AS AN ITEM, or individual items ENUMER-
ATED, or MEASURED BY LENGTH — three units in one clause, the most permissive in the
standard. HOUSE ELECTION: ENUMERATED for discrete items, BY LENGTH for continuous
ones (curtains, blinds). CATEGORY AS AN ITEM IS NEVER USED, for the same reason as
L1.2.

N2 Enclosures

       enclosure construction, shall be measured in accordance with the relevant sections

Unit: NR — enumerated — a count
N = count

In practice. Enclosures. Work WITHIN the enclosure that is not part of the enclosure con-

N3 Installations
N3.1
       Installations shall each be given as an item; alternatively, they may be measured in
       accordance with the relevant sections of this document.
Unit: — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
measured to the RELEVANT SECTIONS

In practice. Installations of a specialist nature. POMI permits AN ITEM EACH or, expressly,
MEASUREMENT TO THE RELEVANT SECTIONS. HOUSE ELECTION: MEASURED TO THE
RELEVANT SECTIONS — it prices against known work rather than a lump. BUT THE SPE-
CIALIST NATURE MUST SURVIVE IN THE WORDING: an item measured under C, F or J
that forms part of a specialist installation is DESCRIBED AS SUCH, naming the installation
it belongs to and the specification clause that governs it. Radiation shielding measured as
lead-lined boarding under F is priced as ordinary boarding unless the description says what
it is. THE MEASUREMENT MOVES SECTION; THE SPECIFICATION DOES NOT.

P3 Work incidental to conveying systems
P3.1
       An item shall be given for incidental work, which shall include: 1. Co-ordination
       with other engineering installations 2. Cutting or forming holes, mortices, chases
       or the like and making good finishings 3. Building in or cutting and pinning brackets
       or the like and making good finishings.
Unit: ITEM — an ITEM — a lump, not a measured quantity
ITEM

In practice. Incidental work AS AN ITEM, three heads: 1 CO-ORDINATION with other en-
gineering installations · 2 CUTTING OR FORMING holes, mortices and chases AND MAKING
GOOD FINISHINGS · 3 BUILDING IN, or cutting and pinning brackets, AND MAKING GOOD
FINISHINGS. BUILDER’S WORK IS AN ITEM, NOT A COUNT — no enumeration of holes, no
area of making good. Heads 2 and 3 BOTH end ‘and making good finishings’, so the make-good
is inside this item and MUST NOT reappear in Section J.

P3.2
       Protective painting and decorative painting shall each be given as an item for each
       system and shall include: 1. Removing protective coating or wrapping 2. Cleaning
       and polishing exposed surfaces.
Unit: ITEM — an ITEM — a lump, not a measured quantity
ITEM per system

In practice. Protective and decorative painting, AN ITEM FOR EACH SYSTEM, and it IN-
CLUDES 1 removing protective coating or wrapping · 2 cleaning and polishing exposed sur-
faces — both PREPARATION, not painting. HOUSE ELECTION: MEP PAINTING IS BILLED
IN THE MEP SECTIONS, HERE, AND NOT IN SECTION J. J6.3 cl.11 (large pipes and trunk-
ing) and cl.12 (structural metalwork) both carry the qualifier ‘unless measured as incidental
work’ — under this election it IS incidental work, so those two J6.3 classes are NOT used for
anything inside an MEP package. Billing both double-pays, and both rows read correctly.

P3.3
       Other incidental work shall be measured in accordance with the relevant sections
       of this document and grouped under an appropriate heading.

Q3 Ductwork
Q3.1
     Rectangular ductwork shall be measured by weight, based upon the area calculated
     as the length, taken along the centre line over all fittings, times the net girth of
     nominal dimensions. Blank ends shall be added to the area for weighting but no
     deduction shall be made for intersections or openings; extra weight for seams, stiff-
     eners, supports, fixings or the like shall be understood to be included.
Unit: KG — by weight, kilogrammes
girth = 2 × (w + d)
A = L_centreline × girth + Σ A_blank_ends
W = A × m_per_m2(gauge)

In practice. RECTANGULAR ductwork BY WEIGHT, from an area built on NOMINAL dimen-
sions. BLANK ENDS ARE ADDED to the area. NO DEDUCTION for intersections or open-
ings. EXTRA WEIGHT FOR SEAMS, STIFFENERS, SUPPORTS AND FIXINGS IS DEEMED
INCLUDED — so the gauge weight is applied flat, with no uplift.

Q3.2
     Circular, oval and flexible ductwork shall be measured by length, taken along the
     centre line over all fittings.
Unit: M — by length, metres
L = Σ L_centreline, over all fittings

In practice. Circular, oval and flexible ductwork BY LENGTH.

rectangular fittings DEEMED INCLUDED

In practice. POMI permits automatic controls to be MEASURED (Q5.1 device by device) or,
expressly, GIVEN AS AN ITEM FOR EACH INSTALLATION. HOUSE ELECTION: AN ITEM
PER INSTALLATION. BUT THE CLAUSE’S OWN EXCEPTION SURVIVES THE ELECTION
AND IS NOT OPTIONAL: EQUIPMENT COMMON TO MORE THAN ONE SYSTEM IS STILL
ENUMERATED. So a BMS is one item per installation, while a shared control panel, a shared
air compressor or a shared receiver serving two or more systems is counted separately —
otherwise it sits inside one installation’s item and the other installations are priced without it.
Q5.2 still applies: wiring, pneumatic tubing, isolators, starters and relays associated with the
controls are DEEMED INCLUDED and are never measured as cable under Section R.

Q6 Connections to supply mains

GP8.1 sum, exclusive of profit
+ profit ITEM
+ attendance ITEM per GP8.2

In practice. Connections to supply mains ENUMERATED, SUBJECT TO GP8. HOUSE ELEC-
TION: WHERE THE AUTHORITY HOLDS THE MONOPOLY — which in the UAE is every
potable water, sewer and district-cooling connection — GP8 GOVERNS AND IT IS NOT A
MEASURED CONNECTION AT ALL. It becomes a GP8.1 SUM EXCLUSIVE OF PROFIT, a
SEPARATE PROFIT ITEM, and an ATTENDANCE ITEM under GP8.2 carrying the eight GP6.2
heads. Three lines, never one. Only where the contractor may lawfully make the connection
himself is it enumerated under this clause.

R3.2

N = count of sub-main circuits, separately identified

In practice. Cable and conduit to individual SUB-MAIN circuits ENUMERATED and SEPA-
RATELY IDENTIFIED; POMI’s express alternative permits them to be measured by length per
R2. HOUSE ELECTION: ENUMERATED PER CIRCUIT, separately identified — a sub-main is
a discrete run between two discrete boards, and identifying it by its boards makes it check-
able against the single-line diagram. THE TIER IS DECIDED BY WHICH BOARDS THE CABLE
RUNS BETWEEN, not by its size or route: incoming supply to the main DB is R2 (by length),
main DB to a sub-main DB is R3, and anything onward to a termination point is R4 (as points).

R4 Final sub-circuits and auxiliary installations
R4.1
     Cable and conduit to termination points shall be enumerated, classified as follows:
     1. Lighting points 2. Lighting switch points, stating whether one-way, two-way or
     intermediate 3. General purpose socket outlets; multi-gang socket outlets or the
     like shall count as one point 4. Equipment points, stating type of equipment or the
     electrical rating; contactors, starters or the like shall be measured separately as
     equipment points 5. Auxiliary installation points (for example, bell push, telephone
     outlet).
Unit: NR — enumerated — a count
N = Σ points, per class

In practice. CABLE AND CONDUIT to termination points ENUMERATED AS POINTS —
and read that literally: the point carries THE CABLE AND THE CONDUIT, and by R1.4 ‘con-
duit’ also means TRUNKING, CABLE TRAY and DUCTING. IT DOES NOT CARRY THE AC-
CESSORY: ceiling roses, switches, socket outlets and bell pushes are separately enumerated
under R5.1, and both are billed at each position. FIVE classes: 1 lighting points · 2 lighting
switch points, STATING one-way, two-way or intermediate · 3 general purpose socket out-
lets — A MULTI-GANG OUTLET COUNTS AS ONE POINT · 4 equipment points, STATING
type of equipment or electrical rating; CONTACTORS AND STARTERS ARE MEASURED SEP-
ARATELY AS EQUIPMENT POINTS · 5 AUXILIARY INSTALLATION POINTS, e.g. bell push,
telephone outlet. Where a circuit is enumerated as a point, DO NOT ALSO MEASURE ITS
CABLE OR CONTAINMENT BY LENGTH — that is the double count.

for the same final circuit, which remains forbidden.

MEASUREMENT FORMULAE — HOW EVERY QUANTITY IS
CALCULATED
skills/pomi-take-off/references/measurement-formulae.md · 1,658 lines

Binding on every measuring seat. POMI tells you what to measure, in what unit, and
what the rate is deemed to include. It does not give you the arithmetic. This file does —
one formula per measurable item, every symbol defined, every deduction rule stated, and a
worked example with real numbers.

How to read this file

[C4.1]                                             the POMI clause the rule comes from. Open
                                                   it in pomi-verbatim.md before relying on it
HOUSE                                              POMI is silent; this is a house convention. It
                                                   is a GP1.1 build-up — “more detailed
                                                   information than is required by this
                                                   document” — and it is declared, not
                                                   smuggled
⚠                                                  the place this item is most often measured
                                                   wrong, and what the error costs


Every formula below produces a NET quantity as fixed in position [GP3.1]. None of them
adds waste, laps, rolling margin, working space or bulking. Those live in the rate, and a
take-off that adds them has billed the same thing twice.



PART 0 — THE RULES THAT GOVERN EVERY SECTION
0.1 Rounding — the 10 mm rule [GP3.1]
     Work shall be measured net as fixed in position and each measurement shall be taken
     to the nearest 10 millimetres; this principle shall not apply to dimensions stated in
     descriptions.
d_measured = round(d_drawn / 0.01) × 0.01          d in metres, so 2 decimal places

Round each dimension as it is taken, not the product. 4.237 × 2.981 is taken as 4.24 × 2.98,
not as 12.630… rounded afterwards.
⚠ The exemption matters. A dimension stated in a description is not rounded — a “150 mm
thick” slab stays 150 mm in the words even though its measured length is rounded. Round
the description and you have changed the specification.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                                              255



0.2 Deductions — the 1.00 m² rule, and its exception [GP3.2] [GP3.3]
       Unless otherwise stated, no deduction shall be made from items required to be mea-
       sured by area for voids of less than 1.00 m².
       Minimum deductions of voids shall refer only to voids WITHIN the edges of mea-
       sured areas; voids which are AT THE EDGES of measured areas shall always be
       deducted, irrespective of size.
A_net = A_gross − Σ A_void(i)                          for every void where   A_void(i) ≥ 1.00 m²   OR    void touches an edge

The test is two-part and both parts must be applied:

Void                                            Area                      Touches an edge?               Deduct?
door opening in the                             1.89 m²                   no                             yes — ≥ 1.00
middle of a wall
small vent in the                               0.36 m²                   no                             no — < 1.00 and
middle of a wall                                                                                         interior
same 0.36 m² vent,                              0.36 m²                   yes                            yes — edge voids
but at the wall’s end                                                                                    always go
stair void in a slab,                           4.20 m²                   yes                            yes
running to the wall


⚠ The edge rule is the one that gets missed. A 0.6 m² opening in the middle of a wall is
not deducted; the same opening at the wall’s end is. The reason is physical: an interior void
leaves the surrounding work continuous and the labour is barely changed, but an edge void
removes an edge and changes the work at it.
Volume has its own threshold [C1.3] — 1.00 m³ for concrete, not 1.00 m². They are different
numbers for different units and they are not interchangeable.

0.3 Timesing and squaring — the dimension-paper convention HOUSE
Every quantity on the measurement sheet is N × L × W × H, recorded in separate columns so
that each factor is auditable on its own:
Qty    =       N    ×     L       ×    W    ×   H
               │          │             │        └── Height / thickness / depth    (m)
               │          │             └──────── Width                            (m)
               │          └────────────── Length                                   (m)
               └──────────────────── Number of times (timesing)                    (dimensionless, an integer)

      • Area items leave H empty: A = N × L × W
      • Linear items leave W and H empty: Len = N × L
      • Enumerated items carry only N
      • Weight items carry the geometry AND the unit mass — see §0.4
⚠ Timesing is a COUNT, never a factor. N = 4 means “four identical bays”. It never means
“×1.05 for waste” or “×2 because it is two-sided”. A two-sided item is measured twice, in two
rows, each citing its own face — because a reviewer must be able to see which face each row
is.

0.4 Weight [GP5.4]
W_kg    =       V_m3       ×       ρ                 where ρ is the material density, kg/m³
W_kg       =       L_m        ×       m_per_m        where m_per_m is the mass per metre, kg/m
W_kg       =       A_m2       ×       m_per_m2      where m_per_m2 is the mass per square metre, kg/m²

The description must state the material thickness and unit weight where relevant [GP5.4].
Take ρ and m_per_m from the project specification or the manufacturer’s data — never from
memory — and record the source on the measurement row.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                   256



0.5 The three quantities that are NEVER added

Never add                            Because                             Clause
working space and bulking            quantity is the bulk before         [B8.2]
on excavation                        excavation
rolling margin, supports,            the weight is the net weight        [C3.1]
spacers, tying wire on rebar
laps on fabric reinforcement,        measured flat, without              [C3.3] [G1.1] [J1.1]
on roofing, on finishes              addition for laps or seams


Each of these is a real cost and each belongs in the rate, under GP4.1 — “all items shall be
fully inclusive of all that is necessary to fulfil the liabilities and obligations arising out of the
contract”. A take-off that adds them has billed the same money twice: once in the quantity
and once in the rate.



PART 1 — SECTION B · SITE WORK
B1 Site exploration [B1.1–B1.3]
All three are ITEM — no arithmetic. Records, samples/tests/analyses, reports.

B2 Trial holes [B2.1]
Unit: DEPTH (m), along the centre line. State the number and the maximum depth
below commencing level.
Depth_total = Σ   d(i)            over every trial hole i
N           = count of holes                  ← stated, not multiplied
d_max       = max d(i)                        ← stated

⚠ Depth is measured from the commencing level, which is the level the excavator starts
from — not from finished floor level and not from datum. Getting the commencing level wrong
shifts every hole by the same amount and is invisible in the total.

B3 Boreholes [B3.1–B3.3]
Same shape as B2. Cappings enumerated [B3.3].

B4 Site preparation [B4.1–B4.2]
Clearance (m²)        = L_site × W_site   −    Σ (areas not within the clearance scope)
Tree removal (nr)     = count, by girth band


B5 Demolitions and alterations [B5.1–B5.5]
Demolition of a whole structure is ITEM. Cutting openings and alterations are each ITEM,
stating what they are.

B6 Shoring [B6.1–B6.2]
ITEM. Incidental shoring to demolitions is one item; other shoring is a separate item stating
the type and the construction supported.

B7 Underpinning [B7.1–B7.5]
Length (m) = Σ L(i)      over each length of underpinning                         [B7.1]

The work within it — concrete, masonry, formwork — is measured in accordance with the
appropriate sections [B7.2]. Excavation is the exception: B7.4 gives it its own rule.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                257



B7.4 — underpinning excavation [B7.4]
V = L × W × D             W taken to the OUTSIDE LINE of the PROJECTING FOUNDATION,
                          or to the outside line of the NEW foundation,
                          WHICHEVER IS THE GREATER


#                                    Class
1                                    Excavation in preliminary
                                     trenches DOWN TO the
                                     base of the existing
                                     foundations
2                                    Excavation BELOW the base
                                     of the existing foundations


⚠ The width is not the new foundation’s width. It is measured to whichever projects
further — the existing footing’s toe or the new work. Taking the new foundation width alone
under-measures every bay where the existing footing projects, which is most of them.
⚠ The two classes are priced very differently — working above the existing footing is open
trench, working below it is hand excavation in short lengths under a load. One combined item
loses that distinction and will be disputed.

B8–B9 EARTHWORKS AND EXCAVATION — the section with the most money in it
The bulk-before-excavation rule [B8.2]
        The quantities for excavation shall be understood to be the bulk BEFORE excavation,
        and no allowance shall be made for any working space or subsequent variation in
        bulk; existing voids shall be deducted.
V_exc    =   V_void_to_be_occupied            ← the designed void, nothing more
         −   Σ V_existing_voids                ← cellars, old tanks, existing basements

Three things this rule forbids, each of them a common over-measure:

Do NOT add                           Typical wrong uplift                 On a 1,000 m³ dig
working space beyond the             0.60 m all round                     +340 m³, +34%
permanent construction
bulking of excavated                 ×1.25                                +250 m³, +25%
material
battering / side slopes not in       1:1 to 3.00 m                        +180 m³
the design


All three are real contractor costs. All three go in the rate, not the quantity.

B9.1 Excavation — by VOLUME [B9.1]
        Excavation shall be measured by volume as the void which is to be occupied by the
        permanent construction, or vertically above any part of the permanent construction.
V = N × L × W × D

where L, W are the plan dimensions of the permanent construction (not of the dig), and D
is measured from the commencing level to the underside of the construction.
The seven classifications [B9.1], each given separately:
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                      258

1                          Oversite, to remove          A_site × d_avg              state the average
                           topsoil                                                  depth

                                                        method below
4                          Basement                     L × W × D
5                          Trench to receive            L_trench × W_trench × D     includes pile caps

                                                                                    those separately

End-area method for cuttings and irregular ground HOUSE — POMI gives the unit, not
the technique:
V = Σ    ( (A(i) + A(i+1)) / 2 ) × c               simple end-area, chainage interval c


V = (c/3) × [ A(0) + 4(A1+A3+…) + 2(A2+A4+…) + A(n) ]             Simpson, n even, more accurate

Record which method was used on the measurement row. The two differ by a few percent on
curved ground and a reviewer must know which is in front of him.

B9.2 Service and drain trenches — by LENGTH [B9.2]
Len = Σ L(i)       along the centre line
d_avg = ( Σ (L(i) × d(i)) ) / Σ L(i)               ← state this

⚠ Disposal and filling are DEEMED INCLUDED [B9.2]. Measure the trench by length and
stop. Adding separate disposal and filling rows for a service trench double-counts them.

B8.5 Rock — EXTRA OVER [B8.5]
        the volume of rock shall be measured but no deduction shall be made from the
        volume of excavation in which the rock occurs
V_excavation = full designed volume               ← unchanged, rock included
V_rock         = the rock volume                  ← measured AS WELL, not INSTEAD

⚠ This is the classic extra-over error. The rock is billed on top of the excavation, so the
excavation quantity is not reduced. Deduct it and you have paid for the rock but lost the dig
it sits in.

B11 Disposal — by VOLUME [B11.1]
        Disposal … shall be measured by volume as EQUAL TO the volume of excavation.
V_disposal_total = V_excavation                         ← identically equal, always
V_backfilled       = V_excavation − V_permanent         ← what goes back in
V_removed          = V_excavation − V_backfilled        ← what leaves site

Four classifications [B11.1]: backfilled into excavation · backfilled making up levels · backfilled
oversite (giving details of contouring) · removed, which shall include providing a suitable
tip.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                                 259



⚠ V_disposal_total must reconcile to V_excavation exactly. If it does not, either the excavation
or the disposal is wrong. This is a gate, not a guideline.

B12 Filling — by VOLUME [B12.1]
     Filling material (OTHER THAN that arising from excavation…) shall be measured
     by volume as equal to the VOID TO BE FILLED.
V_fill = V_void_to_be_filled              ← the compacted void, not the loose delivered volume

Three classifications: filled into excavation · filled making up levels · filled oversite.
⚠ Imported fill only. Material arising from the site’s own excavation is billed under B11 as
backfilled, not here. Measure it in both and you have paid twice for the same soil.

Heads and shoes = enumerated
Cutting off / lengthening connections = enumerated

⚠ Supply length ≠ driving length. Supply is the pile as delivered; driving is only the travel
from pitched to driven. They are different numbers and POMI asks for both.

Corner piles (m) · Cutting (m)

⚠ Strutting, waling and withdrawing are DEEMED INCLUDED in driving [B16.4]. Three
