B24.1 — tunnel and shaft excavation [B24.1]
V = the void TO BE OCCUPIED, INCLUDING THE VOLUME OF THE PERMANENT LINING
    grouped as appropriate to identify different lengths

⚠ The lining volume is INSIDE the excavation quantity, not deducted from it. The
excavation is the whole bored void; the lining is then measured again as lining under [B25.1].
That is not a double count — one is the dig, the other is the concrete — but netting the lining
out of the excavation is a real under-measure.
Seven classes, and the last one is the one that is missed:

#                    Class                                      #                       Class
1                    Straight tunnels                           5                       Tapered tunnels
2                    Straight shafts                            6                       Tapered shafts
3                    Curved tunnels                             7                       Other cavities,
                                                                                        which include
                                                                                        transitions,
                                                                                        breakaways
                                                                                        and
                                                                                        intersections
                                                                                        between shafts
                                                                                        and tunnels
4                    Curved shafts


⚠ Class 7 carries the junctions. A tunnel-to-shaft intersection is not part of either the tunnel
or the shaft — it is its own class, and it is the most expensive cubic metre on the job. A take-off
with six classes has billed the junctions at plain tunnel rates.
Tunnel linings [B25.1] are then measured by area, stating whether spray or cast concrete,
in two classes — the primary lining and the secondary lining. (The RICS text prints class
1 as a bare “lining”; the qualifying word is lost in the source. Read against class 2 it is the
primary lining, and pomi-verbatim.md preserves the defect as printed.)

PART 2 — SECTION C · CONCRETE WORK
2.1 The deduction rule for concrete [C1.3]
     No deduction shall be made for voids less than 1.00 m³, nor for the volume of any re-
     inforcement or structural metal enclosed in the concrete, EXCEPT that voids caused
     by boxed or tubular structural metalwork shall ALWAYS be deducted.
V_net = V_gross
      − Σ V_void(i)           for voids ≥ 1.00 m³
      − Σ V_boxed_or_tubular_steel         ← ALWAYS, irrespective of size
      − 0                     for rebar and for solid enclosed steel sections

Enclosed in the concrete                            Deduct?
bar reinforcement, any quantity                     no
a solid rolled steel section cast in                no
a boxed or tubular steel section cast in            YES — always, any size
a void, opening or duct < 1.00 m³                   no
a void ≥ 1.00 m³                                    yes


⚠ The boxed/tubular exception is absolute and has no size threshold. It is there because a
hollow section displaces concrete that would otherwise fill it, and it is easy to miss.

2.2 C2 Poured concrete — by VOLUME [C2.1]
V = N × L × W × T

The eleven classifications, each given separately, and each with what it includes:

                                                                                Includes — do not
#                         Class                     Formula                     measure separately
1                         Foundations               L × W × T                   combined and
                                                                                isolated bases
2                         Pile caps                 N × L × W × T               ground beams
3                         Blinding                  A × t
4                         Beds                      A × t, state                roads and footpaths
                                                    thickness
5                         Suspended slabs           A × t, state                floors, landings,
                                                    thickness                   roofs
6                         Walls                     L × H × t, state            attached columns
                                                    thickness
7                         Columns                   N × A_sect × H              casing to metal
                                                                                stanchions [sic]
8                         Beams, measured           N × b × (D − t_slab) × L    lintels, casing to
                          below the slab                                        metal beams
9                         Staircases                by volume                   steps and strings
10                        Diaphragm walls           L × W × D
11                        Other classifications     as appropriate


⚠ Class 8 is where concrete is most often over-measured. A beam is measured below
the slab — its depth is the total depth minus the slab thickness, because the slab already paid
for that band. A 600 mm beam under a 200 mm slab is measured 400 mm deep.
V_beam = N × b × (D_total − t_slab) × L

⚠ Class 6 includes attached columns. A column cast integrally with a wall is part of the
wall, not a separate column item. Measuring it twice is a real double count that survives most
checks because both rows look correct on their own.

C2.2 Special-construction suspended slabs — by AREA [C2.2]
       Poured concrete suspended slabs of SPECIAL construction … shall be measured
       by AREA; coffered and troughed slabs shall be so described, giving details of solid
       margins.
A = Σ (L × W)      −   voids per GP3.2/GP3.3            ← AREA, not volume

⚠ A coffered or troughed slab switches unit from m³ to m². Measuring it by volume means
computing a void deduction for every coffer, which is exactly what this clause exists to avoid.

C2.3 Grouping thicknesses [C2.3] Items of differing thickness may be grouped provided
the range of thicknesses is stated.

2.3 C3 Reinforcement [C3.1–C3.4]
Bar — by WEIGHT [C3.1] [C3.2]
W_kg = Σ over each bar mark:      N_bars × L_bar × m_per_m(Ø)


m_per_m = (π/4) × Ø² × 7850 / 1e6              Ø in mm, gives kg/m for steel at 7850 kg/m³

Standard masses, for checking:

               Ø mm      8        10       12        16       20      25       32          40
               kg/m      0.395    0.617    0.888     1.579    2.466   3.854    6.313       9.864


Bars of differing diameters are given SEPARATELY [C3.2] — never a single blended ton-
nage.
NET weight — nothing added [C3.1]:

                  Never add                Why
                  rolling margin           a mass tolerance, not steel you can point at
                  supports and chairs      accessory steel, not designed bar
                  spacers                  ditto
                  tying wire               ditto


⚠ The lap question. POMI excludes laps expressly for FABRIC only. For bar it is silent.
The house treatment is in ref-reinforcement-measurement.md: a lap is measured as bar length
where the DETAIL SHOWS IT, because a lapped bar is steel fixed in position. It is never a
percentage uplift on a total — “+7.5% for laps” has no clause behind it, is not net as fixed in
position, and fails GP3.1.
L_bar = L_designed + Σ lap(i)              where the detail places lap(i)
lap    = k × Ø                             k from the structural detail, typically 40

Read [C3.1]’s exclusion list exactly: rolling margin, supports, spacers or tying wire. Laps are
not in it. The contrast with [C3.3], which excludes laps from fabric in terms, is what proves
the omission from [C3.1] is deliberate — a lap is steel fixed in position and [GP3.1] measures
what is fixed in position.

HOUSE METHOD AT TENDER — no bar bending schedule issued A BBS is rarely issued
with a tender, so the bar arrangement is measured from the section drawings and the laps
derived from the specified lap length at the locations the sections show them:
for each bar mark, read from the SECTION:
      N_bars     = (L_run / spacing) + 1                      ← count, not an assumption
      L_bar      = L_designed
                 + n_laps × (k × Ø)                           ← k and the lap positions FROM THE
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                   263



                                                              SPECIFIED DETAIL, not from habit
              + bends and hooks where the section details them
    W         = N_bars × L_bar × m_per_m(Ø)

Every row records the section drawing it came off, the spacing read, the lap length k × Ø used,
and how many laps that bar carries. That is measurement — it is citable line by line, and a
checker can re-derive it from the same section.
⚠ What remains forbidden is a blanket percentage. +7.5% for laps applied to a total has
no clause behind it, names no location, and cannot be re-derived. The difference is not the
steel — it is whether anyone can check it.

THE SECTION DRAWINGS ARE THE SOURCE — not the bar bending schedule HOUSE
Reinforcement is measured from the SECTION DRAWINGS. That is the house rule, and
it holds whether or not a BBS exists — declared under [GP1.1] and recorded under [GP1.2].

The source                                          the section drawings — bar arrangement,
                                                    spacing, cover, lap positions, bends and
                                                    hooks, read off the section
The BBS                                             a cross-check, never the source. Where
                                                    one is issued, reconcile the measured weight
                                                    against it and record the variance;
                                                    investigate a difference, do not silently adopt
                                                    the schedule’s figure


Why the sections and not the schedule:
   • At tender no BBS is issued, so a method that depends on one has no answer at tender
     and a different answer later. The take-off must produce the same figure at both.
   • A BBS is the fabricator’s cutting list. It carries the bars as they will be ordered and
     bent, which is not the same document as the designed arrangement, and it is revised on
     its own cycle.
   • A section drawing is issued with the tender under [GP2.3] and is therefore the document
     the contractor priced against. Measuring from it means the quantity and the tender
     documents are the same evidence.
⚠ So a variance against a later BBS is a finding to be recorded, not a correction to be applied.
Where the two genuinely disagree the answer is a technical query, because the disagreement
is between the fabricator’s list and the design — not an error in the take-off.

Fabric — by AREA [C3.3]
A_fabric = A_covered             NO addition for laps, ever

⚠ Fabric is measured by area of coverage. A lap covers the same square metre twice; adding
it counts one area twice. This one is explicit in the clause and there is no argument.

C3.4 Contractor-designed reinforcement              ITEM, where the detailed design is the con-
tractor’s responsibility.

C4.3 Grooves — the 2500 mm² threshold [C4.3]
if    A_section ≥ 2500 mm²        →    measure by LENGTH
if     A_section <   2500 mm²     →    DEEMED INCLUDED, measure nothing

Covers throats, rebates, chamfers. A 50 × 50 chamfer is 2500 mm² exactly — measured,
since the clause says “2500 mm² sectional area or over”.

C4.8 Shuttering to a void [C4.8]
if    V_concrete for the void was NOT deducted        →    shuttering to the void's faces is DEEMED INCLUDED

⚠ This pairs with [C1.3]. A void under 1.00 m³ is not deducted from the concrete, so its form-
work is not measured either. Deduct neither or both — never one.

PART 3 — SECTION D · MASONRY
3.1 D2 Walls and piers — by AREA [D2.1]
A = Σ (L × H)     −   voids per GP3.2 / GP3.3


#                             Class                         Formula                    Note
1                             Walls                         L × H                      integral piers

                                                                                       of COMBINED pier
                                                                                       and wall thickness
2                             Walls built against           L × H                      so described

                                                            cavity by area

✔ Class 3 gives the measurer a CHOICE, and POMI says so in terms. The clause reads
“Cavity walls measured as a composite item, including skins and cavity; alternatively, the skins
and cavity may each be measured by area.” So both of these are correct:
METHOD A — composite          A = Σ (L × H)     at one description "100 + 50 cavity + 100"
METHOD B — separately         A_outer = Σ (L × H)      at 100 mm
                              A_cavity = Σ (L × H)     at 50 mm
                              A_inner   = Σ (L × H)    at 100 mm
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                               266



⚠ What is wrong is mixing them — billing the composite item AND a skin, or measuring
Method B on one elevation and Method A on the next. Choose one for the whole bill and state
which in the preambles. A cross-check that assumes Method A will read a correct Method B
take-off as a ×2 over-measure, so the checker must be told which method is in force.
⚠ Closing the cavity at ends and around openings is deemed included — never a separate
item, under either method.
⚠ Class 1’s integral pier rule — a pier bonded into a wall is measured as wall at the combined
thickness over the pier’s own length, not as a separate pier item:
A_pier_zone = L_pier × H     at thickness (t_wall + t_pier)

Same extra-over logic as rock [B8.5]: no deduction from the wall.

PART 4 — SECTION E · METALWORK
4.1 The weight rule [E1.1]
      The weight of metalwork shall be the NET weight, WITHOUT addition for rolling mar-
      gin or welding material and WITHOUT DEDUCTION for holes, splay cuts, notches
      or the like.
W_kg = Σ over each member:     N × L × m_per_m

The rule cuts both ways, and both halves are routinely got wrong:

                                                                 Adjust?
                           rolling margin                        no addition
                           welding material, weld metal          no addition
                           bolt holes                            no deduction
                           splay cuts, notches, copes            no deduction


⚠ So a beam with forty bolt holes is measured at its full gross section mass. Deducting the
holes is as wrong as adding a rolling margin — it is the same clause forbidding both.
m_per_m comes from the section tables in the project specification. Record the section designa-
tion on the measurement row so the mass is checkable.

PART 6 — SECTION G · THERMAL AND MOISTURE PROTECTION
6.1 The flat-measurement rule [G1.1]
     Work shall be measured FLAT without addition for laps or seams.
A = Σ A_covered                no laps, no seams, no side or end laps

⚠ A membrane at 150 mm side laps and 100 mm end laps is measured at its covered area.
The lap material is a rate cost. Adding it is typically +8 to +12% of a roof.
Curved, spherical and conical work are each so described [G1.2] — described, not uplifted.
The extra labour is in the rate.

6.2 G2 Coverings and linings — by AREA [G2.1]
A = Σ (L × W)    −   voids per GP3.2 / GP3.3


Flat coverings         A = L × W
Sloping coverings     A = L × (W / cos θ)         ← ON THE SLOPE, θ from the horizontal
Vertical coverings     A = L × H

⚠ Sloping coverings are measured on the slope, not on plan. A roof of 200 m² on plan
at a 30° pitch is 200 / cos 30° = 231 m² on the slope — a 15.5% difference. Measuring on plan
under-measures every pitched roof, and the error scales with the pitch:

                       Pitch     Factor 1/cos θ   Under-measure if taken on plan
                       15°       1.035            −3.4%
                       22.5°     1.082            −7.6%
                       30°       1.155            −13.4%
                       40°       1.305            −23.4%
                       45°       1.414            −29.3%

Eaves, ridges, skirtings, fascias, flashings, aprons (m) = Σ L          [G2.2]
   — skirtings/fascias to composite roofing may alternatively be m²
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                         270



Roof lights, ventilators, soaker collars,
   special roofing sheets (nr)                       = count                  [G2.3]
ALTERNATIVELY, special roofing sheets only          = EXTRA OVER roofing     [G2.3]
   — the special sheets are MEASURED, and NO DEDUCTION is made
     from the roofing in which the special sheeting occurs

⚠ The extra-over alternative is offered for the special SHEETS only, not for the roof
lights, ventilators or soaker collars — those are enumerated either way. And under the extra-
over route the base roofing area stays whole: deducting the special sheet from the roofing is
the [B8.5] / [D2.2] error again, in a third place.

7.1 H5 Glass — the smallest-rectangle rule [H5.1]
     glass shall be measured by area; panes of IRREGULAR SHAPE shall be measured
     as the SMALLEST RECTANGLE from which such irregular shape can be cut
A_regular      = L × W
A_irregular = L_bounding × W_bounding               ← the smallest enclosing rectangle

Worked — a triangular gable pane, base 1.80 m, height 1.10 m:
true triangle area       = ½ × 1.80 × 1.10 = 0.99 m²
MEASURED                 = 1.80 × 1.10       = 1.98 m²         ← the smallest rectangle it cuts from

⚠ Exactly double here, and that is correct. The glazier buys and cuts the rectangle; the offcut
is waste he cannot use. Measuring the true triangle halves a real cost.

PART 8 — SECTION J · FINISHES
8.1 The rules that govern the whole section [J1.1–J1.3]
A = measured FLAT, no addition for laps or seams                                     [J1.1]

     • finishes on corrugated or ornamental surfaces are each so described [J1.1]
     • curved, spherical, conical each so described [J1.2]
     • internal and external each so described [J1.3]
⚠ All three are descriptions, not quantity adjustments. Do not uplift the area for a curved
wall; describe it as curved and let the rate carry it.

10.2 Q2 Pipework — by LENGTH [Q2.1]
        Pipes and gutters shall be measured by length, taken along the CENTRE LINE OVER
        ALL FITTINGS.
Len = Σ L_centreline                      bends, tees, reducers NOT deducted

⚠ Over all fittings means you run the tape straight through every bend and tee. Do not deduct
the fitting’s own length. The length pays for the run; the fitting, where it is enumerable, pays
for its extra cost on top.
State whether the diameter is internal or external [GP5.2] — a mandatory statement for
pipework, and rates differ.

The 60 mm rule — the most important threshold in the MEP bill [Q2.2]
if   Ø_internal ≤ 60 mm        →       FITTINGS ARE DEEMED INCLUDED.    Measure NOTHING for them.
if   Ø_internal >     60 mm        →    FITTINGS ARE ENUMERATED
                                        (except joints in the running length, which are included),
                                        GROUPED per size, described as 'fittings'


the same rule applies to FITTINGS TO GUTTERS, grouped per size of GUTTER

⚠ The rule covers gutters, not only pipes. [Q2.2] says “fittings … to large pipes … and to
gutters”. Gutter fittings — stop ends, outlets, angles — are enumerated and grouped per size
of gutter, on the same wording and in the same item, and are routinely missed because the
clause is filed mentally under pipework.
⚠ This single threshold decides whether an MEP bill has a hundred fitting items or none.
Enumerating fittings on 20 mm PPR is billing work already inside the linear rate; failing to
enumerate them on 100 mm ductile iron leaves real money unbilled.
Valves, traps, expansion compensators (nr) = count
     — sleeves, cover-plates DEEMED INCLUDED                                                 [Q2.3]


10.3 Q3 Ductwork — the compound formula
Rectangular ductwork — by WEIGHT [Q3.1]
        Rectangular ductwork shall be measured by WEIGHT, based upon the AREA calcu-
        lated as the LENGTH, taken along the centre line over all fittings, TIMES THE NET
        GIRTH of nominal dimensions. Blank ends shall be added to the area for weighting
        but NO DEDUCTION shall be made for intersections or openings; extra weight for
        seams, stiffeners, supports, fixings or the like shall be understood to be included.
girth    =    2 × (w + d)                                  w, d the NOMINAL duct dimensions, m
A         =   L_centreline × girth                         m², over all fittings
A         =   A + Σ A_blank_ends                           blank ends ADDED to the area
                                                           NO DEDUCTION for intersections or openings
W_kg     =    A × m_per_m2(gauge)                          the BARE gauge weight, applied FLAT —
                                                           NO uplift for seams, stiffeners, supports
                                                           or fixings; all deemed included

Worked — 12.40 m of 600 × 400 duct, 1.0 mm galvanised steel at 8.0 kg/m², one blank
end:
girth          = 2 × (0.60 + 0.40)              = 2.00 m
A_run          = 12.40 × 2.00                   = 24.80 m²
A_blank        = 0.60 × 0.40                    =   0.24 m²
A_total        = 24.80 + 0.24                   = 25.04 m²
W              = 25.04 × 8.0                    = 200.32 kg

⚠ Five ways this goes wrong. Using internal rather than nominal dimensions; forgetting
that blank ends are added to the area and not enumerated; deducting the area of a branch
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                      276



intersection or a grille opening, which POMI forbids; uplifting the weight by the usual 10–
15% trade allowance for seams, stiffeners and hangers, which POMI deems included; and
stating the gauge but not the unit weight, which [GP5.4] requires for a weight item.
The last two pull in opposite directions and can hide each other in a total — a duct that has
been deducted for openings and then uplifted for stiffeners can foot to about the right figure
while every row in it is wrong.
⚠ Fittings to rectangular ductwork are DEEMED INCLUDED [Q3.3]. The centre-line
length runs over them and nothing more is measured.

Circular, oval and flexible ductwork — by LENGTH [Q3.2]
Len = Σ L_centreline, over all fittings
Fittings (excluding test holes and covers) = ENUMERATED, grouped per duct size,
                                                 described as 'fittings'          [Q3.3]

⚠ Note the asymmetry: rectangular fittings are included, circular fittings are enumer-
ated. Same section, opposite treatment, and it follows the unit — a weight-based item absorbs
its fittings, a length-based one does not.
Dampers, grilles, flexible connectors (nr) = count                                [Q3.4]

⚠ Q7.2 says AREA, while Q3.1 says WEIGHT — for the same duct. The duct is billed by
weight; its insulation is billed by the area from the same girth calculation. Same geometry,
two different units, and using the wrong one is a whole-item error:
duct         W_kg = (L × girth) × m_per_m2
insulation   A_m2 =   L × girth

11.1 The two definitions that decide the unit [R1.3] [R1.4]
'cable'     INCLUDES tape, bus-bar trunking or the like                           [R1.3]
'conduit'   INCLUDES trunking, cable tray, ducting or the like                    [R1.4]

⚠ These are wide. Cable tray and trunking are “conduit” for measurement, so they follow
the conduit rules, not a rule of their own.

11.2 The circuit hierarchy — the whole logic of Section R

Level                                 Definition                        Unit
Main                                  the incoming supply to the        cable by LENGTH, conduit

                                                                        [R4.1]


Main          Len (m) = Σ L_cable ;    Σ L_conduit
Sub-main      N (nr)   = count of circuits, separately identified
                         (alternatively measured by length per R2.2/R2.3)
Final         N (nr)   = count of POINTS, classified per R4.1

⚠ This is the single biggest structural decision in an electrical bill. A final sub-circuit is
billed as a point — one number that carries its cable, its conduit, its boxes and its terminations.
Measuring the cable length of a lighting circuit as well as enumerating the point is a double
count of the entire final distribution.

⚠ Class 3 is a counting rule, not a description rule. A twin 13 A socket, a 4-gang outlet

PART 12 — THE CROSS-CHECKS A MEASUREMENT MUST SURVIVE
These are arithmetic identities, not opinions. A take-off that fails one of them is wrong some-
where, even when every individual row looks right.

12.1 Excavation ↔ disposal [B11.1]
V_disposal_total      ==   V_excavation_total    +   V_dredging    +   V_tunnelling      EXACTLY
V_backfill + V_removed       ==   V_disposal_total


12.2 Excavation ↔ substructure concrete
V_excavation    ≥    V_concrete_below_ground     +   V_blinding    +   V_hardcore

The dig must at least contain what is built in it. Where it does not, either the excavation is
short or a foundation has been measured that nothing was dug for.

12.3 Concrete ↔ formwork HOUSE
For a rectangular member, the ratio of shuttered area to concrete volume has a knowable
range. Outside it, one of the two is wrong:
r   =   A_shutter / V_concrete                  m²/m³


                    Member                                        Typical r   Read as
                    slab, 200 mm, soffit only                     ≈ 5.0       1/t
                    wall, 250 mm, both faces                      ≈ 8.0       2/t
                    column, 400 × 400                             ≈ 10.0      perimeter / A_sect
                    beam, 300 × 600 under a 200 slab              ≈ 7–9
                    foundation, mass, sides only                  ≈ 1–3


⚠ r far above the range usually means formwork was measured to faces that are cast against
earth or against existing construction. Far below usually means a face was missed.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                            279



12.4 Concrete ↔ reinforcement HOUSE
ρ_rebar    =    W_rebar_kg / V_concrete_m3                kg/m³


                                      Element                      Typical range
                                      blinding                     0
                                      mass foundation              30 – 60
                                      raft, ground beam            90 – 160
                                      suspended slab               80 – 130
                                      column                       150 – 300
                                      beam                         120 – 220
                                      core / shear wall            100 – 200


These are sense checks, not rules. A figure outside the range is a question to answer, not a
quantity to change — and the answer goes in the run audit either way.

12.5 Wall finishes ↔ wall area HOUSE
A_finish    ≈   A_wall_structure      ×    (number of finished faces)
                 −   Σ voids ≥ 1.00 m² and all edge voids
                 +   Σ reveals, returns, columns                  [J3.1 class 2]

The + term is the one that gets dropped, and it always makes the finish larger than the struc-
ture.

12.6 Doors and windows ↔ their voids
count(door items, H1.1)          ==       count(door voids deducted from walls)
count(window items, H2.1)        ==       count(window voids deducted from walls)

⚠ A door counted in H but never deducted from D or J means the wall and its plaster were
paid for through the opening. A void deducted with no door item means the door was never
billed.

12.7 Roof area ↔ pitch [G2.1]
A_slope    ==   A_plan / cos θ                         θ = roof pitch from horizontal

If A_slope == A_plan on a pitched roof, the roof was measured on plan and is under-measured
by the table in §6.2.

12.8 Drainage ↔ excavation [B9.2]
if drain trenches measured by LENGTH under B9.2
   then    NO separate disposal and NO separate filling rows for those trenches

Both are deemed included. Their presence is a double count.

12.9 MEP points ↔ cable HOUSE, from [R4.1]
if final sub-circuits enumerated as POINTS
   then    NO cable or conduit length measured for those same circuits

PART 14 — WHAT THE SEAT MUST RECORD FOR EVERY QUANTITY
Every measurement row carries, without exception:
1    the POMI clause           the rule applied — an item with no clause is a HOUSE EXTENSION
                               and must declare itself
2    the classification        which numbered class within the clause
3    N × L × W × H             each factor in its own column, never a pre-multiplied total
4    the deduction basis       which voids were deducted and under which limb of GP3.2/GP3.3
5    the source                doc_id, sheet, and the read tier from the extraction record
6    the DWG Ref hyperlink     to the marked-up sheet that proves it
7    the mandatory statements the clause demands — thickness, number, range, drop, diameter
                               basis, unit weight, average depth

A row missing 1, 4 or 6 is not a measurement. It is an assertion.

SUPERSEDES v1.0 ENTIRELY.
Source: POMI (RICS, 1979, reprinted 2004), Sections GP, P, Q, R.
Version 1.0 of this file was written before the standard was consulted and was wrong in twelve
places — it over-enumerated where POMI groups or gives an item, and it measured ductwork
by the wrong unit entirely. Every rule below now cites its clause. Anything without a clause
is a HOUSE EXTENSION declared at §9 and notified in the bill preamble under GP1.2.
POMI TELLS YOU WHAT THE ITEM IS, WHAT IS IN IT, AND WHAT IS NOT. THE HOUSE
BUILD-UP TELLS YOU HOW TO ARRIVE AT THE LENGTH. THE BUILD-UP MAY NOT
CHANGE THE ITEM.
NOTATION — two internal codes appear below and NEITHER is a POMI clause: C3 the Lead

minism class “produced by a script” (determinism.md §1). NOT POMI Section D Masonry.

               0 THE MEASURED ITEM — WHAT POMI ACTUALLY REQUIRES


For a pipe riser, the bill line is:
LENGTH, taken along the CENTRE LINE, OVER ALL FITTINGS Q2.1 stating the diam-
eter, and stating whether it is INTERNAL or EXTERNAL GP5.2 measured net as fixed in
position, to the nearest 10 mm GP3.1
That is the whole item. Not net of fittings. Not with fittings deducted. The tape runs through
every bend, tee and valve on the centre line and does not stop.
Everything else on the riser is one of exactly three things:
ENUMERATED SEPARATELY valves, traps, expansion compensators Q2.3 fittings to pipes
over 60 mm ID, GROUPED PER SIZE and described as ‘fittings’ Q2.2 dampers, grilles, flexi-
ble connectors Q3.4 insulation boxes around accessories Q7.4 connections to supply mains —
SUBJECT TO GP8: where the work may only be carried out by a government or public au-
thority it is a SUM exclusive of profit, with a profit item GP8.1 and an item for ASSISTANCE BY
THE CONTRACTOR GP8.2, whose contents are those listed at GP6.2 — NOT an enumerated
measured item [Q6.1/GP8.1/GP8.2]
AN ITEM supports — including fixings, anchors, insulating blocks, anti-vibration devices [P2.1
/ Q8.1] identification, testing and commissioning, tools and spares, documents [P2.1 / Q8.1] in-
cidental work — co-ordination, cutting or forming holes and making good, building in brackets
and making good [P3.1 / Q9.1]
INCLUDED IN THE RATE fittings to pipes 60 mm ID or less Q2.2 joints in the running length,
any size Q2.2 sleeves, cover-plates or the like — Q2.3 says these are “understood to be in-
cluded”; it does not say in WHICH item. Either way they are not measured Q2.3 fittings to
rectangular ductwork Q3.3 the EXTRA WEIGHT FOR seams, stiffeners, supports and fixings
to rectangular ductwork — Q3.1 includes the added weight of that metal in the weighted area.
It does NOT abolish the P2.1 supports ITEM, which is still given Q3.1 additional insulation
to flanges Q7.2 wiring, tubing, isolators, starters and relays associated with AUTOMATIC
CONTROLS — starters and contactors forming part of the ELECTRICAL installation are enu-
merated under R6.1, or as equipment points under R4.1.4 Q5.2 labour, materials, plant, tem-
porary works, overheads and profit GP4.1
The 60 mm internal diameter threshold is the most load-bearing number in the ser-
vices sections. It decides whether every fitting on a run is in the rate or enumerated, and it
appears again in J6.3/J6.4 for decoration.

1 THE RISER REGISTER [HOUSE — GP1.2 extension, class D] ===========================
POMI requires the length; it does not tell you how to arrive at it. This is how.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                             283



One row per riser, from the riser diagram or schematic — never from a floor plan, which shows
where a riser passes, not what it is.
riser_id the identifier printed on the schematic. Not invented. service the system it carries.
Installations are classified BY FUNCTION and given separately [Q1.1 / R1.1] start_point a
NAMED point: plant room, tank, incoming main, board, manhole end_point a NAMED point:
roof tank, highest fixture, terminal board, vent levels_served the levels at which it makes a
connection, listed individually shaft_ref the shaft or duct it occupies, where identified
A riser with an unbounded end is NOT_MEASURABLE. Assuming it starts at the lowest slab
is how the plant-room run and the tank connection disappear.
Alternative permitted by Q1.2 / R1.2: an installation may instead be ENUMERATED ON
A LOCATIONAL BASIS (e.g. “cold water installation to ground floor”). That choice is made
ONCE per project by C3, recorded, and applied consistently. It is not chosen per riser.
================================================================
2 SEGMENTATION BY SIZE [Q2.2, GP5.2 — class D] ================================
Q2.2 groups fittings for each size of pipe, and GP5.2 requires the size stated on every length
item. A riser whose diameter changes is therefore more than one item.
A NEW SEGMENT BEGINS AT EVERY: change of diameter change of material change of in-
sulation thickness or type [GP5.2 — a length item states cross-sectional size; Q7.1 gives only
the unit and the centre line] start or end of a horizontal offset
Sizes come from the SCHEMATIC or riser diagram and from layout size tags. Not from the
plan, which rarely tags a vertical.
Where the schematic shows a size change but not the level at which it occurs, the boundary is
NOT_FOUND: record both sizes, record the unknown transition, raise a query. Do not place
the change at the midpoint.
================================================================
3 THE LENGTH [Q2.1 measured; HOUSE build-up — class D] ===========================
L_segment = (level_top − level_bottom) + Σ horizontal offsets in the segment
Measured along the CENTRE LINE, OVER ALL FITTINGS Q2.1, net as fixed in position, each
measurement to the nearest 10 mm GP3.1.
Levels come from the LEVEL SCHEDULE or the section — structural or finished floor level,
stated, and used consistently. Never floor-to-floor height × floor count. Ground storeys
are taller; podium, transfer and plant levels differ; a riser from a basement pump room starts
below the lowest slab; one terminating at a roof tank continues above the highest; and the top
segment stops at a connection, not at a level.
Base and head allowances. From start_point to the first vertical, and from the last vertical
to end_point. The plant-room horizontal run is frequently longer than a storey and is the first
thing lost, because the eye stops at the top and bottom lines of the schematic.
Offsets are measured where dimensioned. A schematic is not to scale — an offset visible
but undimensioned is NOT_FOUND, raised, never scaled off.
Fittings at the offset are not added as length: the centre line already runs through them Q2.1.
Whether they are enumerated depends only on §4.
================================================================
4 FITTINGS AND VALVES [Q2.2, Q2.3] ========================================
PIPE ID ≤ 60 mm ALL FITTINGS INCLUDED — no fittings item at any size below the threshold.
Valves, traps and expansion compensators are STILL enumerated at every size Q2.3 |
PIPE ID > 60 mm Fittings ENUMERATED, grouped together for each size, described as
‘fittings’. NOT itemised as tees, bends, reducers, take-offs. Joints in the running length
INCLUDED at any size. Q2.2
ANY SIZE Valves, traps, expansion compensators or the like ENUMERATED. Q2.3 Sleeves,
cover-plates or the like INCLUDED. Q2.3
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              284



So a CHW riser at 150 mm produces: one length item per size; one ‘fittings’ item per size,
enumerated; and separate enumerated items for each valve type. A riser at 50 mm produces
the length item, the valves, and no fittings item — but it still produces its insulation length
line Q7.1 and any insulation boxes Q7.4, and it still sits within the P2.1 supports item and the
P3.1 incidental item like every other run.
“One per floor” remains banned — a house rule, and it survives POMI because Q2.3 re-
quires valves enumerated and an enumeration is a count. Count them from the schematic. A
riser serving five levels may carry four branch valves because the lowest comes off the header,
or seven because two levels are twinned.
Where the schematic is single-line and shows no branch fittings, the count is NOT_FOUND
with a query. It is not the level count.
================================================================
5 INSULATION [Q7] ===================================================
Insulation to PIPEWORK by LENGTH, along the centre line OVER ALL FITTINGS Q7.1 Insu-
lation to RECTANGULAR ductwork by AREA, calculated per Q3 Q7.2 additional insulation to
flanges INCLUDED Q7.2 Insulation to circular, oval and flexible ductwork by LENGTH over all
fittings Q7.3 Insulation BOXES around accessories ENUMERATED Q7.4 Insulation to EQUIP-
MENT ENUMERATED Q7.5
Pipe insulation is measured on the SAME centre line as the pipe and therefore on the same seg-
mentation, because thickness follows diameter. Q7.1 gives only the unit and the centre-
line rule; the requirement to state the size comes from GP5.2, and the thickness state-
ment is a house requirement declared at §9. An insulated riser produces at least two length
lines per segment. A riser take-off with pipe lengths and no insulation lines is incomplete on
its face.
Vapour barrier, foil, cladding and mesh are stated in the description; they are not separate
items unless the specification bills them apart.
================================================================
6 SUPPORTS, IDENTIFICATION, TESTING [P2.1 via Q8.1 / R9.1] =========================
These are ITEMS. They are not enumerated and not measured.
1 Supports — INCLUDES fixings, anchors, insulating blocks and anti-vibration devices 2 Identi-
fication — INCLUDES plates, discs, labels, charts, colour coding 3 Testing and commissioning
— INCLUDES operating completed installations and providing fuel and power 4 Tools and
spares — INCLUDES loose keys and consumable stores 5 Documents — INCLUDES drawings,
operating instructions, maintenance manuals
An item is given for each, per installation. Riser clamps, brackets, anchors and guides all fall
within item 1. Counting them per level, as v1.0 required, bills work that is already in an item
— a double count.
Where the specification requires a support regime that is not at the contractor’s discretion,
give the particulars in the item description. The particulars change what the item covers; they
do not turn it into a measured quantity.
================================================================
7 HOLES, MAKING GOOD AND PENETRATIONS [P3.1 via Q9.1 / R10.1] =====================
An ITEM is given for incidental work, which INCLUDES:
1 Co-ordination with other engineering installations 2 Cutting or forming holes, mortices,
chases or the like, and making good finishings 3 Building in or cutting and pinning brackets
or the like, and making good finishings
So the penetration, the hole, and the making good are inside this item. They are not enumer-
ated per floor.
What is still separately measured, and the distinction matters:
the SLEEVE or cover-plate INCLUDED — not measured. Q2.3 does not name the item it sits in;
do not assert one Q2.3 the structural opening formed in concrete, and any cast-in structural

8.1 CHILLED WATER, HEATING, DOMESTIC WATER [Q2, Q7]
Length per size over all fittings; diameter stated internal or external. Fittings grouped per
size where over 60 mm ID. Valves enumerated by type and size. Insulation by length on the
same segmentation.
Hot water carries a return. Flow and return are two runs and two sets of segments.
Measured once, half the pipework is gone. [HOUSE — arises from Q1.1, installations
classified by function.]
Tanks, pumps, air-handling units, fans, hoods and sanitary fittings are ENUMERATED Q4.1
— they are not part of the riser.



8.2 SOIL, WASTE AND VENT STACKS [Q2]
Measured downward: from the highest connection or the vent terminal above roof to the drain
connection. The below-slab drainage belongs to the drainage measurement — cross-reference
at the boundary, do not measure through it.
Stacks are almost always over 60 mm ID, so fittings are enumerated grouped per size as
‘fittings’. Traps are enumerated Q2.3. Access and rodding eyes are fittings, not separate
items, unless the specification names them as accessories.
The vent above the roof and the connection below the lowest slab are the two ends that vanish.
Both are within the measured centre line.

8.3 FIRE — WET AND DRY RISERS, SPRINKLER [Q2, Q4]
Riser main by length per size. Landing valves, breeching inlets, air release and drain
assemblies are valves or the like and are ENUMERATED Q2.3. Hose reels and cabinets are
equipment or accessories — enumerated [Q4.1 / K1.2]. Sprinkler heads are enumerated.
Flow switches are sensing devices Q5.1 and enumerated.



8.4 DUCTWORK RISERS [Q3]
RECTANGULAR duct — BY WEIGHT. Q3.1 Area = centre-line length OVER ALL FITTINGS
× net girth of nominal dimensions. Blank ends ADDED to the area for weighting. NO
deduction for intersections or openings. Extra weight for seams, stiffeners, supports,
fixings INCLUDED. State material thickness and unit weight. GP5.4
Weight = weighted area × unit weight for the stated material thickness. The AREA
IS AN INTERMEDIATE; the BILLED QUANTITY IS WEIGHT. GP5.4
CIRCULAR, OVAL and FLEXIBLE duct — BY LENGTH, centre line over all fittings. Q3.2
Fittings to RECTANGULAR duct — INCLUDED. Q3.3 Fittings to CIRCULAR and OVAL duct —

Fire dampers are dampers and are enumerated Q3.4.
Test holes and covers ARE addressed — Q3.3 enumerates fittings to circular and oval duct

Measuring final-circuit cable by the metre AND enumerating the POINT double-
counts the cable, invisibly. R4.1 puts the cable inside the point. R5.1 accessories are
a SEPARATE and ADDITIONAL enumeration — ceiling roses, switches, socket outlets
and bell pushes are enumerated as well as the point, and suppressing them under-bills the
fittings.

REINFORCEMENT MEASUREMENT
skills/pomi-take-off/references/ref-reinforcement-measurement.md · 356 lines
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                  289



Version 1.2 — verified against the source; lap argument rebuilt,
B17.1 double count removed, C6.3 restored.
Binding on every measurement seat.
Source: POMI (RICS, 1979, reprinted 2004), Sections GP, C3, C4, D4.
Reinforcement is measured by weight, and almost every dispute about it is a dispute about
what is inside that weight. POMI settles it in four clauses, and the settlement is narrower than
most house practice assumes.
C3.1 THE WEIGHT OF BAR REINFORCEMENT SHALL BE THE NET WEIGHT WITHOUT
ADDITION FOR ROLLING MARGIN, SUPPORTS, SPACERS OR TYING WIRE.
C3.2 BAR REINFORCEMENT SHALL BE MEASURED BY WEIGHT, STATING THE DIAMETER;
BARS OF DIFFERING DIAMETERS SHALL BE GIVEN SEPARATELY.
C3.3 FABRIC REINFORCEMENT SHALL BE MEASURED BY AREA, WITHOUT ADDITION
FOR LAPS.
C3.4 REINFORCEMENT SHALL BE GIVEN AS AN ITEM WHERE THE DETAILED DESIGN
WORK IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE CONTRACTOR.

  1 THE LAP QUESTION — POMI IS SILENT, AND WHY THE ANSWER STILL FOLLOWS


State this accurately: POMI does not say bar laps are measured. It excludes laps ex-
pressly for FABRIC only C3.3 and says nothing about bar. The house treatment below is a
GP1.1 build-up — more detailed information than the document requires — and it is declared
at §9.
The argument is NOT that C3.1’s silence proves anything. C3.1 governs what is added to
the WEIGHT BASIS — rolling margin (a mass tolerance), supports, spacers and tying wire
(accessory steel that is not the designed bar). It is not a list of geometric exclusions, so its
silence on laps carries no weight either way.
The argument is the measurement basis, and it is decisive:
FABRIC is measured by AREA OF COVERAGE C3.3. A lap overlaps the same square metre
twice. Adding it would count one area twice — so C3.3 excludes it expressly, and must.
BAR is measured by LENGTH × mass per metre C3.2. A lapped bar is genuinely, physically
longer. GP3.1 requires work measured net as fixed in position, and a lap is steel fixed in
position, part of the permanent works.
The two clauses differ because the two bases differ, not because a drafter signalled an inten-
tion.
THEREFORE: BAR LAPS ARE MEASURED, as bar length, WHERE THE DETAIL SHOWS
THEM. FABRIC LAPS ARE NOT MEASURED, EVER. C3.3
A lap is measured because it is a real length of a real bar on a real detail. It is not a percentage
uplift on a total. A lap allowance applied as “+7.5% for laps” has no clause behind it, is not
net as fixed in position, and fails GP3.1 and the fabrication gate alike.
MEASURED LAP bar runs 6.80 m, detail shows a 40Ø lap at midspan, T16 → lap 0.64 m → bar
length 7.44 m FABRICATED LAP total tonnage × 1.075 no clause, no evidence, not measurable
WHERE THE DETAIL DOES NOT PLACE THE LAP. Do NOT derive the number of laps
from an assumed stock length. How many laps a bar needs is then a function of the bar length
the contractor chooses to buy — a construction method decision, which GP4.1 puts in the rate
(“materials, goods and all associated costs”). On a 6.80 m bar a single assumed 40Ø lap adds
9.4 per cent to that bar’s weight, on an assumption about somebody else’s procurement.
The correct treatment is GP2.2: measure the bar as detailed, and describe the item as AP-
PROXIMATE, or give it in a bill of approximate quantities. The tenderer prices knowing it
will be re-measured against the executed BBS.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                 290




                 2 WHAT IS EXPRESSLY EXCLUDED FROM THE WEIGHT C3.1


None of these is added to the weight, and none is a separate measured item — they fall into
the rate under GP4.1.
ROLLING MARGIN the permitted mass tolerance on the bar as rolled. The measured weight
is the theoretical weight from the nominal diameter, not the delivered weight. SUPPORTS
chairs, stools, continuous high chairs, trestles SPACERS blocks, wheels, clips TYING WIRE all
of it
A take-off carrying a line for spacers or tying wire has billed work already in the rate. A
take-off uplifting tonnage for rolling margin has billed steel that does not exist in the design.

                               3 BY DIAMETER, SEPARATELY C3.2


Bars of differing diameters shall be given separately. T12 and T16 are two items. They
may not be grouped, summed, averaged, or presented as a single tonnage with a mixed de-
scription.
The description states the diameter. Under GP5.4, an item measured by weight states the
material thickness and unit weight where appropriate — for bar, the diameter carries both.
Grade is stated where the specification distinguishes grades. This is a house requirement,
not a POMI one — C1.1 requires reinforced and plain CONCRETE each to be so described,
which is a rule about the concrete item and says nothing about reinforcement grade. Declared
at §9.

                      4 THE CONVERSION [physical constants — class D]


weight (kg) = total bar length (m) × mass per metre (kg/m)
Theoretical mass per metre for round bar, from nominal diameter:

Bar      T6         T8         T10        T12     T16      T20       T25       T32       T40
kg/m     0.222      0.395      0.617      0.888   1.579    2.466     3.854     6.313     9.864


These are derived constants (7850 kg/m³ × πd²/4) and are class D. They are not a benchmark,
a ratio or a rule of thumb — they are the geometry of a cylinder.
Bar counts come from the detail:
bars = (element dimension ÷ spacing) + 1
taken each way and each face as the detail shows, with the element dimension and the spacing
both read from the drawing. Neither is assumed.

                       5 WHEN THERE IS NO BAR BENDING SCHEDULE


At tender a BBS is frequently not issued. That does not make reinforcement unmeasurable,
and it does not license a ratio. Work down this order:
1 BBS ISSUED. Measure the weight from the schedule. R1 read, one row per bar mark. This
is the only case that requires no derivation.
2 NO BBS, BUT REINFORCEMENT SHOWN ON SECTIONS AND DETAILS. This is
the normal tender case, and it is ordinary POMI measurement — NOT a departure
and NOT declared under GP1.2. C3.2 prescribes the ITEM: weight, stating the diameter,
differing diameters separately. It says nothing about which document the dimension is taken
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                 291



from. Reading a bar length off a section rather than off a schedule is no more a departure
than reading a wall length off a plan rather than off a schedule. The bill item is identical either
way. Measure it: count bars from the printed spacing over the printed element dimension,
take each bar’s length from the detail including laps and anchorage as shown, convert at §4,
and show the derivation in the description. Where the derivation carries real uncertainty —
laps undimensioned, anchorage not shown, bar marks incomplete, secondary steel around
openings undetailed — GP2.2 applies: describe the item as APPROXIMATE, or give it in
a bill of approximate quantities. That is the honest treatment, and it is far better than the
two things offices do instead: a kg/m³ allowance (no clause, fails GP3.1) or a rate-only item
(leaves the tender total understated).
3 DETAILED DESIGN IS THE CONTRACTOR’S RESPONSIBILITY. Give reinforcement
AS AN ITEM. C3.4
 **C3.4 turns on design RESPONSIBILITY, not on document AVAILABILITY.**
 A missing bar bending schedule does NOT engage it. The BBS is a
 construction-stage document; its absence at tender says nothing about who
 designed the steel. Where the structural sections and details carry the
 engineer's reinforcement design, the design is the engineer's and route 2
 governs.


 C3.4 applies where the CONTRACT puts the rebar design on the contractor
 AND the element is measured under Section C: contractor-designed precast,
 and elements the specification hands over as a performance requirement.


 **TWO CASES THAT ARE NOT C3.4, AND ONE IS A DOUBLE COUNT:**


 **PERFORMANCE-DESIGNED PILING — NO reinforcement item at all.** B17.1:
 *"Performance designed piles shall be enumerated; reinforcement and
 disposal of material arising from boring shall be understood to be
 INCLUDED."* The reinforcement is inside the enumerated pile. Giving a C3.4
 reinforcement item beside it bills the same steel twice.


 **SHORING — no reinforcement item arises either way.** Shoring other than
 incidental is an ITEM under B6.2, and its reinforcement is within that
 item. B6.3 is not a design-allocation clause at all — it requires
 particulars to be given *where the design of the shoring is NOT at the
 contractor's discretion*, which is the opposite reading.


 **Applying C3.4 because a BBS is missing is a commercial error, not only a
 measurement one.** It transfers a design responsibility the contract has
 not transferred, and it converts a measurable quantity into a lump the
 employer cannot re-measure.

4 NEITHER A SCHEDULE NOR A DETAIL, AND THE DESIGN IS NOT THE CONTRAC-
TOR’S. The item is NOT_MEASURABLE. Quantity null, reason recorded, gap raised, and
GP2.2 applies — describe it as approximate or give it in a bill of approximate quantities.
Never a kg/m³ ratio. 120 kg/m³ is a CHECKING benchmark for a senior QS looking at
a finished take-off. It has never generated a quantity, it traces to no drawing, and it fails
GP3.1, R-COUNT-FROM-DRAWINGS and the fabrication scan together. A tonnage derived
from concrete volume is the single clearest example of a number that looks like a measurement
and is not one.

                                           6 FABRIC C3.3


Measured by AREA, without addition for laps.
Not by weight. Not by sheet. The mesh reference is stated in the description.
The area is the area covered, measured net as fixed in position — so the laps, which overlap,
are not added, and neither are they deducted twice: measure the covered area once.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                             292



In masonry, fabric may alternatively be measured by LENGTH D4.1. That alternative is
chosen once by C3 and applied consistently.

                 7 WHAT REINFORCEMENT DOES NOT DEDUCT FROM C1.3


No deduction shall be made from the concrete volume for the volume of any rein-
forcement or structural metal enclosed in the concrete.
Except: voids caused by boxed or tubular structural metalwork are ALWAYS deducted.
So concrete is measured gross of its reinforcement. A take-off that nets rebar volume out of
the concrete has under-measured the concrete and has done so on an assumption no clause
supports.

                            8 COMPANION ITEMS [C1.1, C2.1, C4.1]


A reinforced concrete element yields three companion items, and the description of each iden-
tifies the element so a reader can tie them together:
POURED CONCRETE m³, classified per the eleven at C2.1, stating thickness where the clas-
sification requires it, and described as REINFORCED C1.1 REINFORCEMENT weight, by di-
ameter, separately per diameter C3.2 SHUTTERING m² net contact area, classified per the
eleven at C4.1
Where a concrete item is described as reinforced C1.1 and no reinforcement item appears
against it, that is a coverage failure — raise it, do not infer a tonnage to close it.

               9 ITEMS NOT NAMED BY POMI [HOUSE — declare under GP1.2]


POMI does not name these. Each is a house extension and each must be declared:
couplers and threaded connectors enumerated, stating size and type starter bars and dowels
measured as bar, by diameter, where the detail shows them; otherwise NOT_FOUND gal-
vanised or epoxy-coated bar stated in the description, not a separate item stainless reinforce-
ment given separately, stated in the description (post-tensioning strand and cables are NOT
a house item — see §9.1)

             9.1 PRESTRESSING — NAMED BY POMI, NOT A HOUSE ITEM [C6]


C6.2 Prestressed concrete measured by VOLUME, classified per C2 C6.3 Reinforcement per
C3; SUPPORTING STEEL WIRES OR CABLES MEASURED BY WEIGHT C6.4 Shuttering
per C4, stating whether to PRE-TENSIONED or POST-TENSIONED members
Strand and cable are therefore a POMI weight item under C6.3, not an undeclared house
extension. Ducts, anchorages and grouting are not named; those are house items and are
declared.

                                      10 BLOCK CONDITIONS


BB1 Any reinforcement weight derived from concrete volume by a kg/m³ ratio. BB2 Any per-
centage uplift applied for laps, waste, cutting or bending. BB3 Any addition to the weight for
rolling margin, supports, spacers or tying wire. C3.1 BB4 A separate measured item for chairs,
spacers or tying wire. C3.1 BB5 Bars of differing diameters grouped into one item. C3.2 BB6
A weight item that does not state the diameter. [C3.2/GP5.4] BB7 Fabric measured by weight
or by sheet rather than by area. C3.3 BB8 Any addition for fabric laps. C3.3 BB9 Reinforce-
ment measured as a weight where the detailed design is the contractor’s responsibility — it
is an ITEM. C3.4 BB10 Concrete volume reduced for the volume of enclosed reinforcement.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                             293



C1.3 BB11 A concrete item described as reinforced with no companion reinforcement item
and no raised gap. C1.1 BB12 A lap measured where neither the detail nor the specification
gives its length. BB13 A bar count derived other than from a printed spacing and a printed el-
ement dimension. BB14 A house item at §9 used without declaration under GP1.2. BB15 C3.4
applied because a bar bending schedule was unavailable, rather than because the contract
places the design on the contractor. BB16 Measurement from sections and details declared
as a GP1.2 departure — it is not one. BB17 A derivation carrying material uncertainty billed as
firm rather than described as approximate. GP2.2 BB18 A reinforcement item given against a
performance-designed pile — the reinforcement is INSIDE the enumerated pile. B17.1 BB19
A reinforcement item given against shoring — it is within the shoring ITEM. [B6.1/B6.2] BB20
A lap quantity derived from an assumed stock length where the detail does not place the lap.
[GP4.1/GP2.2] BB21 Bar laps claimed as a POMI requirement rather than a declared GP1.1
build-up.

                                          11 SELF-CHECK


AB.1 Every reinforcement item is by weight, stating the diameter, with bars of differing di-
ameters given separately. AB.2 The weight is net — no rolling margin, supports, spacers or
tying wire. AB.3 Bar laps are measured as bar length from the detail or the specified lap
length, never as a percentage. AB.4 Fabric is by area with no lap addition. AB.5 Every bar
count came from a printed spacing over a printed element dimension. AB.6 Every conversion
used the theoretical mass per metre for the nominal diameter. AB.7 No quantity was derived
from concrete volume. AB.8 Where the detailed design is the contractor’s, reinforcement is
an ITEM. AB.9 Where neither schedule nor detail exists, the item is NOT_MEASURABLE with
a reason and a gap, and is described as approximate per GP2.2. AB.13 Measurement from
sections and details rather than from a BBS was NOT declared as a departure — it is ordinary
POMI measurement of the C3.2 item. AB.14 C3.4 was applied only where the CONTRACT
places the rebar design on the contractor, never because a bar bending schedule was un-
available. AB.15 Where the derivation carried material uncertainty, the item is described as
approximate under GP2.2 rather than billed as firm. AB.16 No reinforcement item was given
against a performance-designed pile or against shoring. AB.17 No lap was derived from an
assumed stock length. AB.18 The bar-lap treatment is presented as a declared GP1.1 build-up,
not as a POMI requirement. AB.19 Prestressing strand and cables are measured by weight
under C6.3, not treated as a house extension. AB.10 Concrete volume was not reduced for
enclosed reinforcement. AB.11 Every reinforced concrete element has its three companion
items, or a raised gap. AB.12 Every §9 house item is declared under GP1.2.

This file is superseded. Do not measure from it.
Audited against POMI (RICS 1979, reprinted 2004) and found to contain 8 wrong rules, 1
wrong section letter, 2 wrong clause citations and 40 material omissions. See AUDIT-pomi-
measurement.md for the itemised findings.

It is withdrawn rather than patched because the errors are distributed through it, and a
patched file would be trusted where it should not be.

Measure from these instead

The eight rules that were wrong, in one line each
  1. Pipe fittings “where in doubt, enumerate” — Q2.2 sets a 60 mm ID threshold and admits
     no doubt
  2. Ductwork by length — Q3.1 measures RECTANGULAR duct by WEIGHT
  3. Electrical cable by the metre — R4.1 enumerates final sub-circuits as POINTS
  4. Masonry “m³ for mass” — D2.1 has no volume measurement
  5. Furnishings at Section N — POMI is L Equipment, M Furnishings, N Special Construction
  6. Stair risers cited to one clause — C4.1, J3.1, J6.3 and C2.1 each say something different
  7. Riser length as floor-to-floor × floors — Q2.1 measures the centre line over all fittings
  8. Riser supports and penetrations enumerated — P2.1 and P3.1 make them ITEMS

The two miscitations
   • The 1.00 m² void limit is GP3.2, not GP3.3. GP3.3 is the rule that voids AT THE EDGE
     of a measured area are ALWAYS deducted, irrespective of size — and it was missing
     entirely.
   • The volume deduction limit was never cited. It is C1.3: 1.00 m³, with no deduction for
     enclosed reinforcement or structural metal, except boxed or tubular metalwork which is
     always deducted.


AUDIT — pomi-measurement.md AGAINST THE STAN-
DARD
skills/pomi-take-off/references/AUDIT-pomi-measurement.md · 209 lines


Every claim in the existing reference, checked clause by clause.
Source: POMI, RICS 1979, reprinted 2004.
Verdict: 8 wrong rules, 1 wrong section letter, 2 wrong clause citations, and 40 ma-
terial omissions (O1–O40). The file should be withdrawn and replaced by a pointer to
ref-pomi-rules.md, not patched.

The errors are not evenly distributed. The concrete and formwork content is largely sound.
The services content, the site-work content and the unit table are unreliable.
================================================================
PART 1 — WRONG RULES ================================================
W1 · Pipework fittings — “where in doubt, enumerate and note it” File: “fittings on a
measured run are generally deemed included unless POMI requires them enumerated; where
in doubt, enumerate and note it.” Q2.2 is precise and admits no doubt: fittings to pipes of
60 mm internal diameter or less are INCLUDED; fittings to pipes exceeding 60 mm ID
are ENUMERATED, grouped for each size, described as ‘fittings’; joints in the running
length are included at any size. “Where in doubt, enumerate” is the opposite of a deterministic
rule and would over-measure every small-bore run in the building.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                295



W2 · Ductwork unit File: “Q | Mechanical | nr / set (plant), m (pipe/duct runs, stating size)”
Q3.1: RECTANGULAR ductwork is measured BY WEIGHT — area computed as centre-
line length over all fittings × net girth of nominal dimensions, blank ends added for weighting,
no deduction for intersections or openings, and seams, stiffeners, supports and fixings in-
cluded. Only circular, oval and flexible duct is by length (Q3.2). The file offers no weight
route at all.
W3 · Electrical final circuits File: “R | Electrical | nr (boards/fittings), m (cable/containment,
stating size)” R4.1: cable and conduit to termination points are ENUMERATED AS
POINTS — lighting points, switch points (stating one-way, two-way, intermediate), socket
outlets (multi-gang = one point), equipment points (stating type or rating), auxiliary points.
Measuring final-circuit cable by the metre while also enumerating the accessory double-counts
the cable invisibly.
W4 · Masonry by volume File: “D | Masonry | m² (walls by area, stating thickness), m³ for
mass” There is no volume measurement of masonry in POMI. D2.1 gives walls and piers
by AREA in four classifications and nothing else. “m³ for mass” is invented.
W5 · Section letters L / M / N File: “N | Furnishings | nr, item” POMI is L Equipment, M
FURNISHINGS, N SPECIAL CONSTRUCTION. The file has Furnishings at N. This is the
same mislabel that appears in the BOQ skill, where Stage 3 calls N “Special Construction —
pool, spa” while the output summary prints “N - FURNISHINGS”. Both are wrong against the
standard, in opposite directions.
W6 · Stair risers — right answer, three conflated clauses File: “POMI is explicit: a
staircase item includes treads, risers and strings (it excludes soffits).” Three different clauses
say three different things: - C4.1 item 10 SHUTTERING — includes treads, risers and strings,
excludes soffits - J3.1 item 4 FINISHES — includes treads, risers and edges of landings,
excludes soffits — not strings - J6.3 item 4 DECORATIONS — includes treads, risers, strings
and edges of landings, excludes soffits - C2.1 item 9 CONCRETE staircases — includes steps
and strings The conclusion is right for each, but the clause quoted covers only shuttering.
W7 · MEP riser length File: “length = floor-to-floor height × number of floors served.”
Q2.1: measured by length along the CENTRE LINE, OVER ALL FITTINGS, net as fixed
in position to the nearest 10 mm (GP3.1). Superseded in full by ref-mep-riser-measurement.md
v2.0.
W8 · Riser supports and penetrations File enumerates valves, tap-offs, fire dampers and
fittings “per floor” and treats supports as counted. P2.1 (via Q8.1 / R9.1): supports are
an ITEM, including fixings, anchors, insulating blocks and anti-vibration devices. P3.1 (via
Q9.1 / R10.1): cutting or forming holes and making good is within the incidental-work
ITEM.
================================================================
PART 2 — WRONG CLAUSE CITATIONS ========================================
C1 · The void deduction limit File cites GP3.3 for “no deduction for voids under 1.00 m²”.
That is GP3.2. GP3.3 is a different and more dangerous rule, and the file omits it entirely:
minimum deductions apply only to voids WITHIN the edges of measured areas — voids
AT THE EDGE are ALWAYS deducted, irrespective of size. An 0.4 m² opening at the end
of a wall is deducted; the file’s rule would keep it.
C2 · Volume deductions File: “For volume, deduct voids over the stated limit.” The limit
is never stated and the clause is never cited. C1.3: no deduction for voids less than
1.00 m³, nor for the volume of any reinforcement or structural metal enclosed in the
concrete, EXCEPT voids caused by boxed or tubular structural metalwork, which are
always deducted.

PART 4 — WHAT THE FILE GETS RIGHT =======================================
Keep, with clause citations added:
   • Measure net, evidence only, count don’t factor — consistent with GP3.1 and the house
     R-rules
   • The three-family concrete separation: concrete m³, shuttering m², reinforcement by
     weight
   • Shuttering as net contact area, no reuse factor — and now confirmed: there is no reuse
     provision anywhere in C4
   • No formwork to faces cast against earth or blinding
   • Reinforcement measured from sections and details where no BBS is issued, with the
     derivation shown
   • The bar mass-per-metre table — physical constants
   • Laps measured as bar length, never as a percentage uplift
   • Stair risers not separately measured
   • Structural shaft walls measured as concrete plus shuttering

The take-off and the bill are two documents with two different jobs, and they do not
share wording. The take-off proves the quantity — it narrates the calculation, cites the
drawing and says where on the plan. The bill binds the rate — it describes the work and says
what the money covers. A take-off line copied into a bill describes nothing; a bill description
copied into a take-off proves nothing.
Generated 2026-09-07. Nothing below is retyped. POMI comes from pomi-verbatim.md; the arith-
metic from scripts/formula_register.py; the take-off wording from scripts/takeoff_register.py;
the markup and hyperlink rules from scripts/markup_register.py; the bill wording from
scripts/wording_register.py. The generator refuses to build if any clause has no formula entry,
or any section is missing a take-off, markup or wording entry, in either direction. Coverage
is proved, not asserted.
No project data appears anywhere in this document. Where an issued bill named a
particular design standard, approving party, grade, system or schedule reference, it is written
{like this} — a field a run fills, never a constant.

PART 0 — WHAT GOVERNS EVERY SECTION
Read this once. It is the part that decides numbers in all sixteen measured sections.

0.1 The three things a quantity NEVER carries
[GP4.1] makes every rate fully inclusive of all that is necessary to fulfil the liabilities and obli-
gations arising out of the contract. [GP9.8] cl.2 independently makes waste in storage an
overhead. Between them:

Never added to the quantity          Lives in                            Clause
Working space, battering,            the rate                            [B8.2] + [GP4.1]
bulking on excavation
Rolling margin, welding              the rate                            [E1.1] [C3.1] + [GP4.1]
material, spacers, tying wire
Laps and seams on fabric,            the rate                            [C3.3] [G1.1] [J1.1]
roofing, finishes
Waste of any kind                    overheads                           [GP9.8] cl.2



Add any of them to a quantity and the same money is billed twice — once in the number
and once in the rate. The DESCRIPTION may list them as included; that is correct and does
not license adding them to the figure.

0.2 Rounding — [GP3.1]
d_measured = round(d_drawn / 0.01) × 0.01               d in metres, 2 decimals


  4.237 × 2.981   →   4.24 × 2.98   = 12.6352 m²        CORRECT
  4.237 × 2.981   = 12.630…         → 12.63 m²          WRONG

Round each dimension as it is taken, never the product. Dimensions stated in a descrip-
tion are exempt — a “150 mm thick” slab stays 150 mm in the words.

0.3 Deductions — the two-part test [GP3.2] [GP3.3]
deduct if   A_void ≥ 1.00 m²           OR          the void TOUCHES AN EDGE


Void                       Area                         At an edge?               Deduct?
Door in the middle of      1.89 m²                      no                        yes — ≥ 1.00
a wall
Vent in the middle of      0.36 m²                      no                        no
a wall
The same 0.36 m²           0.36 m²                      yes                       yes
vent, at the wall’s
end


Volume has its own threshold — 1.00 m³ [C1.3], with boxed or tubular structural metalwork
always deducted irrespective of size. The two thresholds are different numbers for different
units and are not interchangeable.

0.5 How an item is laid out — the description-and-variants structure
Present in all 31 sheets of the issued set. What varies by discipline is what the variants vary
BY — thicknesses in Concrete and Masonry, sizes in Mechanical and Electrical, widths and
types in Finishes, and named schedule references, not sizes, in Equipment and Furnish-
ings. Expect the structure; do not expect a size.

                                                            ← blank

The description is what makes the rate binding. 20mm Piping at a rate says nothing about whether
the rate covers the fittings, the valves or the supports — the paragraph above it does, and
that paragraph is what the contractor is held to. So the group is atomic and never splits
across a page: a contractor pricing page 5 cannot read page 4.

0.6 Item serial letters
A B C D E F G H J K L M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z

I and O are never used — I next to 1 and O next to 0 is exactly the confusion a priced bill
cannot afford, and the error is invisible once printed. Letters restart at A on every page
and run straight through a description-and-variants group; the variants take the next letters
in the page’s sequence, they do not restart.

Row 1 — the SPEC ROW. Bold. Item code, POMI clause and description only: no di-
mensions, no unit, no quantity. It says what the thing is — the thickness, the grade, the
build-up, the rating — and under which POMI rule it is being measured. This is where
the mandatory statements [GP5.2] [GP5.3] [GP5.4] are first fixed, before any number is taken.

Column D — the POMI clause, and why it is on the sheet Every row is measured under
a rule, and the rule is what makes the quantity defensible. A row reading
{dwg}   {level}   C-B                General raft slab: plan area {A} m2 x {t} m thick           {qty}       m3

says what was measured and where it came from, but not why that is the right way to
measure it. With the clause it does:
{dwg}   {level}   C-B    C2.1 cl.5   General raft slab: ...                                  {qty}    m3

— C2.1 class 5 measures suspended slabs by volume, stating the thickness, and that is exactly
what this row does.
    • The clause sits on the spec row, and every dimension row beneath inherits it.
    • It is restated on a dimension row only where that row is measured under a dif-
      ferent clause — an extra-over line, a deduction taken under a different limb, a class
      change.
    • A row with no clause anywhere above it is not a measurement. It is an assertion, and
      [GP1.1] says so in the other direction: an item POMI does not cover is a house extension
      and must declare itself, recorded under [GP1.2].
Without this column the answer to “why is your raft quantity that figure?” has to be recon-
structed from memory, item by item, months after the take-off was done.
Row 2 — the DIMENSION ROWS. One per location. The drawing reference in column A
is hyperlinked to the drawing, and the description narrates the calculation in words
— “{element}: plan area {A} m² × {t} m thick” — so the arithmetic can be read without
recomputing it. Qty each and Tot. are live formulas, never typed numbers.
Row 3 — the CARRY ROW. Two leading spaces, 8pt italic, the words qty to bill, and =SUM()
of the dimension rows above it. This is the figure that goes to the bill, and it is the only figure
that does.

The unit vocabulary is POMI’s, and closed
item · m · m2 · m3 · nr · kg

POMI’s own units and no others. A linear metre is m, not lm. There is no set: a set of things
is nr if it is counted and item if it is a lump. Where another unit is genuinely needed, [GP3.4]
permits it only if the amendment is stated and recorded in POMI’s Appendix under [GP1.2].

The item-code serial          The item-code serial runs:
A B C D E F G H J K L M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z        then    AA AB AC AD ...
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                 306



I and O are never used, in the take-off exactly as in the bill. I next to 1 and O next to 0 is the
confusion a priced document cannot afford, and the error is invisible once printed — every
OTHER code on the sheet still looks right, so nothing draws the eye to it.
The serial runs through the whole section tab; it does not restart per page, because the
take-off has no page rhythm. (The BILL’s letters do restart at A on every page — the two
documents differ here, deliberately.)
⚠ The issued sample deviates from this rule: eight of its seventeen tabs use O, and the General
Requirements tab uses I. Those are defects in those tabs, not the rule. A run built to this
document re-letters them.

The discipline tabs — the office scheme, and what each measures to The tabs are
lettered as the office letters them, not as POMI letters its sections. POMI remains what
the work is measured to, so every tab declares which POMI section its clauses come from.
That declaration IS the [GP1.2] amendment — without it, a tab lettered S would be measuring
against a section POMI does not have.

The pivot Columns O P Q, separated by an empty spacer column N: one row per item code, its

are never summed across units.

0.9 THE MARKUP — what proves the quantity on the drawing
A quantity that cannot be pointed at on a drawing is an assertion. Every measured element is
coloured up in its trade colour, so an unmarked element is visibly un-measured — the
drawing shows what has NOT been taken off as clearly as what has.

Three primitives cover all seventeen sections
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                308



                                                             Closure
Primitive            Units                The mark           re-derives it as     Tolerance
AREA                 m² · m³              a translucent      shoelace area /      K42 ±1%
                                          SHADED             scale²   — and ×
                                          POLYGON in the     the stated
                                          trade colour,      thickness where
                                          with the area      the unit is m³

                                          a count

The rules
   • The primitive follows the MEASURED UNIT, not the discipline. A blockwork wall
     measured in m² is an area shade; the same wall measured in m is a polyline. Three
     primitives cover all seventeen sections.
   • Every measured element is coloured up, so an UNMARKED element is visibly
     un-measured. That is the whole point of colouring up: the drawing shows what has not
     been taken off as clearly as what has.
   • The tag carries the ITEM CODE and the QUANTITY — C-B 720.00 m3 — and the item
     code matches the take-off row exactly, so the workbook and the drawing cross-reference
     BOTH ways.
   • Every marked sheet carries a LEGEND listing every item taken off that sheet: colour
     dot, item code, quantity, short description. A line that could not be placed on the drawing
     still appears in the legend, so nothing is lost — it is simply not spotted. Never invent a
     coordinate; leave it to the legend and say so.
   • Volume is an area shade × a stated thickness. There is no volume primitive. Prelim-
     inaries and PC sums are LISTED, not spotted — they have no geometry.
   • Where the measurer declared TYPE / ZONE × TIMESING, closure is on ONE IN-
     STANCE multiplied by the stated timesing. The gate is testing the type, not the building.

The closure gate — why the markup can DISAGREE build_house_takeoff.py ABORTS on
any DWG Ref cell without a markup hyperlink, and on any hyperlink whose target does not exist.
A broken link is not a cosmetic defect — it is a quantity that has stopped being traceable.
markup_closure.py EXITS NON-ZERO on any item where the geometry does not reproduce the
quantity. The batch does not close and the comment goes back to the measurer.

P+60                                               D To Collection, H =SUM() over the body rows
