The body is 46 rows and it is not a target: an item that does not fit starts the next page,
because a description-and-variants group is atomic and never splits.
BILL NO. is {bill}/{section}. PAGE NO. is {bill}/{section}/{page}, and the page number restarts at
1 for each section, not for each bill.
⚠ A bill with no sections uses the TWO-PART form {bill}/{page} — measured across the
issued set, 286 three-part codes and 17 two-part, every two-part one in the Dayworks bill,
which has no POMI section of its own because it is [GP9]. A builder that assumes three parts
cannot produce a dayworks bill.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                          311



Borders — VERTICAL RULES ONLY The page is not a ruled grid. Horizontal rules appear
only at the band boundaries. Reading down the page the rules stand at: left of A, right of
A, left of E, right of E, right of F, right of G, right of H. Reproducing this as a fully ruled
table is wrong.

Frozen strings — reproduce character for character
BILL OF QUANTITIES           ITEM               QUANTITY         To Collection
BILL NO.                     REF.               UNIT
PAGE NO.                     ITEM DESCRIPTION   RATE
                                                TOTAL PRICE
                                                AED

A section heading repeated on a later page takes (CONT'D) — upper case. An element heading
repeated takes (Cont'd) — title case. The two are different in the issued bills and both
are frozen.
Counted across the eight workbooks: (CONT'D) 155, (Cont'd) 87 — and a trailing-period variant,
(CONT'D.) 13 and (Cont'd.) 10. The period variants are a minority and are not reproduced;
they are recorded so a comparison against those sheets does not read the correct string as a
deviation.
Each section closes on its own page with LIST ANY ADDITIONAL ITEMS and its five-line paragraph,
immediately after the column-head band.

The project band — what the four rows carry                   Rows P+0 to P+3, repeated on every page.
All four are fields a run fills, never constants:

Row                  Col A                   Col D                 Col G                Col H
P+0                  {client}                BILL OF               BILL NO.             PAGE NO.
                                             QUANTITIES
P+1                  {project}
P+2                  {package}               {SECTION TITLE}       {bill}/{section}     {bill}/{section}/{page}
P+3                  {building or
                     sub-package}



The band is drawn in cells, not in Excel’s page header, and print_title_rows is deliberately
not set — the band is repeated as real rows, so a page break in the wrong place shows up as
a visibly wrong page rather than a silently right one.

The builder writes the majority for each column; the gate accepts either, because asserting
one would fail the client’s own bills. Do not substitute one for the other because they
look similar in a populated cell — they differ exactly where a bill is read hardest, at zero
and at a negative.

Non-numeric entries in the money columns — frozen strings                      The issued bills write
words where a figure would mislead:

                            Entry        In   Means
                            item         F    the unit for a lump-sum item
                            Included     H    priced within another item
                            N.A          H    not applicable to this project
                            By OSE       H    by others / owner-supplied


⚠ A checker reading a section total must not treat these as zero-value omissions. A bill row
carrying INCLUDED is priced — it is priced somewhere else.

The page break
    • No explicit row breaks. Pagination is the fixed 62-row rhythm and nothing else.
    • A description-and-variants group is ATOMIC. If it does not fit in what remains of the
      46-row body, the whole group starts the next page. A contractor pricing page 5 cannot
      read the description on page 4.
    • The body is 46 rows and it is not a target to fill.

The COLLECTION page — last page of every section The column-head band is abbre-
viated: only C = ITEM DESCRIPTION and H = TOTAL PRICE / AED. No ITEM, QUANTITY, UNIT or RATE.
SECTION {L} - {TITLE}


COLLECTION


Page {bill}/{section}/1                =H{To Collection row of page 1}
Page {bill}/{section}/2                =H{To Collection row of page 2}
...


TOTAL FOR BILL NO. {bill}/{section}/{last page} - SECTION {L} - {TITLE},
CARRIED TO SUMMARY     - {summary ref}

⚠ The TOTAL FOR ... line ends with a comma and a trailing space and continues on the next
row. CARRIED TO SUMMARY is followed by TWO spaces before the dash. Both are frozen and both
are the kind of thing a re-typing loses.

The BILL SUMMARY sheet D = SUMMARY. One row per section: C the last page code, D the
section title, H a link to that section sheet’s TOTAL FOR ... cell. Closes with:
TOTAL CARRIED TO FORM OF TENDER


The GRAND SUMMARY sheet D = GRAND SUMMARY, H page code GS. One row per bill: C = BILL
NO. {n}, D the bill title, H a link to that bill’s summary total. Closes with TOTAL CARRIED TO FORM OF
TENDER and, lower down:

AMOUNT IN WORDS


Workbook architecture              One workbook per bill. Inside it a Cover sheet precedes every
section sheet:
Cover 1 · Summary · Cover 2 · {first section} · Cover 3 · {second section} · ...

Cover sheets are A1:J38, use merged rows A{n}:I{n}, and carry the project identity only. The
Grand Summary is its own workbook and links to each bill workbook by external reference.

The money chain, end to end
item rows                 H = E x G                       quantity x rate
    -> page               To Collection = SUM(body)      P+60 of each page
      -> collection       one line per page               last page of the section
        -> bill summary      one line per section         links to TOTAL FOR ...
          -> grand summary     one line per bill          links to the bill summary total
              -> FORM OF TENDER    +   AMOUNT IN WORDS

Every link in that chain is a live reference, not a typed figure. A summary that carries a
number instead of a link is a bill that can silently disagree with itself.

0.12 What every measurement row must record
1   the POMI clause               an item with no clause is a HOUSE EXTENSION and must
                                  declare itself under [GP1.1], recorded under [GP1.2]
2    the classification           WHICH numbered class within the clause
3    N × L × W × H                each factor in its own column, never pre-multiplied
4    the deduction basis          which voids were deducted, under which limb of GP3.2/GP3.3
5    the source                   doc id, sheet, and the read tier from the extraction record
6    the DWG Ref hyperlink        to the marked-up sheet that proves it
7   the mandatory statements the clause demands — thickness, number, girth, drop,
                                  diameter basis, unit weight, average depth

A row missing 1, 4 or 6 is not a measurement. It is an assertion.

                                                     particulars, not measured work

The description block
GP is the rule set the OTHER sections are billed under. Its only lines in a bill are
the nominated sums and their profit items (GP6.1, GP7.1, GP8.1), the daywork sums and
their addition items (GP9), and contingencies (GP10.1) — all of which appear in the
PRELIMINARIES or a PROVISIONAL SUMS bill, not in a measured bill.

The priced variants under it
A   Prime cost sum for {nominated specialist work}          Sum     …
B   Add for contractor's profit                             Item    …
C   Add for attendance, as clause GP6.2                     Item    …

What POMI forces into the wording in this section
    • GP6.1/7.1/8.1 — the sum is EXCLUSIVE of profit and a SEPARATE profit item follows.
    • GP10.1 — contingencies carry NO profit item. It is the one sum that does not.
⚠ Never one line. A nominated sum is always a PAIR — sum, then profit — and where atten-
dance applies (GP6.2, GP8.2) a THIRD line. A single combined line cannot be adjusted when
the sum is expended, which is the whole point of keeping profit separate.

GP1 Principles of measurement
GP1.1    What POMI says.
     These principles of measurement provide a uniform basis for measuring bills of quan-
     tities for works of construction. More detailed information than is required by this
     document may be given to define the precise nature of work or the circumstances
     under which it is to be carried out.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              315



Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. Scope. More detail than POMI requires MAY be given — this is the clause every
HOUSE build-up is made under.

GP1.2    What POMI says.
     Amendments to these principles of measurement for use in a particular locality or
     adopted for work not envisaged by this document shall be stated; an appendix is
     provided for such amendments to be recorded.
Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. Local amendments SHALL BE STATED and recorded in POMI’s own Appendix. A
house rule not recorded there is undeclared.

GP1.3    What POMI says.
     These principles of measurement may be applied equally to the measurement of
     proposed works and of completed works.
Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. Applies equally to proposed and completed works — so the same formulae serve a
take-off and a final account.

GP2 Bills of quantities
GP2.1    What POMI says.
     The objects of bills of quantities are: 1. To assist in the accurate preparation of
     tenders, by providing for measurement of quantities on a uniform basis 2. To provide
     a basis for the financial control of a project, in accordance with the conditions of
     contract.
Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. The TWO stated objects of a bill of quantities: 1 TO ASSIST IN THE ACCURATE
PREPARATION OF TENDERS, by providing for measurement of quantities ON A UNIFORM
BASIS · 2 TO PROVIDE A BASIS FOR THE FINANCIAL CONTROL OF A PROJECT, in accor-
dance with the conditions of contract. No arithmetic — but object 2 is why a quantity must
stay traceable after award, not only until tender.

GP2.2    What POMI says.
     Bills of quantities shall describe and represent the works to be carried out; work
     which cannot be measured accurately shall be described as approximate or given in
     bills of approximate quantities.
Unit. RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. THE PROVISIONAL RULE, and it is a DUTY, not a fallback. Bills shall DESCRIBE
AND REPRESENT the works; WORK WHICH CANNOT BE MEASURED ACCURATELY SHALL
BE DESCRIBED AS APPROXIMATE, or given in bills of approximate quantities. HOUSE RULE:
WHERE THE INFORMATION IS NOT CLEAR, THE ITEM IS MARKED PROVISIONAL — never
estimated into a precise-looking figure, and never silently omitted. A provisional item carries
FOUR things: (1) the quantity as best it can be derived, (2) the word PROVISIONAL in the
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                               316



description, (3) WHY it is provisional — what is missing, which document would settle it, and
(4) the technical query raised to close it. Both failure modes are worse than the mark: an
invented precise quantity transfers a risk nobody has priced, and an omitted item is found by
the contractor after award. GP2.2 is what makes ‘I do not know’ a compliant answer.

GP2.3    What POMI says.
     Conditions of contract, drawings and specifications shall be provided with the bills
     of quantities.
Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. Conditions, drawings and specification issued with the bill.

GP2.4    What POMI says.
     The section headings and classifications do not impose restrictions upon the format
     and presentation of bills of quantities.
Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. Section headings do not restrict format — which is why a commercial heading may
differ from POMI’s, if declared.

GP3 Measurement
GP3.1    What POMI says.
     Work shall be measured net as fixed in position and each measurement shall be taken
     to the nearest 10 millimetres; this principle shall not apply to dimensions stated in
     descriptions.
Unit. RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
The formula.
d = round(d_drawn / 0.01) × 0.01

The rule. NET as fixed in position, each dimension to the nearest 10 mm. Round each dimen-
sion as taken, not the product. Dimensions in DESCRIPTIONS are exempt.

GP3.2    What POMI says.
     Unless otherwise stated, no deduction shall be made from items required to be mea-
     sured by area for voids of less than 1.00 m².
Unit. RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
The formula.
A_net = A_gross − Σ A_void   for A_void ≥ 1.00 m²

The rule. The area deduction threshold. Applies to items measured BY AREA.

GP3.3    What POMI says.
     Minimum deductions of voids shall refer only to voids within the edges of measured
     areas; voids which are at the edges of measured areas shall always be deducted,
     irrespective of size.
Unit. RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
The formula.
deduct ALL voids at an edge, any size
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                   317



The rule. The exception to GP3.2, and the one most often missed. Interior voids under 1.00
m² stay; edge voids always go.

GP3.4    What POMI says.
     These principles of measurement may be used with other units of measurement but
     the particular amendments shall be stated.
Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. Other units may be used if the amendment is stated.

GP3.5    What POMI says.
     Notwithstanding these principles of measurement, a separate minor building or
     structure may be enumerated.
Unit. NR — enumerated — a count
The formula.
N = 1 per minor building

The rule. A separate minor building or structure MAY be enumerated whole instead of mea-
sured.

GP4 Items to be fully inclusive
GP4.1    What POMI says.
     Unless otherwise stated, all items shall be fully inclusive of all that is necessary
     to fulfill the liabilities and obligations arising out of the contract and shall include:
     1. Labour and all associated costs 2. Materials, goods and all associated costs 3.
     Provision of plant 4. Temporary works 5. Establishment charges, overheads and
     profit.
Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. What EVERY rate is deemed to include, FIVE heads: 1 LABOUR AND ALL ASSO-
CIATED COSTS · 2 MATERIALS, GOODS AND ALL ASSOCIATED COSTS · 3 PROVISION OF
PLANT · 4 TEMPORARY WORKS · 5 ESTABLISHMENT CHARGES, OVERHEADS AND PROFIT.
This is THE clause that makes waste, laps, rolling margin, working space and bulking rate mat-
ters — add any of them to a quantity and the same money is billed twice.

GP5 Description of items
GP5.1    What POMI says.
     Items which are required to be enumerated, or for which an item is required, shall
     be fully described.
Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. Enumerated items and items must be FULLY DESCRIBED.

GP5.2    What POMI says.
     Items which are to be measured by length or depth shall state the cross-sectional size
     and shape, girth or ranges of girths or such other information as may be appropriate;
     for items of pipework it shall be stated whether the diameter is internal or external.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                318



Unit. RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. Length and depth items STATE the cross-sectional size and shape, girth or range
of girths. FOR PIPEWORK IT SHALL BE STATED WHETHER THE DIAMETER IS INTERNAL
OR EXTERNAL. HOUSE ELECTION: INTERNAL DIAMETER IS STATED, converting from a
nominal or external figure where the schedule gives that instead. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-
LEVERAGE STATEMENT IN AN MEP BILL: POMI expresses the Q2.2 60 mm threshold as an
INTERNAL diameter, so a pipe quoted at 65 mm EXTERNAL may be under 60 mm internal —
and a whole class of enumerated fittings appears or disappears on the basis alone. The same
threshold governs J6.3 cl.11 versus J6.4 for decoration.

GP5.3    What POMI says.
     Items which are to be measured by area shall state the thickness or such other
     information as may be appropriate.
Unit. RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. Area items STATE the thickness.

GP5.4    What POMI says.
     Items which are to be measured by weight shall state the material thickness and
     unit weight if appropriate (for example, ductwork).
Unit. RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
The formula.
W = A × m_per_m2   or   L × m_per_m   or   V × ρ

The rule. Weight items STATE the material thickness and unit weight IF APPROPRIATE —
POMI’s own example is DUCTWORK. THE QUALIFIER IS POMI’S: the statement is required
where it bears on the work, not mechanically on every weight item. It plainly IS appropriate
for sheet material sold by gauge — ductwork, sheet metal, flashings — where the thickness is
the whole difference in cost, and for rolled sections where the unit mass identifies the section.
Take the density and unit mass FROM THE SPECIFICATION OR MANUFACTURER’S DATA,
never from memory, and record the source on the row.

GP5.5    What POMI says.
     Notwithstanding these principles of measurement, proprietary items may be mea-
     sured in a manner appropriate to the manufacturer’s tariff or customary practice.
Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. Proprietary items may follow the manufacturer’s tariff — a declared departure from
the formulae here.

GP5.6    What POMI says.
     The description of items in bills of quantities may refer to other documents or draw-
     ings and any reference to such information shall be understood to fulfill any require-
     ment of these principles of measurement; alternatively, reference may be made to
     published information.
Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. A description may refer to another document, and that reference satisfies POMI’s
requirement.

GP9 Dayworks
GP9.1    What POMI says.
     The cost of labour in dayworks shall be given as a sum; alternatively, a schedule of
     the different categories of labour may be given containing a provisional quantity of
     hours for each category.
Unit. SCHEDULE
The formula.
one priced line per labour category × PROVISIONAL hours

The rule. DAYWORK LABOUR. POMI permits A SUM or, expressly, A SCHEDULE OF CATE-
GORIES carrying a PROVISIONAL QUANTITY OF HOURS for each. HOUSE ELECTION: THE
SCHEDULE. A sum is one number against one number and reveals nothing about the rates
that will be applied when daywork is ordered; a schedule prices each category, so the tender is
comparable AND the rates are fixed before anyone needs them. The hours are PROVISIONAL
by POMI’s own wording and adjust on the actual, so the schedule costs nothing in accuracy.

GP9.2    What POMI says.
     The cost of labour included in a sum or schedule shall include wages, bonuses and all
     allowances paid to operatives directly engaged on dayworks (including those operat-
     ing mechanical plant and transport) in accordance with the appropriate employment
     agreement or, where no such agreement exists, the actual payments made to the
     work people concerned.
Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. What daywork labour cost includes.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              321



GP9.3    What POMI says.
     The cost of materials in dayworks shall be given as a sum; alternatively, a schedule
     may be given containing a provisional quantity of different materials.
Unit. SCHEDULE
The formula.
one priced line per material × PROVISIONAL quantity

The rule. DAYWORK MATERIALS, as a SCHEDULE with provisional quantities — same elec-
tion as GP9.1. GP9.4 fixes the basis: the NET INVOICED PRICE, INCLUDING DELIVERY TO
SITE.

GP9.4    What POMI says.
     The cost of materials included in a sum or schedule shall be the net invoiced price,
     including delivery to site.

The rule. Daywork materials at NET INVOICED PRICE including delivery.

GP9.5    What POMI says.
     The cost of constructional plant employed exclusively in dayworks shall be given as
     a sum; alternatively, a schedule of the different categories of plant may be given
     containing a provisional quantity of hours, or such other period of time as may be

Unit. SCHEDULE
The formula.
one priced line per plant category × PROVISIONAL hours

The rule. DAYWORK PLANT, as a SCHEDULE with provisional hours — same election as
GP9.1. NOTE THE WORD ‘EXCLUSIVELY’: only plant employed EXCLUSIVELY in dayworks

and insurance.

one addition item against EACH of the three schedules
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                       322



The rule. An item for the addition of establishment charges, overheads and profit TO EACH of
the sums or schedules of labour, materials and plant. THE WORD IS ‘EACH’ — three schedules
produce THREE addition items, so a daywork section is SIX blocks, not four: labour schedule +
its addition, materials schedule + its addition, plant schedule + its addition. A single combined
addition cannot be applied when only one of the three is expended.

The description block
Section A is billed as one ITEM per group, each carrying POMI's own list of heads as its
description. The description IS the list — that is what the contractor prices against.
Where the employer has specified the nature or extent (A7.2, A8.2, A9.2), or imposed a
restriction (A3.1) or required a facility (A6.1), the PARTICULARS are stated in the
description of the item they affect.

SECTION B — SITE WORK
26 groups · 95 clauses · 65 carrying arithmetic

How this section is TAKEN OFF
The spec row says what the thing is
{depth / classification / destination} — e.g. 'to underside of raft blinding formation, maximum depth not exceeding {d}

The dimension rows narrate the calculation
Bulk excavation to {formation}: {element} plan area {A} m2 x {d} m deep
EO deepening to {element}: {element} area {A} m2 x {d} m
Surplus = total cut ({a}+{b}+{c}={T}) less selected re-use {r}

The arithmetic. Qty each = G*I for a plan area x depth; the surplus line narrates the sub-
traction IN FULL so the reconciliation is readable on the sheet.
⚠ B is where the narration earns its place. B11 disposal must EQUAL total excavation, so
the disposal row spells out the arithmetic — every cut added, the re-use subtracted — and a
checker verifies the equality by reading, without opening another tab. Extra-over items are
prefixed ‘EO’ so that B8.5 and B15.2 are visibly extra over and not deductions.

How this section is MARKED UP

Trade colour                                          brown
Primitive                                             AREA for excavation, fill and paving ·
                                                      LINEAR for trenches, kerbs and fencing ·
                                                      TAG for trial holes, boreholes, trees, piles
                                                      and drainage accessories
Call-out tag                                          B-{serial} {qty} {unit} — and for extra-over
                                                      items the tag reads EO, so the reviewer sees it
                                                      is measured OVER the shade beneath it, not
                                                      cut out of it


What carries a mark. the excavation footprint at each formation level, each as its own shade;
the deepening zones separately; the fill footprint; the paved areas; every service and drain
trench as a polyline; every pile, gully, chamber, isolated tree and special fence post as a tag.
⚠ The extra-over items must be marked ON TOP OF the base shade, not instead of it.
Rock under B8.5, deepening under B9, boring through rock under B15.2 — each is a second,
overlapping mark. A markup that replaces the base shade with the extra-over shade is drawing
the error that B8.5 exists to prevent. And B9.2 service trenches are a POLYLINE only — no
separate disposal or backfill mark, because there is no separate quantity.

     over excavation (that is, the volume of rock shall be measured but no deduction shall
     be made from the volume of excavation in which the rock occurs).
Unit. M3 — by volume, cubic metres
The formula.
ROUTE A    V_soil = V_total − V_rock   (two items, summing to the total)
ROUTE B    V_excavation = V_total UNCHANGED
           V_rock       = measured AS WELL

The rule. Excavation in rock. POMI’S PRIMARY LIMB IS ‘SHALL BE SO DESCRIBED’ — rock
described as its own excavation item, the two summing to the total. EXTRA OVER IS THE
EXPRESS ALTERNATIVE, and it is the HOUSE ELECTION: the volume of rock is measured
but NO DEDUCTION is made from the excavation in which it occurs. Under the elected route
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                334



the base dig stays whole, which matters because rock is FOUND, not designed. DEDUCTING
THE ROCK FROM THE EXCAVATION LOSES THE BASE ITEM — the same error as B15.2 rock
boring, D2.2 faced work and G2.3 special sheets, and the one people reverse. B8.6 defines
rock, and it is an OPINION, not a geological test.

B8.6   What POMI says.
     For the purposes of measurement rock is defined as any material met with which is
     of such size or position that, in the opinion of the employer’s representative, it can
     only be removed by means of wedges, special plant or explosives.
Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. Definition of rock: removable only by wedges, special plant or explosives, in the
employer’s representative’s opinion.

B9 Excavation
B9.1   What POMI says.
     Unless otherwise stated, excavation shall be measured by volume as the void which
     is to be occupied by the permanent construction, or vertically above any part of
     the permanent construction, classified as follows: 1. Oversite excavation to remove
     top soil, stating the average depth 2. Excavation to reduce levels 3. Excavation in
     cuttings 4. Basement excavation 5. Trench excavation to receive foundations, which
     shall include pile caps and ground beams 6. Pit excavation to receive foundation
     bases, stating the number 7. Excavation for diaphragm walls, stating the width of
     the permanent construction and the type of support fluid.
Unit. M3 — by volume, cubic metres
The formula.
V = N × L × W × D

The rule. Excavation as the VOID TO BE OCCUPIED by the permanent construction, or
vertically above any part of it — L and W are the PERMANENT CONSTRUCTION’s dimensions,
not the dig’s. SEVEN classes: 1 OVERSITE EXCAVATION to remove top soil, STATING THE
AVERAGE DEPTH · 2 EXCAVATION TO REDUCE LEVELS · 3 EXCAVATION IN CUTTINGS ·
4 BASEMENT EXCAVATION · 5 TRENCH EXCAVATION to receive foundations, which SHALL
INCLUDE PILE CAPS AND GROUND BEAMS · 6 PIT EXCAVATION to receive foundation bases,
STATING THE NUMBER · 7 EXCAVATION FOR DIAPHRAGM WALLS, STATING THE WIDTH
of the permanent construction AND THE TYPE OF SUPPORT FLUID. Three classes carry a
mandatory statement: 1 average depth, 6 the number, 7 width and support fluid.

B9.2   What POMI says.
     Excavation of trenches for service pipes, drain pipes, cables or the like shall each
     be measured by length, stating the average depth; disposal and filling shall be un-
     derstood to be included.
Unit. M — by length, metres
The formula.
Len = Σ L, per trench type
d_avg STATED

The rule. Trenches for service pipes, drain pipes, cables or the like shall EACH be measured
BY LENGTH — ‘each’ meaning ONE ITEM PER TRENCH TYPE, not one combined trench item
— STATING THE AVERAGE DEPTH. DISPOSAL AND FILLING ARE DEEMED INCLUDED, so
NOTHING ELSE is measured for that trench: no disposal row under B11, no filling row under
B12, no earthwork support. A drainage trench carrying all three has been paid three times
for one operation, and it is the most double-counted item in a site-work bill.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                               335

The rule. Tunnel excavation is B24, not B9.

B11 Disposal
B11.1    What POMI says.
     Disposal of material arising from excavation, dredging or tunnelling shall be mea-
     sured by volume as equal to the volume of excavation, dredging or tunnelling and
     each shall be classified as follows: 1. Backfilled into excavation 2. Backfilled in
     making up levels 3. Backfilled oversite to make up levels, giving details of special
     contouring, embankments or the like 4. Removed, which shall include providing a
     suitable tip.
Unit. M3 — by volume, cubic metres
The formula.
V_disposal = V_excavation   (EXACTLY)

The rule. Disposal EQUALS the excavation, dredging or tunnelling volume EXACTLY — no
bulking, no shrinkage. FOUR classes, each measured separately: 1 BACKFILLED INTO EX-
CAVATION · 2 BACKFILLED IN MAKING UP LEVELS · 3 BACKFILLED OVERSITE TO MAKE
UP LEVELS, GIVING DETAILS of special contouring, embankments or the like · 4 REMOVED,
which SHALL INCLUDE PROVIDING A SUITABLE TIP — so tipping charges are in the rate,
never a separate item.

B12 Filling
B12.1    What POMI says.
     Filling material (other than that arising from excavation, dredging or tunnelling)
     shall be measured by volume as equal to the void to be filled, classified as follows:
     1. Filled into excavation 2. Filled in making up levels 3. Filled oversite to make up
     levels, giving details of special contouring, embankments or the like.
Unit. M3 — by volume, cubic metres
The formula.
V_fill = V_void_to_be_filled

The rule. Filling material OTHER THAN that arising from excavation, dredging or tunnelling
— so IMPORTED fill only; site-won material returned is B11 ‘backfilled’, and the test is WHERE
THE MATERIAL CAME FROM. Measured as EQUAL TO THE VOID TO BE FILLED — the de-
signed void, not the loose volume delivered. THREE classes: 1 FILLED INTO EXCAVATION
· 2 FILLED IN MAKING UP LEVELS · 3 FILLED OVERSITE TO MAKE UP LEVELS, GIVING
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                             336



DETAILS OF SPECIAL CONTOURING, EMBANKMENTS OR THE LIKE. Note there is NO ‘re-
moved’ class, the asymmetry with B11’s four: imported material is not taken away. If you
want to bill ‘filling — removed’, you are in the wrong clause.

SECTION C — CONCRETE WORK
7 groups · 36 clauses · 25 carrying arithmetic

How this section is TAKEN OFF
The spec row says what the thing is
{thickness} {element} — e.g. '600 mm thick general raft', '250/280 mm thick slabs to typical floors'

The dimension rows narrate the calculation
General raft slab: plan area {A} m2 x {t} m thick
Shear walls {ref}-{ref}: {L} m x {h} m ht x {t} m thick
Typical floor slab {t1}/{t2} mm: {A} m2 x {t_avg} m average

The arithmetic. Qty each = GI for area x thickness, = GH*I for length x height x thickness.
Nr carries the FLOOR COUNT — 4 typical floors is Nr = 4, not four rows.
⚠ The spec row carries the THICKNESS because GP5.3 makes it a mandatory statement in
the bill, and the take-off is where it is first fixed. Where a slab has two thicknesses the spec
row states both and the dimension row states the average actually used — so the averaging
is visible, not buried.

How this section is MARKED UP

Trade colour                                        blue
Primitive                                           AREA for slabs, beds and walls in elevation ·
                                                    TAG for columns and isolated bases
Call-out tag                                        C-{serial} {qty} m3 — the label states the
                                                    thickness, because the shade is an AREA and
                                                    the volume is that area × the thickness


What carries a mark. every slab by level as a shaded polygon with its thickness in the label;
thickened zones and drops as separate overlapping shades; walls and cores in plan; every
column and isolated base as a tag; each formwork face as its own shade where formwork is
marked separately.
⚠ A volume mark is an area × a STATED thickness, and the thickness must be in the
label — otherwise the closure test has nothing to multiply by and the mark cannot be checked.
Beams under C2.1 cl.8 are measured BELOW the slab, so a beam mark must show the beam
zone, not the full depth through the slab; mark the slab and the beam as two shades, never
one.

The rule. Poured concrete by VOLUME, ELEVEN classes: 1 FOUNDATIONS, which IN-

C2.3   What POMI says.
     Where an item is required to be measured by volume and the thickness stated, then
     items of differing thickness may be grouped together, provided that the range of the
     different thicknesses is stated.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              350



Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. Differing thicknesses MAY be GROUPED provided the RANGE is stated. HOUSE
RULE: grouping is used, but ONLY WITHIN ONE CONSTRUCTION STAGE — substructure,
superstructure, roof. Items are never grouped ACROSS stages, because a 200 mm raft and
a 200 mm roof slab do not price alike and a range spanning them tells a tenderer nothing.
Grouping removes the individual thickness statement C2.1 cl.4, cl.5 and cl.6 require, so the
stated range is what carries that duty and it must be tight.

C3 Reinforcement
C3.1   What POMI says.
     The weight of bar reinforcement shall be the net weight without addition for rolling
     margin, supports, spacers or tying wire.
Unit. KG — by weight, kilogrammes
The formula.
W = Σ (N_bars × L_bar_INCLUDING_LAPS × m_per_m(Ø))

The rule. THE NET WEIGHT RULE, and read its exclusion list EXACTLY: no addition for
ROLLING MARGIN, SUPPORTS, SPACERS or TYING WIRE. LAPS ARE NOT IN THAT LIST.
A lap is steel fixed in position, so under GP3.1 it IS measured — and the contrast with C3.3,
which excludes laps from FABRIC in terms, proves the omission here is deliberate. WHAT
IS FORBIDDEN is a BLANKET PERCENTAGE UPLIFT with no derivation. HOUSE RULE ON
THE SOURCE: reinforcement is MEASURED FROM THE SECTION DRAWINGS, never from
a bar bending schedule. N_bars = (L_run / spacing) + 1 read off the section; each lap derived
from the SPECIFIED LAP LENGTH (k x diameter) at the positions the section shows. A BBS,
where one is later issued, is a CROSS-CHECK ONLY — reconcile and record the variance,
raise a technical query on a real difference, but do not adopt the schedule’s figure. Chairs,
spacers and tying wire remain excluded at all times.

C3.2   What POMI says.
     Bar reinforcement shall be measured by weight, stating the diameter; bars of differ-
     ing diameters shall be given separately.
Unit. KG — by weight, kilogrammes
The formula.
W = Σ N_bars × L_bar × m_per_m(Ø)
m_per_m = (π/4) × Ø² × 7850 / 1e6

The rule. Bar reinforcement, STATING THE DIAMETER. Differing diameters GIVEN SEPA-
RATELY — never a blended tonnage.

C3.3   What POMI says.
     Fabric reinforcement shall be measured by area, without addition for laps.
Unit. M2 — by area, square metres
The formula.
A = A_covered, NO addition for laps

The rule. Fabric reinforcement. A lap covers the same square metre twice.

A = Σ A_contact

The rule. Shuttering as the NET AREA IN CONTACT with the finished face of the concrete,
ELEVEN classes: 1 SOFFITS — soffits of special construction SO DESCRIBED · 2 SLOPING
SOFFITS, which INCLUDE SOFFITS OF STAIRCASES · 3 SLOPING UPPER SURFACES, which

C4.3      What POMI says.
     Grooves, which shall include throats, rebates, chamfers or the like, 2500 mm2 sec-
     tional area or over shall be measured by length; grooves less than 2500 mm2 sec-
     tional area shall be understood to be included.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              352



Unit. M — by length, metres
The formula.
if sectional area ≥ 2500 mm² → Len = Σ L
if sectional area <   2500 mm² → DEEMED INCLUDED

The rule. THE 2500 mm² THRESHOLD. Grooves — which INCLUDE throats, rebates and
CHAMFERS — of 2500 mm² SECTIONAL AREA OR OVER are measured by length; under that
they are DEEMED INCLUDED. COMPUTE THE SECTIONAL AREA FROM THE SHAPE, NOT
FROM THE LEG DIMENSIONS. A chamfer is a TRIANGLE: 50 x 50 mm legs give ½ × 50 ×
50 = 1250 mm², which is UNDER the threshold and therefore FREE. A chamfer only reaches
2500 mm² at about 71 x 71 mm legs. A rebate or a throat is rectangular, so 50 x 50 there
IS 2500 mm² and is measured. Reading the leg dimensions as the area bills a whole class of
chamfers POMI deems included.

How this section is TAKEN OFF
The spec row says what the thing is

The dimension rows narrate the calculation

The arithmetic. Qty each = G*I. Openings are a SEPARATE NEGATIVE row, never netted
silently.
⚠ Deductions get their own row. GP3.2/GP3.3 make the deduction a decision — over or under
1.00 m2, interior or at an edge — and a decision that leaves no row cannot be checked. Where
the cavity-wall method (D2.1 cl.3) is composite, say so on the spec row.

where the skins are measured separately, each skin gets its own shade. Never both on one

The rule. Arches BY LENGTH. THAT IS THE WHOLE CLAUSE — POMI states no basis along

girth is the line the work actually follows and both the span and the intrados understate it.
This is the HOUSE’s basis, not POMI’s, and it is recorded in the Appendix under GP1.2. GP5.2
separately requires the cross-sectional size or girth to be STATED in the description.

What POMI forces into the wording in this section

    • E2.1 cl.5 — roof trusses STATE THE NUMBER.

      them.
⚠ Classes 4 and 5 carry a NUMBER as well as a weight, and the number belongs in the variant

E1 Generally
E1.1    What POMI says.
      The weight of metalwork shall be the net weight, without addition for rolling margin
      or welding material and without deduction for holes, splay cuts, notches or the like.
Unit. KG — by weight, kilogrammes
The formula.
W = Σ (N × L_gross × m_per_m(section))
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                361



The rule. THE NET WEIGHT RULE, and it cuts BOTH ways. NO ADDITION for rolling margin
or welding material — a fabricator’s own tonnage adds both, because that is what he buys and
consumes, and both are RATE matters under GP4.1. NO DEDUCTION for holes, splay cuts,
notches or the like — a careful measurer deducts them because they are visibly not steel, and
POMI forbids that too. The two errors pull in opposite directions and partially cancel, so a
wrong figure can foot to about the right total, which is exactly why neither gets caught. It is
the GROSS SECTION over the GROSS LENGTH: a beam notched at both ends and drilled for
twelve bolts is still its full length at its full unit mass.

E1.2   What POMI says.
     Welded, riveted or bolted work shall each be so described.

The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. Welded, riveted or bolted work EACH SO DESCRIBED.

The formula.

The rule. Protective treatment. POMI SAYS AN ITEM. HOUSE AMENDMENT, DECLARED
UNDER GP1.2 AND RECORDED IN POMI’S APPENDIX: it is MEASURED BY AREA. The
treated surface is the cost driver — a galvanising or intumescent system prices per square
metre, and the surface area of a tonne of steel varies several-fold between a heavy stanchion
and a light truss. An item forces the tenderer to compute that area himself and price a risk he
cannot see, and it cannot be valued on variation. The AREA is measured; the SYSTEM stays
in the description. Surface area is the developed girth of the section times its length, plus the
area of any plates and cleats.

F1.2    What POMI says.

Unit. RULE — governs how OTHER quantities are calculated
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. Descriptions SHALL STATE whether sizes are BASIC (before machining) or FIN-

K1 Generally
K1.1    What POMI says.
      For the purposes of identification, accessories to be measured in accordance with

Unit. — — no arithmetic — a descriptive, definitional or administrative rule
The formula. None — this clause carries no arithmetic.
The rule. THE DEFINITION, and it is a RESIDUAL: accessories are specially manufactured or
proprietary items NOT INCLUDED IN OTHER SECTIONS. SO K IS TESTED LAST — an item
reaches K only after Q, R, H, J and every other section has been tested and none of them takes
it. Reaching for K early pulls work out of the sections that price it properly. HOUSE RULE:
BECAUSE THE SECTION IS DEFINED BY EXCLUSION, EVERY K ITEM MUST BE FULLY
DESCRIBED — what the thing is, what it is made of, how it is fixed, and the schedule or type
reference it comes from. A section defined by what it is not cannot rely on its heading to say
what an item is; only the description can.

K1.2    What POMI says.

Unit. NR — enumerated — a count
The formula.
N = count

The rule. Unless otherwise stated, accessories ENUMERATED — the section’s default, and
‘unless otherwise stated’ is the licence for K2.1’s length. Everything not caught by K2 falls to
this count, FULLY DESCRIBED under GP5.1 and under the K1.1 house rule: the description
is the only thing identifying an item in a section defined by exclusion.

Unit. KG — by weight, kilogrammes
The formula.
girth = 2 × (w + d)
A = L_centreline × girth + Σ A_blank_ends
W = A × m_per_m2(gauge)

The rule. RECTANGULAR ductwork BY WEIGHT, from an area built on NOMINAL dimensions.

What POMI forces into the wording in this section

0.13 PROVISIONAL — what to do when the information is not clear
[GP2.2] is a duty, not a fallback: bills shall describe and represent the works, and work which
cannot be measured accurately SHALL BE DESCRIBED AS APPROXIMATE, or given in
bills of approximate quantities.
Where the information is not clear, the item is marked PROVISIONAL. Never estimated
into a precise-looking figure, and never silently omitted. Both failure modes are worse than
the mark:

                                                 What happens
Invented precision                               a risk nobody has priced is transferred to the
                                                 contractor, and nothing on the face of the bill
                                                 says so
Silent omission                                  the contractor finds it after award, when it is
                                                 a claim rather than a quantity


A provisional item carries four things:
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                  403



1   the quantity            as best it can be derived from what IS available
2    the word PROVISIONAL   in the description, not in a footnote
3   WHY                     what is missing, and which document would settle it
4    the technical query    raised to close it, by its TQ reference

⚠ [GP2.2] is what makes “I do not know” a compliant answer. An item marked provisional
with its reason and its query is POMI-compliant. A confident wrong number is not.
⚠ The take-off row says so too. Where the extraction chain returns SCALE_UNVERIFIED or ABSENT,
or a schedule is not issued, the row is provisional and the POMI clause column carries GP2.2
alongside the measurement clause.

0.14 DAYWORKS — six blocks, not four
[GP9] gives dayworks nine clauses. The shape is three cost heads, each with its own addition
item:

                                     The schedule                      Its addition
Labour                               [GP9.1] categories ×              [GP9.7]
                                     provisional hours
Materials                            [GP9.3] materials ×               [GP9.7]
                                     provisional quantities
Plant                                [GP9.5] categories ×              [GP9.7]
                                     provisional hours


Daywork Labour         one priced line per category    x provisional hours
    + Item: addition of establishment charges, overheads and profit
Daywork Materials      one priced line per material   x provisional quantity
    + Item: addition of establishment charges, overheads and profit
Daywork Plant          one priced line per category    x provisional hours
    + Item: addition of establishment charges, overheads and profit

⚠ [GP9.7] says the addition is given to EACH of the sums or schedules. Three schedules
produce three addition items. A single combined addition cannot be applied when only one
of the three is expended.
What each rate covers, fixed by POMI:

Clause                                                The basis
[GP9.2]                                               labour: wages, bonuses and all allowances
                                                      to operatives directly engaged, including
                                                      those operating plant and transport, per the

[GP9.6]                                               plant: fuel, consumable stores, repairs,

⚠ [GP9.5] says EXCLUSIVELY. Only plant employed exclusively in dayworks belongs here.
Plant shared with the permanent works is an overhead under [GP9.8] cl.4 and must not appear
in the daywork schedule at all.
⚠ Dayworks sits with the preliminaries, not in a measured bill — it has no POMI section

into exactly one of three kinds, and each is disclosed differently:

                                   the house has picked one       is being followed — but a
