AMENDMENTS — 3
E2.6 POMI says. Protective treatment to structural metalwork SHALL BE GIVEN AS AN
ITEM.
The house does. Protective treatment is MEASURED BY AREA.
Why. The treated area is the cost driver — a galvanising or intumescent system prices per
square metre of surface, and the surface area of a tonne of steel varies by a factor of several
between a heavy stanchion and a light truss. An item forces the tenderer to compute the
area himself from the same drawings, price a risk he cannot see, and it cannot be valued on
variation. The area is measured; the SYSTEM stays in the description.

take-off tabs J1 / N / S POMI says. POMI letters its sections A B C D E F G H J K L M N P Q
R. K is Accessories, M is Furnishings, N is Special Construction, and THERE IS NO SECTION
S.
The house does. The take-off carries the office’s own tabs: J1 ID FINISHES (a sub-tab of J),
N FURNISHINGS (POMI’s M), and S COMMS & ELV (inside POMI’s R).
Why. The tabs follow how the packages are let and priced, not how POMI letters its sections.
POMI remains what the work is MEASURED to, so every tab declares its POMI section and ev-
ery row carries its POMI clause. Without that declaration a tab lettered S would be measuring
against a section POMI does not have.

                POMI says. POMI gives EQUIPMENT its own section, L, distinct from
Section L placement
FURNISHINGS at M.
The house does. There is NO L TAB. Equipment arrives as a supplied schedule and is billed
straight into the N tab alongside furnishings.
Why. The two arrive together on these projects, as one schedule from one supplier, and
splitting them across two tabs splits one procurement package. The distinction is not lost:
EVERY ROW DECLARES ITS OWN POMI CLAUSE, so an L1.2 equipment item and an M1.2
furnishing item are distinguishable on the sheet and in the bill even though they share a tab.

ELECTIONS — 42
D2.1 cl.3  POMI says. Cavity walls measured as a COMPOSITE ITEM including skins and
cavity; ALTERNATIVELY the skins and cavity may EACH be measured by area.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                405



The house does. THE COMPOSITE ITEM. One area at one description carrying the whole
build-up.
Why. It prices as one operation, and a composite description carries the whole build-up where
a checker can see it. What matters more than the choice is that the bill states it: a cross-check
written for the composite method reads a correct skin-by-skin take-off as a double count.

D2.2 POMI says. Faced or fair faced work SO DESCRIBED; ALTERNATIVELY measured as
EXTRA OVER walls.
The house does. EXTRA OVER. The wall area stays whole and the faced area is measured
AS WELL, STATING WHETHER ONE SIDE OR BOTH.
Why. It keeps one wall quantity for the whole elevation and prices the facing against it, which
is how the work is actually carried out. NO DEDUCTION is made from the walling — the same
discipline as B8.5 rock, B15.2 rock boring and G2.3 special sheets.

D4.1 POMI says. Fabric reinforcement to masonry measured in accordance with Section C
by AREA; ALTERNATIVELY by LENGTH.
The house does. BY LENGTH for bed-joint reinforcement.
Why. Brick-force is bought, laid and paid by the metre of bed joint. An area for a strip a few
centimetres wide is a number nobody prices against.

C2.3 POMI says. Items of differing thickness MAY be grouped together, PROVIDED THAT
THE RANGE of the different thicknesses is stated.
The house does. Grouping is used, but ONLY WITHIN ONE CONSTRUCTION STAGE —
substructure, superstructure, roof. Never across stages.
Why. A 200 mm raft and a 200 mm roof slab do not price alike, so a range spanning them
tells a tenderer nothing. Grouping removes the individual thickness statement C2.1 cl.4, cl.5
and cl.6 require, so the stated range is what carries that duty and it must be tight.

E3.2 / E3.3 POMI says. Handrails measured BY LENGTH, EXCEPT WHERE INCLUDED
WITH A STAIRCASE. Staircases enumerated.
The house does. The handrail is a SEPARATE LENGTH ITEM, and the enumerated staircase
is DESCRIBED AS EXCLUDING IT.
Why. This is POMI’s own exception read the other way, and it is within the clause: the handrail
is only inside the staircase where the bill puts it there. Separating them prices the two properly
— a stair balustrade is a different trade and a different rate from the stair. THE STAIRCASE
DESCRIPTION MUST SAY ‘excluding handrail’ or the two readings collide and the handrail is
either billed twice or not at all.

F5.1 POMI says. Framework shall be measured by AREA, TAKEN OVERALL; ALTERNA-
TIVELY it may be measured by LENGTH.
The house does. AREA, TAKEN OVERALL.
Why. A stud framework is a surface. Measuring the studs by length over-measures for the
same reason open-spaced battens do under F4.1, and it puts the item in a unit that cannot be
summed with the area items around it.

F6.3 POMI says. Shelving shall be measured by AREA; ALTERNATIVELY it may be measured
by LENGTH.
The house does. BY LENGTH, with the depth stated in the description under GP5.2.
Why. Shelving is bought and fixed by the running metre at a stated depth. An area for a 300
mm shelf is a number nobody prices against.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                            406



F6.6 POMI says. Plastic coverings shall be DESCRIBED WITH THE ITEM on which they
occur, STATING WHETHER ON ONE OR MORE FACES; ALTERNATIVELY they may be mea-
sured separately by area.
The house does. DESCRIBED WITH THE ITEM.
Why. This is POMI’s primary limb. A laminated worktop is a worktop described as laminated
on the top and front edge, not a worktop plus an area of laminate. ‘One or more faces’ stays
a MANDATORY STATEMENT either way — it is the difference between one face and four at
the same running length.

G3.1 POMI says. Damp-proof courses shall be measured by LENGTH; ALTERNATIVELY they
may be measured by AREA.
The house does. BY LENGTH, with the WIDTH stated in the description under GP5.2.
Why. A DPC is bought and laid by the roll at a stated width. The width is then a mandatory
statement, not a courtesy — a length with no width is not a quantity anyone can price.

G4.1POMI says. Insulation shall be measured by AREA; ALTERNATIVELY it may be DE-
SCRIBED WITH items of composite roofing.
The house does. A SEPARATE AREA ITEM.
Why. It keeps the insulation visible on the face of the bill and valuable on variation, where
the alternative buries it in the roofing rate. The two limbs are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE: a
composite roofing item whose description mentions insulation, plus a separate insulation area,
bills it twice — and the second row reads perfectly reasonably.

G2.2 POMI says. Eaves, ridges, skirtings, fascias, flashings and aprons shall be measured
by LENGTH; ALTERNATIVELY, skirtings, fascias or the like TO COMPOSITE ROOFING may
be measured by AREA.
The house does. LENGTH THROUGHOUT — the alternative is not used.
Why. One trim unit for the whole section rather than two. The alternative is narrow in any
case: skirtings and fascias only, and only to composite roofing. It never reaches flashings,
ridges or aprons.

G2.3 POMI says. Roof lights, ventilators, soaker collars and special roofing sheets shall be
ENUMERATED; ALTERNATIVELY, SPECIAL ROOFING SHEETS may be measured as EXTRA
OVER roofing.
The house does. ENUMERATE ALL FOUR. Extra over is not used.
Why. The counts are unambiguous, and extra over is the limb that gets mis-applied — the same
no-deduction discipline as B8.5, B15.2 and D2.2, and the one people reverse. The alternative
never reached roof lights, ventilators or soaker collars in any case.

H1.2 POMI says. Jambs, heads, sills, mullions and transomes shall be measured by LENGTH;
ALTERNATIVELY, FRAME AND LINING SETS may be ENUMERATED.
The house does. ENUMERATED SETS, each fully described under GP5.1.
Why. Door schedules are issued as types, so a set per type keeps one bill line per schedule
row and survives a schedule revision. With no length in the item the DESCRIPTION is the
only thing saying how big the frame is, so it must carry the girth and the material.

H3.1 POMI says. Screens, borrowed lights and curtain walling shall be measured by AREA;
ALTERNATIVELY they may be ENUMERATED.
The house does. BY AREA.
Why. Curtain walling prices per square metre. A ‘1 nr curtain wall’ cannot be priced, cannot
be valued on variation, and cannot be compared between tenderers.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              407



H5.3 POMI says. Glass louvres shall be ENUMERATED; ALTERNATIVELY they may be mea-
sured by LENGTH, STATING THE NUMBER.
The house does. ENUMERATED.
Why. The count is the quantity and it reconciles against the window schedule. Note the
alternative never permits length alone — the number is mandatory under either limb.

           POMI says. Units or sets of ironmongery shall be ENUMERATED. The clause
H4.1 / F10.1
appears TWICE in POMI, word for word, at H4.1 and at F10.1.
The house does. ALL ironmongery is billed under H4.1, whatever the door is made of. F10.1
is never used.
Why. The two clauses are identical, so ironmongery to a timber door could legitimately be
billed in either section — and if the office uses both, the sets get counted twice across two
bills with nothing on the face of either showing it. One home for every set.

J4.1  POMI says. Non-slip inserts, dividing strips, metal angle beads and lathing at junc-
tions of differing backgrounds shall be measured by LENGTH; ALTERNATIVELY, they may be
DESCRIBED WITH THE ITEMS IN WHICH THEY OCCUR.
The house does. DESCRIBED WITH THE ITEM. No separate linear item is raised.
Why. Consistent with the F6.6 treatment of plastic coverings, and it keeps a finishes bill from
carrying a linear item for every bead. THE FINISH DESCRIPTION MUST NAME THEM —
beads, stops, dividing strips, lathing at junctions — or the rate is not bound to anything. The
two limbs are mutually exclusive: a bead length plus a description mentioning beads bills
them twice.

L1.2 POMI says. Each category of equipment shall be given as an ITEM; ALTERNATIVELY,
individual items of equipment may be ENUMERATED.
The house does. ENUMERATED. Category-as-an-item is never used.
Why. An ‘Item’ for laboratory or kitchen equipment prices nothing, compares between ten-
derers on nothing, and cannot be valued on variation. Equipment arrives as a schedule, so a
count against that schedule is both available and checkable.

M1.2  POMI says. Each category of furnishing shall be given as an ITEM; ALTERNATIVELY,
individual items may be ENUMERATED or MEASURED BY LENGTH, as may be appropriate.
The house does. ENUMERATED for discrete items, BY LENGTH for continuous ones.
Category-as-an-item is never used.
Why. Same reason as L1.2. Curtains and blinds are continuous and price by the metre; chairs
and rugs are discrete and price by the number.

N3.1 POMI says. Installations of a specialist nature shall EACH BE GIVEN AS AN ITEM;
ALTERNATIVELY, they may be MEASURED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE RELEVANT SEC-
TIONS.
The house does. MEASURED TO THE RELEVANT SECTIONS — and the DESCRIPTION
carries the specialist nature, naming the installation the item belongs to and the specification
clause that governs it.
Why. Measuring to the relevant sections prices against known work rather than a lump. But
the measurement moving section must not move the SPECIFICATION with it: radiation shield-
ing measured as lead-lined boarding under F is priced as ordinary boarding unless the words
say what it is. THE MEASUREMENT MOVES SECTION; THE SPECIFICATION DOES NOT.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                               408



P3.2 / J6.3 cl.11 and cl.12  POMI says. Protective and decorative painting to conveying
systems shall be given as AN ITEM FOR EACH SYSTEM. J6.3 cl.11 (large pipes, trunking) and
cl.12 (structural metalwork) measure decoration by AREA, in each case ‘UNLESS MEASURED
AS INCIDENTAL WORK’.
The house does. MEP PAINTING IS BILLED IN THE MEP SECTIONS — P3.2, and its Q and
R counterparts. J6.3 cl.11 and cl.12 are NOT used for anything inside an MEP package.
Why. POMI’s own qualifier makes this an election, not a conflict: under this election MEP
painting IS incidental work, so the J6.3 classes stand down. The two overlap by design and
billing both double-pays — with both rows reading correctly, which is why it survives a check.

P2.1 / Q8.1 / R9.1  POMI says. An item shall be given for each of five sundries — supports, iden-
tification, testing and commissioning, tools and spares, documents. The same list is adopted
by Section Q and by Section R.
The house does. EACH MEP SECTION CARRIES ITS OWN SET OF FIVE. They are not
consolidated across the MEP package.
Why. Conveying, mechanical and electrical are let and priced as separate packages, often to
separate specialists. One consolidated set of five could not be apportioned between them, and
could not be valued when one package varies.

Q1.2 POMI says. Installations shall be MEASURED in accordance with the relevant clauses
of this section; ALTERNATIVELY, they may be ENUMERATED ON A LOCATIONAL BASIS.
The house does. MEASURED.
Why. The locational alternative dissolves the section into counts that price nothing a checker
can test and cannot be valued when the layout changes.

Q5.3  POMI says. Sensing and activating devices, control panels, air compressors and re-
ceivers shall be ENUMERATED (Q5.1); ALTERNATIVELY, automatic control systems shall be
GIVEN AS AN ITEM FOR EACH INSTALLATION, BUT EQUIPMENT COMMON TO MORE
THAN ONE SYSTEM SHALL BE ENUMERATED.
The house does. AN ITEM PER INSTALLATION — with the clause’s own exception applied
in full: SHARED EQUIPMENT IS STILL ENUMERATED.
Why. Controls are let as a specialist package against a functional specification, so an item per
installation matches how the work is bought. The exception is not optional and it is the part
that gets dropped: a shared control panel, compressor or receiver serving two installations
must be counted separately, or it sits inside one installation’s item and the others are priced
without it.

GP5.2 — pipework diameter basis POMI says. For items of pipework IT SHALL BE STATED
WHETHER THE DIAMETER IS INTERNAL OR EXTERNAL. POMI does not say which to use.
The house does. INTERNAL DIAMETER, converted from a nominal or external figure where
the schedule gives that instead.
Why. POMI expresses the Q2.2 60 mm fittings threshold as an INTERNAL diameter, so stating
any other basis puts the bill and the rule on different measures. A pipe quoted at 65 mm
EXTERNAL may be under 60 mm internal, and a whole class of enumerated fittings appears
or disappears on the basis alone. The same threshold governs J6.3 cl.11 against J6.4.

Q6.1 / R8.1  POMI says. Connections to supply mains shall be ENUMERATED, SUBJECT TO
CLAUSE GP8. GP8.1 makes work which may only be carried out by a government or public
authority a SUM exclusive of profit, with a separate profit item, and GP8.2 adds an attendance
item.
The house does. WHERE THE AUTHORITY HOLDS THE MONOPOLY the GP8 route applies
and it is NOT a measured connection: a SUM, a PROFIT ITEM and an ATTENDANCE ITEM.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              409



Three lines, never one. Only where the contractor may lawfully make the connection himself
is it enumerated.
Why. In the UAE every potable water, sewer and district-cooling connection is an authority
monopoly, so the GP8 limb is the normal case rather than the exception. Enumerating it prices
a connection the contractor is not permitted to make, and leaves the authority’s own charge
with nowhere to sit.

R1.2 POMI says. Installations shall be MEASURED in accordance with the relevant clauses
of this section; ALTERNATIVELY, they may be ENUMERATED ON A LOCATIONAL BASIS.
The house does. MEASURED.
Why. Matches the Q1.2 election so the two MEP sections are read the same way.

R3.2 POMI says. Cable and conduit to individual SUB-MAIN circuits shall be ENUMERATED
and separately identified; ALTERNATIVELY, sub-main circuits may be MEASURED in accor-
dance with R2.
The house does. ENUMERATED PER CIRCUIT, separately identified by the boards it runs
between.
Why. A sub-main is a discrete run between two discrete boards. Identifying it by its boards
makes it checkable against the single-line diagram, which a length cannot be.

          POMI says. Cable and conduit to termination points shall be ENUMERATED AS
R4.1 / R5.1
POINTS (R4.1). Ceiling roses, switches, socket outlets and bell pushes shall be ENUMERATED
(R5.1).
The house does. BOTH are billed at each position — the POINT and the ACCESSORY fitted
to it.
Why. They are supplied and fixed at different times by different people: the point is the cable,
conduit, tray, boxes and terminations reaching the position; the accessory is the plate on the
front. This is NOT the R4.1 double count — that one is measuring a point AND a cable LENGTH
for the same final circuit, which stays forbidden.

R4.1 cl.4 / R6.1POMI says. Equipment points shall state the type of equipment or electri-
cal rating; CONTACTORS, STARTERS OR THE LIKE SHALL BE MEASURED SEPARATELY
AS EQUIPMENT POINTS (R4.1 cl.4). Switchgear, distribution gear, contactors, starters and
composite switchboards shall be ENUMERATED (R6.1).
The house does. CONTACTORS AND STARTERS ARE BILLED TWICE, deliberately — once
as the equipment point, once as the control gear.
Why. POMI directs both in terms: R4.1 cl.4 requires the circuit reaching the device to be
measured as an equipment point, and R6.1 requires the device itself to be enumerated. Two
items, and a bill carrying only one of them is short.

R7.2 POMI says. Controls, which shall include accessories and interconnecting cables, shall
be MEASURED in accordance with the relevant clauses of this section; ALTERNATIVELY, they
may be INCLUDED WITH THE ITEMS OF EQUIPMENT.
The house does. INCLUDED WITH THE EQUIPMENT — and the interconnecting cables go
with them, not measured again under R2, R3 or R4.
Why. Matches the Q5.3 election so controls are treated the same way in both MEP sections.

GP5.6 POMI says. The description of items MAY REFER TO OTHER DOCUMENTS OR DRAW-
INGS and any reference to such information SHALL BE UNDERSTOOD TO FULFIL any re-
quirement of these principles; ALTERNATIVELY, reference may be made to published infor-
mation.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                           410



The house does. REFERENCE IS USED, and it is what makes the Family 1 and Family 2
closing formulas sufficient — but ONLY to a document ISSUED WITH THE BILL under GP2.3.
Why. A reference discharges POMI’s description duty, so a reference to a document the ten-
derer does not hold discharges the duty against nothing. Published information (a standard,
a code) may be referenced because the tenderer can obtain it; a project document may not
unless it is in the tender set.

                              POMI says. The cost of labour, of materials, and of construc-
GP9.1 / GP9.3 / GP9.5 — DAYWORKS
tional plant employed exclusively in dayworks shall EACH be given AS A SUM; ALTERNA-
TIVELY, a SCHEDULE of the different categories may be given CONTAINING A PROVISIONAL
QUANTITY of hours, or of materials, for each category.
The house does. A SCHEDULE with provisional quantities, for all three. Sums are not used.
Why. A sum cannot be compared between tenderers — it is one number against one number,
and it reveals nothing about the rates that will actually be applied when daywork is ordered.
A schedule prices each category, so the tender is comparable AND the rates are fixed before
anyone needs them. The quantities are provisional by POMI’s own wording and are adjusted
on the actual, so the schedule costs nothing in accuracy.

        POMI says. Telephones for the employer, INCLUDING COSTS OF CALLS; ALTER-
A6.1 cl.2
NATIVELY, the cost of calls may be given AS A SUM.
The house does. THE COST OF CALLS IS GIVEN AS A SUM, separately from the telephone
provision.
Why. Call charges are unknowable at tender and depend entirely on how the employer’s team
uses them. Leaving them inside the facilities particulars makes the contractor price an open
risk; a sum adjusts on the actual.

B5.3 POMI says. Demolishing INDIVIDUAL STRUCTURES (or part thereof) shall EACH be
given as an item; ALTERNATIVELY, demolishing ALL STRUCTURES on a site may be given as
ONE item.
The house does. EACH STRUCTURE ITS OWN ITEM, stating its location per B5.1.
Why. B5.1 requires the location of each item, which a single all-structures item cannot give.
And demolition is routinely varied — one building descoped, another added — which a single
lump cannot be valued against.

B8.5 POMI says. Excavation in rock shall be SO DESCRIBED; ALTERNATIVELY, it may be
measured as EXTRA OVER excavation — the volume of rock measured but NO DEDUCTION
from the excavation in which it occurs.
The house does. EXTRA OVER.
Why. Consistent with the D2.2 election. It keeps ONE excavation quantity for the whole dig
and prices the rock against it, which is how the work is carried out and how a variation is
valued. Rock is found, not designed, so the base quantity must not move when it is.

B19.5 POMI says. Inspection chambers or the like shall be ENUMERATED; ALTERNA-
TIVELY, they may be MEASURED in accordance with the relevant sections and given under
an appropriate heading.
The house does. ENUMERATED.
Why. B19.3 already deems the concrete surrounds and additional excavation of drainage
accessories included, so the section is built around counting. Measuring a chamber through
C, D and B for a handful of chambers produces more rows than it does certainty.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                              411



C5.2 POMI says. Reinforcement to precast concrete shall be measured in accordance
with C3 AND GIVEN UNDER AN APPROPRIATE HEADING; ALTERNATIVELY, it may be
DESCRIBED IN THE ITEM.
The house does. DESCRIBED IN THE ITEM.
Why. A precast unit is bought as a unit, at a rate that includes its steel. Separating the
reinforcement produces a weight nobody prices independently and a unit rate that then has
to be read net of it.

C5.4 POMI says. Lintels, sills and duct covers shall be measured by LENGTH; ALTERNA-
TIVELY, DUCT COVERS may be measured by AREA.
The house does. BY LENGTH throughout — the duct-cover alternative is not used.
Why. One unit for the whole clause. Consistent with the F6.3 shelving election: a cover is
bought and laid by the running metre at a stated width, and the width is a GP5.2 mandatory
statement anyway.

C7.5 POMI says. Forming sinkings, channels or the like shall be measured by LENGTH and,
WHERE APPROPRIATE, THE ITEM MAY INCLUDE additional excavation, hardcore, shutter-
ing and concrete; ALTERNATIVELY, they may be ENUMERATED.
The house does. BY LENGTH, AND THE ITEM INCLUDES the additional excavation, hard-
core, shuttering and concrete.
Why. The inclusive limb is the point of the clause: a channel is one operation and splitting
it into four trades produces four rows that must then be kept in step. Because the item is
inclusive, NO SEPARATE excavation, hardcore, formwork or concrete is raised for it — that is
the double count this election exists to prevent.

C7.6 POMI says. Fixings, ties and inserts shall be ENUMERATED; ALTERNATIVELY, they
may be measured by AREA.
The house does. ENUMERATED.
Why. They are discrete objects at discrete positions. An area of cast-in channel or of wall ties
is a density, not a quantity, and it cannot be checked against a drawing.

F9.1 POMI says. Metalwork items associated with woodwork shall be ENUMERATED; AL-
TERNATIVELY, WATERBARS or the like may be measured by LENGTH.
The house does. ENUMERATED, EXCEPT waterbars and the like, which are measured BY
LENGTH.
Why. POMI’s own split, taken as written: discrete ironmongery-like objects are counted,
a continuous bar is measured. Note this clause does NOT reach metalwork inside an F7.1
COMPOSITE ITEM, where all metalwork is deemed included.

EXTENSIONS — 9
C3.1 / C3.2  POMI says. The weight of bar reinforcement shall be the NET WEIGHT without
addition for rolling margin, supports, spacers or tying wire. POMI does not say where the bar
arrangement is read from.
The house does. Reinforcement is MEASURED FROM THE SECTION DRAWINGS. Laps are
measured at the SPECIFIED LAP LENGTH at the positions the sections show. A bar bending
schedule, where one is issued, is A CROSS-CHECK ONLY.
Why. At tender no BBS is issued, so a method depending on one has no answer at tender
and a different answer later — the take-off must give the same figure at both. A BBS is the
FABRICATOR’S CUTTING LIST on its own revision cycle, not the designed arrangement. The
section drawing is issued with the tender under GP2.3 and is therefore the document the
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                               412



contractor priced against. A variance against a later BBS is a finding to record and query, not
a correction to apply.

B4.1 POMI says. Removing isolated trees shall be ENUMERATED. POMI states no size clas-
sification.
The house does. Enumerated BY GIRTH BAND.
Why. A rate for ‘remove tree’ with no girth cannot be priced — a sapling and a mature ghaf
are the same item under POMI and two different jobs on site.

        POMI says. An item shall be given for sundry items, which shall include ALL
A9.1 cl.9
STATUTORY OBLIGATIONS.
The house does. The statutory obligations head is EXPANDED into a stated list under A9.2
— municipality permits, NOCs, civil defence approvals, authority coordination and third-party
inspections.
Why. POMI gives it one phrase. In the UAE it is the most under-priced line in a preliminaries
bill, and A9.2 is POMI’s own mechanism for turning it from a blank cheque into a defined
scope.

GP3.1 POMI says. Each measurement shall be taken to the nearest 10 millimetres. POMI
does not say whether the rounding is applied to each dimension or to the product.
The house does. Each dimension is rounded AS IT IS TAKEN, then multiplied. Never the
product.
Why. Rounding the product hides which dimension was read, so a checker cannot re-derive
the row from the drawing.

GP3.5 POMI says. Notwithstanding these principles, a separate minor building or structure
MAY be enumerated.
The house does. Available but NEVER automatic. A guard house, pump room or substation is
measured through unless a run explicitly elects to enumerate it, and the election is recorded.
Why. POMI says ‘may’. A default that quietly enumerates would lose the detail that makes a
bill checkable, and nothing on the face of the bill would show it had happened.

F1.2 POMI says. Descriptions of timber members SHALL STATE whether the sizes are BASIC
(before machining) or FINISHED (milled, within permitted deviations). POMI does not say
which basis to use.
The house does. FOLLOW THE PROJECT DESCRIPTION — take whichever basis the spec-
ification and drawings use, and state it. No house default, and no conversion between the
two.
Why. The basis belongs to the design, not to the measurer. A ‘50 x 200’ quoted basic finishes
at about 45 x 195 — same words, different timber, different price — so converting one to the
other silently changes the specification. The statement is mandatory; its value comes from
the source documents.

J2.1 / J2.2 / J3.1 POMI says. Backgrounds shall be measured by area and each so described.
Finishings shall be measured by area. POMI does not say in terms that both are measured
over the same surface.
The house does. A BACKGROUND IS ALWAYS MEASURED SEPARATELY FROM THE FIN-
ISH ON IT — two areas over one surface.
Why. They are two operations by two trades at two times. Letting the screed sit inside the
tiling rate makes it invisible on the face of the bill and unvaluable on variation, and it is the
commoner error by far — nobody bills the screed twice, they bill it never.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                     413



K1.1 POMI says. Accessories are defined as specially manufactured or proprietary items
NOT INCLUDED IN OTHER SECTIONS. POMI says nothing further about how they are de-
scribed.
The house does. K IS TESTED LAST, and EVERY K ITEM IS FULLY DESCRIBED — what the
thing is, what it is made of, how it is fixed, and its schedule or type reference.
Why. The section is defined by EXCLUSION, so its heading says nothing about what an item
is. Only the description can. And testing K last stops work being pulled out of the sections
that would price it properly.

D3.2 POMI says. Arches shall be measured by LENGTH. That is the entire clause — POMI
states no basis along which the length is taken.
The house does. The length is taken on the MEAN GIRTH: L = pi x (R_intrados + t/2) x
(theta/180) for a curved arch.
Why. Both the span and the intrados understate the work; the mean girth is the line the
masonry actually follows, and on a semicircular arch the three differ by about 45 per cent.
POMI is silent, so this is the HOUSE’s basis and it is declared rather than presented as the
standard’s.



PART 2 — THE CROSS-CHECKS A TAKE-OFF MUST SURVIVE
These are arithmetic identities, not opinions. A take-off that fails one of them is wrong some-
where, even when every individual row looks right.

12.1 Excavation ↔ disposal [B11.1]
V_disposal_total      ==   V_excavation_total    +   V_dredging    +   V_tunnelling     EXACTLY
V_backfill + V_removed       ==   V_disposal_total


2 Excavation ↔ substructure concrete
V_excavation    ≥    V_concrete_below_ground     +   V_blinding    +   V_hardcore

The dig must at least contain what is built in it. Where it does not, either the excavation is
short or a foundation has been measured that nothing was dug for.

3 Concrete ↔ formwork HOUSE
For a rectangular member, the ratio of shuttered area to concrete volume has a knowable
range. Outside it, one of the two is wrong:
r   =   A_shutter / V_concrete                  m²/m³


                    Member                                        Typical r   Read as
                    slab, 200 mm, soffit only                     ≈ 5.0       1/t
                    wall, 250 mm, both faces                      ≈ 8.0       2/t
                    column, 400 × 400                             ≈ 10.0      perimeter / A_sect
                    beam, 300 × 600 under a 200 slab              ≈ 7–9
                    foundation, mass, sides only                  ≈ 1–3


⚠ r far above the range usually means formwork was measured to faces that are cast against
earth or against existing construction. Far below usually means a face was missed.
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                            414



4 Concrete ↔ reinforcement HOUSE
ρ_rebar    =    W_rebar_kg / V_concrete_m3                kg/m³


                                      Element                      Typical range
                                      blinding                     0
                                      mass foundation              30 – 60
                                      raft, ground beam            90 – 160
                                      suspended slab               80 – 130
                                      column                       150 – 300
                                      beam                         120 – 220
                                      core / shear wall            100 – 200


These are sense checks, not rules. A figure outside the range is a question to answer, not a
quantity to change — and the answer goes in the run audit either way.

5 Wall finishes ↔ wall area HOUSE
A_finish    ≈   A_wall_structure      ×    (number of finished faces)
                 −   Σ voids ≥ 1.00 m² and all edge voids
                 +   Σ reveals, returns, columns                  [J3.1 class 2]

The + term is the one that gets dropped, and it always makes the finish larger than the struc-
ture.

6 Doors and windows ↔ their voids
count(door items, H1.1)          ==       count(door voids deducted from walls)
count(window items, H2.1)        ==       count(window voids deducted from walls)

⚠ A door counted in H but never deducted from D or J means the wall and its plaster were
paid for through the opening. A void deducted with no door item means the door was never
billed.

7 Roof area ↔ pitch [G2.1]
A_slope    ==   A_plan / cos θ                         θ = roof pitch from horizontal

If A_slope == A_plan on a pitched roof, the roof was measured on plan and is under-measured
by the table in §6.2.

8 Drainage ↔ excavation [B9.2]
if drain trenches measured by LENGTH under B9.2
   then    NO separate disposal and NO separate filling rows for those trenches

Both are deemed included. Their presence is a double count.

9 MEP points ↔ cable HOUSE, from [R4.1]
if final sub-circuits enumerated as POINTS
   then    NO cable or conduit length measured for those same circuits
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                                  415

PART 4 — WHAT IS HANDED OVER
Four things, and the measurement defends itself:
    1. The take-off workbook — every quantity a live Nr x dimensions build-up the client can
       click into, one tab per discipline, with the pivot that feeds the bill.
    2. The marked-up drawings — call-out tags and a legend showing exactly what was mea-
       sured on each sheet, colour-coded by POMI section, every tag carrying the item code.
    3. The bill — in the issue format above: A4 portrait, the eight columns, the 62-row page,
       collection page per section, bill summary, grand summary, amount in words.
    4. The audit tabs — an independent re-measure with variances, anything flagged as sub-
       stantive, and drawing-to-section coverage naming every gap (for example rebar pending
       a bar bending schedule).
Plus a short methodology note: POMI as the standard, the traceability rules, and the
evidence-only rule — nothing is measured that is not on a drawing.



PART 5 — THE COUNT RECONCILIATION
For doors, windows, fittings, plant and every other schedule-driven item, the count IS the
quantity, so the check is not a bubble on every instance — it is:
schedule count   ==   number of plan tags          K18, EXACT equality
AETRAA POMI Take-off — the complete prompt set                                       417



Not a tolerance. A door is a whole number and a discrepancy of one is a real discrepancy.
The same reconciliation covers wall marks and core marks, so it reaches every enumerated
discipline — H, L, M, and the tagged items in B, P, Q and R.
APPENDIX — WHERE THE
RUNNING AGENT DIFFERS
FROM THIS BOOK

This book is the plugin, boq-buildings-pomi v4.6.4. The agent that runs when you type
aetraa is pomi_takeoff v4.2.0, and it carries its own copy of these files. Twenty-three are
identical. Seven are not, and three exist only in the plugin.
The three that are missing from the running agent matter most:

The measurement seat in v4.6.4 opens by pointing at the first two. The running agent’s
copy of that seat has no such pointer, and the files are not there to point at. So the
seat that takes the dimensions is working without the arithmetic reference that the current
text assumes it has read. That is worth closing before the next real run — and it is a copy, not
a code change.
